redirect, SSRF and CRLF markers by default. All strings are in the Blitz Strike code at 9d7a6ecb.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Blitz Strike
name: Blitz Strike Scan Markers in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*blitzstrike* OR *BlitzStrike*)) OR user_agent.original:"Mozilla\/5.0 \(recon\-agent\)" OR (url.query:(*evil\-blitz.example.com* OR *blitzstrike\-ssrf\-canary* OR *X\-BlitzStrike* OR *bs\-nonexistent\-* OR *__blitz_xss__* OR *zzblitz*)) OR url.domain:/[bB][sS]-[mM][aA][rR][kK][eE][rR]\.[eE][xX][aA][mM][pP][lL][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects RAPTOR (gadievron/raptor) running on a host: the Claude Code session its launcher bin/raptor starts
(claude --plugin-dir <raptor>/plugins/coverage -n RAPTOR /raptor), the Python supervisors the launcher runs first,
the libexec/raptor-* helper scripts its Claude Code hooks and slash commands call, and its pipelines
(raptor.py agentic, raptor.py web --url, raptor_agentic.py, packages/web/scanner.py and the rest).
false_positives: Authorized security research and code review with RAPTOR
name: RAPTOR Launcher, Pipelines or Helper Scripts
query: (process.command_line:*plugins\/coverage* AND process.command_line:*\-n\ RAPTOR*) OR (process.command_line:(*\/core\/security\/scratch_supervisor.py* OR *\/core\/startup\/install_guard.py* OR *\/core\/security\/launch_scratch.py* OR *\-\-_scratch\-session\-stage*)) OR process.command_line:*libexec\/raptor\-* OR (process.command_line:(*raptor.py\ agentic* OR *raptor.py\ web\ \-\-url* OR *raptor.py\ scan\ \-\-repo* OR *raptor.py\ codeql\ \-\-repo* OR *raptor.py\ fuzz\ \-\-binary* OR *raptor_agentic.py* OR *raptor_fuzzing.py* OR *raptor_codeql.py* OR *packages\/web\/scanner.py* OR *packages\/llm_analysis\/agent.py*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Claude-Red skill pack (SnailSploit/Claude-Red at 6196ba74) being installed on a host: 79 SKILL.md files
named offensive-<topic> (SQL injection, EDR evasion, shellcode, C2 frameworks, AD attacks and more) that a coding
agent loads as instructions. The documented installs are git clone into ~/.claude/skills/claude-red and install.sh,
whose default target is ~/.claude/skills/claude-red/<category>/offensive-<topic>/SKILL.md; --target can point
elsewhere, so the second selection matches the offensive-<topic> skill folder under any skills folder.
false_positives: Security staff who use Claude-Red or another skill pack that names its skills offensive-<topic>
name: Claude-Red Offensive Skills Installed for a Coding Agent
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/skills\/claude\-red\/* OR *\\skills\\claude\-red\\*)) OR ((TargetFilename:*\/skills\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/offensive\-*) AND TargetFilename:*\/SKILL.md) OR ((TargetFilename:*\\skills\\* AND TargetFilename:*\\offensive\-*) AND TargetFilename:*\\SKILL.md)

author: ThreatDefence
description: One identity denied on many different API calls in ten minutes, the pattern of a stolen key trying every discovery call.
false_positives: Automation and infrastructure-as-code pipelines. Baseline before alerting
name: AWS Access Denied Sweep Across Many APIs

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a command run by an ARTEMIS sub-agent: a process whose parent is the forked Codex CLI started with
--wait-for-followup and --instance-id (supervisor/orchestration/instance_manager.py:77-86). Codex runs the shell
commands the model writes, normally as bash -lc <command>, so the children are the scanners, exploits and shells the
model chose. Group by the --instance-id value to see one task.
false_positives: Authorized research or test runs of ARTEMIS
name: Process Started by an ARTEMIS Codex Sub-Agent
query: process.parent.command_line:*\-\-wait\-for\-followup* AND process.parent.command_line:*\-\-instance\-id*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects 0security's verifier creating the container in which it runs a proof-of-concept step for a finding:
docker or podman create with the name 0-verify-<12 hex> and the label 0.verify=1, all capabilities dropped
except DAC_OVERRIDE and FOWNER.
false_positives: Developers using 0security's verification on their own code
name: 0security Verification Container Created
query: process.command_line:*create* AND process.command_line:*\-\-name\ 0\-verify\-* AND process.command_line:*\-\-label\ 0.verify\=1*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an attack tool whose parent is an AI agent CLI or the shell Claude Code runs commands through
(zsh -c source ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/... on Linux and macOS, the CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_LAUNCHER_SCRIPT PowerShell
launcher on Windows). Auto-approve flags are not part of the rule: staff use them too, and an agent can run an
attack tool without one. Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, Codex and opencode start tools through a plain shell, which puts the
agent one level above the parent, so this rule only sees them when they start the tool directly; the KQL hunt in
behaviors/sentinel/hunting covers the grandparent. The model behind the agent does not matter.
Tools written in Python, Ruby or Perl (sqlmap, NetExec, Metasploit, nikto and others) run under their interpreter,
so the image is python3, ruby or perl and the tool is the script in the command line; the script selections cover
them. A tool started as a module (python3 -m) is not covered.
Agents installed with npm or pip run under node or python and are found by their package path in the parent
command line.
false_positives: Staff who use an AI agent for authorized security testing or network troubleshooting
name: AI Agent CLI Starts an Attack Tool
query: ((process.executable:(*\/nmap OR *\\nmap.exe OR *\/naabu OR *\\naabu.exe OR *\/masscan OR *\\masscan.exe OR *\/nuclei OR *\\nuclei.exe OR *\/katana OR *\\katana.exe OR *\/dalfox OR *\\dalfox.exe OR *\/ffuf OR *\\ffuf.exe OR *\/gobuster OR *\\gobuster.exe OR *\/feroxbuster OR *\\feroxbuster.exe OR *\/sqlmap OR *\\sqlmap.exe OR *\/nikto OR *\\nikto.exe OR *\/wpscan OR *\\wpscan.exe OR *\/hydra OR *\\hydra.exe OR *\/kerbrute OR *\\kerbrute.exe OR *\/netexec OR *\\netexec.exe OR *\/nxc OR *\\nxc.exe OR *\/crackmapexec OR *\\crackmapexec.exe OR *\/bloodyAD OR *\\bloodyAD.exe OR *\/coercer OR *\\coercer.exe OR *\/chisel OR *\\chisel.exe OR *\/evil\-winrm OR *\\evil\-winrm.exe OR *\/cloudfox OR *\\cloudfox.exe OR *\/msfconsole OR *\\msfconsole.exe OR *\/dirsearch OR *\\dirsearch.exe OR *\/medusa OR *\\medusa.exe OR *\/enum4linux\-ng OR *\\enum4linux\-ng.exe OR *\/pwncat OR *\\pwncat.exe OR *\/pwncat\-cs OR *\\pwncat\-cs.exe OR *\/responder OR *\\responder.exe OR *\/searchsploit OR *\\searchsploit.exe OR *\/hashcat OR *\\hashcat.exe)) OR ((process.executable:(*\/python* OR *\\python* OR *\/ruby* OR *\\ruby* OR *\/perl* OR *\\perl*)) AND ((process.command_line:(*\/sqlmap\ * OR *\/nikto\ * OR *\/wpscan\ * OR *\/netexec\ * OR *\/nxc\ * OR *\/crackmapexec\ * OR *\/bloodyAD\ * OR *\/coercer\ * OR *\/evil\-winrm\ * OR *\/msfconsole\ * OR *\/dirsearch\ * OR *\/enum4linux\-ng\ * OR *\/pwncat\ * OR *\/pwncat\-cs\ * OR *\/responder\ * OR *\/sqlmap.py* OR *\\sqlmap.py* OR *\ sqlmap.py* OR *\/nikto.pl* OR *\\nikto.pl* OR *\ nikto.pl* OR *\/bloodyAD.py* OR *\\bloodyAD.py* OR *\ bloodyAD.py* OR *\/dirsearch.py* OR *\\dirsearch.py* OR *\ dirsearch.py* OR *\/enum4linux\-ng.py* OR *\\enum4linux\-ng.py* OR *\ enum4linux\-ng.py* OR *\/Coercer\/Coercer.py* OR *\ Coercer\/Coercer.py* OR *\\Coercer\\Coercer.py* OR *\ Coercer\\Coercer.py* OR *\/Responder\/Responder.py* OR *\ Responder\/Responder.py* OR *\\Responder\\Responder.py* OR *\ Responder\\Responder.py*)) OR (process.command_line:(*\/sqlmap OR *\/nikto OR *\/wpscan OR *\/netexec OR *\/nxc OR *\/crackmapexec OR *\/bloodyAD OR *\/coercer OR *\/evil\-winrm OR *\/msfconsole OR *\/dirsearch OR *\/enum4linux\-ng OR *\/pwncat OR *\/pwncat\-cs OR *\/responder))))) AND ((process.parent.command_line:(*shell\-snapshots* OR *CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_LAUNCHER_SCRIPT* OR *\-\-provider\ cairn* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-pi\/*)) OR (process.parent.executable:(*\/claude OR *\\claude.exe OR *\/codex OR *\\codex.exe OR *\/qwen OR *\\qwen.exe OR *\/kimi OR *\\kimi.exe OR *\/opencode OR *\\opencode.exe OR *\/hermes OR *\\hermes.exe)) OR (process.parent.command_line:(*@anthropic\-ai\/claude\-code* OR *@anthropic\-ai\\claude\-code* OR *@qwen\-code\/* OR *@qwen\-code\\* OR *@openai\/codex* OR *@openai\\codex* OR *opencode\-ai* OR *kimi\-cli* OR *kimi_cli*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Cyber-AutoAgent Python agent starting an assessment (cyberautoagent.py with --target, or the
--objective via environment placeholder its terminal front end always passes), its idle compose container
(--service-mode), its front end, or a container from the cyber-autoagent image.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent AI Pentest Agent Started
query: (process.command_line:*cyberautoagent.py* AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-target* OR *\-\-service\-mode*))) OR process.command_line:*\-\-objective\ via\ environment* OR process.command_line:*\/interfaces\/react\/dist\/index.js* OR process.command_line:*cyber\-autoagent\:latest*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests from Clearwing (Lazarus-AI-OSS/clearwing) reaching a web server: its Playwright browser
("Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 Clearwing/1.0"), its JavaScript bundle analyzer
("Mozilla/5.0 Clearwing/1.0") and its attack-surface liveness probe ("clearwing-asm/0.5
(+https://github.com/Lazarus-AI/clearwing)"). All three are hard-coded.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Clearwing
name: Clearwing Probe User Agents in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:(*Clearwing\/1.0* OR clearwing\-asm\/*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects PentesterFlow's own HTTP clients and downloads: the user agent pentesterflow/0.1 of its http tool,
Mozilla/5.0 pentesterflow/0.1 (+research) of its web_fetch tool and Mozilla/5.0 pentesterflow/0.1 of its
web_search tool (html.duckduckgo.com), and its installer, release binaries and self-update script under
github.com/PentesterFlow/agent and raw.githubusercontent.com/PentesterFlow/agent. HTTPS URLs and user agents are
only visible where the proxy inspects TLS.
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentesterFlow
Someone reading the PentesterFlow repository pages on GitHub
name: PentesterFlow Client Traffic in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:*pentesterflow\/* OR url.original:*\/PentesterFlow\/agent\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the fixed invalid code and state values ARTEX sends to OAuth callback routes while mapping
an application.
false_positives: Unknown
name: ARTEX OAuth Callback Probe
query: url.query:*code\=AAAA\&state\=notvalidb64\!\!*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the processes of Sage, the AI operator that installs into a Mythic C2 server as a chat container: its entrypoint
"python3 /usr/local/bin/sage-entrypoint" and the BloodHound MCP server it launches over stdio,
"uv --directory /opt/bloodhound_mcp run --no-sync main.py".
false_positives: A Mythic server you run with Sage installed
The BloodHound MCP server installed under /opt/bloodhound_mcp for another client
name: Sage (Mythic) AI Operator Container Processes
query: process.command_line:*\/usr\/local\/bin\/sage\-entrypoint* OR (process.command_line:*\-\-directory\ \/opt\/bloodhound_mcp* AND process.command_line:*main.py*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files OpenHack (openhackai/OpenHack) writes. Both versions use ~/.openhack: v2 keeps settings.json,
credentials.json (API keys in plain text), dashboard-<port>.json and .log, and projects/<hash>/scans/<id>.json
reports with source evidence and findings; v0.x keeps config, auth.json (ChatGPT OAuth tokens), scans/ and
checkpoints/. v2 also writes <tmp>/openhack-subscription-* and <tmp>/openhack-login-* folders for its Claude Code
and Codex children, and v0.x writes .openhack-evidence/ and .openhack-sandbox-override-*.yml into the folder it
tests.
false_positives: Developers and security teams running OpenHack
Another program that uses a folder named .openhack
name: OpenHack Workspace, Temporary or Evidence Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.openhack\/* OR *\\.openhack\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/openhack\-subscription\-* OR *\/openhack\-login\-* OR *\\openhack\-subscription\-* OR *\\openhack\-login\-*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.openhack\-evidence\/* OR *.openhack\-sandbox\-override\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Virga beacon talking to its listener: a POST to the default check-in path /api/updates with one of the
user agents Virga's generator builds in (the Chrome 96 string without a beacon config, the truncated Chrome
string from the shipped beacon.yaml), or a request for /api/updates/stage2. The path and user agent are settings
the operator can change. The truncated user agent is also used by other agent frameworks.
false_positives: A real Chrome 96 browser posting to an application path named /api/updates
name: Virga Beacon Check-in or Stage 2 Request in Proxy Logs
query: (cs-method:POST AND url.original:*\/api\/updates AND (user_agent.original:("Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36 \(KHTML, like Gecko\) Chrome\/96.0.4664.110 Safari\/537.36" OR "Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36"))) OR url.original:*\/api\/updates\/stage2

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the BreachWeave multi-agent pentest platform (package tch-agent) on a host: the web console started from
the source tree (bun run apps/cli/src/main.ts web) or a compiled tch-agent binary, the docker run that starts a
solver container named tch-solver-<id> with the host's tch-agent binary mounted at /opt/tch-agent/tch-agent, the
solver RPC process inside that container, the docker buildx build of the tch-agent:latest solver image, and the
bun compile of the Linux solver binary into ~/.tch-agent/runtime/self/.
false_positives: Red teams, CTF teams and researchers running BreachWeave
name: BreachWeave (tch-agent) Web Console, Solver Container or Image Build Started
query: (process.command_line:(*apps\/cli\/src\/main.ts\ web* OR *tch\-agent\-linux\-x64\ web* OR *tch\-agent\-darwin\-arm64\ web* OR *tch\-agent\-darwin\-x64\ web* OR *tch\-agent\-windows\-x64.exe\ web*)) OR (process.command_line:*\-\-name\ tch\-solver\-* AND process.command_line:*\/opt\/tch\-agent\/tch\-agent*) OR process.command_line:*\/opt\/tch\-agent\/tch\-agent\ solver\ rpc* OR process.command_line:*ai.tch\-agent.dockerfile\-sha256\=* OR (process.command_line:*scripts\/build.ts* AND process.command_line:*bun\-linux\-x64\-baseline* AND process.command_line:*\/.tch\-agent\/runtime\/self\/tch\-agent\-linux\-x64*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the curl command ARTEMIS uses to post a finding to its Slack webhook:
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"title": ..., "asset": ..., "vuln_type": ...,
"severity": ..., "description": ..., "repro_steps": ..., "impact": ..., "cleanup": ...}' <webhook url>
(supervisor/submissions/vulnerability.py:72-80, supervisor/triage/triage_tools.py:652-660,
codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs:2052-2061). The JSON keys are in the code; the URL is set by the operator.
false_positives: Other reporting scripts that post findings with the same field names
name: ARTEMIS Vulnerability Report Posted with curl
query: (process.executable:(*\/curl OR *\\curl.exe)) AND (process.command_line:*vuln_type* AND process.command_line:*repro_steps* AND process.command_line:*cleanup* AND process.command_line:*application\/json*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files PentestGPT writes on the host that runs it. Current main writes runs/<run>/trial-config.json,
state.sqlite3, summary.json and traces/supervisor-r<n>/ and traces/executor-<id>/ with input.json, events.jsonl and
output.json, and works in agent-workspaces/<run>/supervisor and executor. v1.0.0 writes ~/.pentestgpt/user_id,
~/.pentestgpt/sessions/<id>.json and pentestgpt-debug.log. The legacy mode writes logs/pentestGPT.log and
logs/pentestGPT_log_<time>.txt.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF practice and research runs with PentestGPT
Other software that writes a trial-config.json or an agent-workspaces folder
name: PentestGPT Run, Session or Log Files Written
query: ((TargetFilename:(*\/.pentestgpt\/sessions\/* OR *\\.pentestgpt\\sessions\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.pentestgpt\/user_id OR *\\.pentestgpt\\user_id OR *pentestgpt\-debug.log))) OR ((TargetFilename:(*\/pentestGPT.log OR *\\pentestGPT.log)) OR TargetFilename:*pentestGPT_log_*) OR TargetFilename:/.*[\/\\]traces[\/\\](supervisor-r[0-9]+(-a[0-9]+)?|executor-[0-9a-f]{32})[\/\\](input|output)\.json/ OR TargetFilename:/.*[\/\\]agent-workspaces[\/\\][A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*[\/\\](supervisor|executor)[\/\\].*/ OR (TargetFilename:(*\/trial\-config.json OR *\\trial\-config.json))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects NeuroSploit's bash beacon and the Linux persistence commands its C2 hands an agent. The whole beacon is on
the command line (nohup bash -c '...' started directly, from an @reboot crontab entry or from ~/.bashrc), so it
carries the X-Implant-Token header and the /api/beacon path; the systemd variant writes
~/.config/systemd/user/nsupdate.service and enables it with systemctl --user.
false_positives: Authorized tests with NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit Beacon or Persistence on Linux
query: (process.command_line:*X\-Implant\-Token* AND process.command_line:*\/api\/beacon*) OR process.command_line:*nsupdate.service* OR (process.command_line:*#\ NSUpdate* AND process.command_line:*.bashrc*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files hackingBuddyGPT writes: the WebAPITesting report (reports/<name>/report_<timestamp>.md) and the
OpenAPI document it builds from a target (openapi_spec/<strategy>/<name>/<timestamp>/<name>_spec.yaml), both inside
the installed hackingBuddyGPT/usecases/web_api package folder, and the per-run traces of its benchmark launcher under
benchmark_results/<timestamp>/traces/.
false_positives: Researchers running hackingBuddyGPT
Another project with a benchmark_results/<run>/traces/ layout
name: hackingBuddyGPT Web API Report, Generated Spec or Benchmark Trace Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/hackingBuddyGPT\/usecases\/web_api\/reports\/* OR *\/hackingBuddyGPT\/usecases\/web_api\/openapi_spec\/* OR *\\hackingBuddyGPT\\usecases\\web_api\\reports\\* OR *\\hackingBuddyGPT\\usecases\\web_api\\openapi_spec\\*)) OR ((TargetFilename:*\/benchmark_results\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/traces\/*) AND (TargetFilename:(*.jsonl OR *\/console.log)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the wrapper HackSynth puts around every command its Planner model writes: timeout 10s /bin/bash -c <command>,
started through a Docker exec in the attackbox container, so the parent is the container runtime
(pentest_agent.py:81). The timeout comes from timeout_duration, 10 in every shipped config. Scripts use the same
wrapper, so look for many of them from one container in a short time, each followed by a security tool.
false_positives: Health checks and scripts run with docker exec that wrap a command in timeout and bash
name: HackSynth Agent Command Wrapper in a Container
query: process.executable:*\/timeout AND process.command_line:/([^ ]*\/)?timeout [0-9]+s \/bin\/bash -c .*/ AND (process.parent.executable:(*\/containerd\-shim OR *\/containerd\-shim\-runc\-v2 OR *\/runc))

author: ThreatDefence
description: An event carries an address, domain, URL or file hash that public reporting ties to an agentic attack framework (iocs/indicators.csv, medium and high confidence, addresses not past their review date). Load generated/elastic_ndjson/agentic-attack-indicators.ndjson into logs-ti_agentic_attacks-default first. Addresses from cloud and VPS providers are reassigned: check the indicator's description and date before acting.
false_positives: Reassigned cloud and VPS addresses
Shared hosting behind a reported domain
name: Agentic Attack Framework Indicator Match
query: destination.domain:* or destination.ip:* or dns.question.name:* or file.hash.md5:* or file.hash.sha256:* or process.hash.md5:* or process.hash.sha256:* or source.ip:* or url.domain:* or url.full:* or url.original:*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Windows persistence commands NeuroSploit's C2 hands an agent: a scheduled task NSUpdate
(schtasks /Create /F /SC ONLOGON /TN "NSUpdate") or a Run value NSUpdate added with reg.exe, both starting
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand with the PowerShell beacon.
false_positives: Software that really names its updater task or Run value NSUpdate (check the command it starts)
name: NeuroSploit Beacon Windows Persistence Named NSUpdate
query: (process.command_line:*schtasks* AND process.command_line:*\/create* AND process.command_line:*NSUpdate*) OR (process.command_line:*reg* AND process.command_line:*\ add\ * AND process.command_line:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run* AND process.command_line:*NSUpdate*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the pentestswarm binary or its container image, and the switches that skip its consent prompt
(PENTESTSWARM_AUTHORIZED=1, --authorized). Pentest Swarm AI runs a swarm of agents that scan and exploit a target
with no approval for each action unless assist mode is on.
false_positives: Penetration testers running Pentest Swarm AI
name: Pentest Swarm AI Started on a Host
query: (process.executable:(*\/pentestswarm OR *\\pentestswarm.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*armur\-ai\/pentestswarm* OR *PENTESTSWARM_AUTHORIZED* OR *pentestswarm\ scan\ * OR *pentestswarm\ serve* OR *pentestswarm\-lab\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects LazyOwn traffic in proxy logs. Beacon side: requests to the LazyOwn C2's default malleable route
/gmail/v1/users/ on a host that is not Google, the user agents of the beacon configuration LazyOwn ships
(LAzyOwnRedTeam, and a Windows string with both Chrome/120.0.0.0 and Firefox/120.0), and beacon paths through a
Cloudflare quick tunnel, which LazyOwn's redirector uses. Operator side: LazyOwn/1.0 on exploitalert.com searches and
lazyown-depconfuse/1.0 on PyPI checks. HTTPS needs TLS inspection.
false_positives: Authorized tests with LazyOwn
A Gmail API client that goes through a self-hosted gateway on another host name (selection_route)
name: LazyOwn Beacon Route, Beacon User Agents or Operator Clients in Proxy Logs
query: (url.original:*\/gmail\/v1\/users\/* AND (NOT ((url.domain:/.*\.[gG][oO][oO][gG][lL][eE][aA][pP][iI][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[gG][oO][oO][gG][lL][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/) OR (url.domain:/[gG][oO][oO][gG][lL][eE][aA][pP][iI][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/[gG][oO][oO][gG][lL][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/)))) OR ((user_agent.original:(*LAzyOwnRedTeam* OR *Chrome\/120.0.0.0\ Firefox\/120.0*)) OR (user_agent.original:(LazyOwn\/1.0 OR lazyown\-depconfuse\/*))) OR (url.domain:/.*\.[tT][rR][yY][cC][lL][oO][uU][dD][fF][lL][aA][rR][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ AND (url.original:(*\/gmail\/v1\/users\/* OR *\/command\/* OR *\/api\/poll\/* OR *\/stage\/beacon* OR *\/stage\/config*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects PentestCode (s0ld13rr/pentestcode, a hard fork of OpenCode) on the host that runs it: the pentestcode binary
and the shells it starts for its agents, the fixed seclists check of its ensure_tools tool, the proxychains file
/tmp/pc.conf that its tunnel_manage tool writes, its screenshot tool, and its install commands.
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentestCode
A different program that is also named pentestcode
name: PentestCode AI Pentest Agent Running or Installed
query: (process.executable:(*\/pentestcode OR *\\pentestcode.exe)) OR (process.parent.executable:(*\/pentestcode OR *\\pentestcode.exe)) OR process.command_line:*ls\ \/usr\/share\/seclists\ 2\>\/dev\/null\ \|\|\ ls\ \/opt\/seclists\ 2\>\/dev\/null\ \|\|\ ls\ \~\/seclists* OR process.command_line:*\-f\ \/tmp\/pc.conf* OR (process.command_line:*\-\-headless* AND process.command_line:*\-\-no\-sandbox* AND process.command_line:*\-\-screenshot\=\/tmp\/screenshot\-*) OR (process.command_line:(*pentestcode\-ai* OR *pentestcode\-bin* OR *s0ld13rr\/pentestcode* OR *s0ld13rr\/tap*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects command lines from Pentest Agent Suite (H-mmer/pentest-agents at 41d49b64) in a bounty workspace or a clone:
the Claude Code hooks it installs (scope_hook.py, chain_pressure_hook.py, validity_guard.py, cvss_version_guard.py,
file_path_guard.py, cost_hook.py through uv run python3), its statusline script, its two MCP servers
(mcp-bounty-server/server.py, mcp-writeup-server/server.py through uv run --with mcp), the camofox_ctl.sh wrapper that
starts the Camoufox stealth browser server, the workspace scaffolder and the cross-tool installer.
false_positives: Bug bounty researchers using Pentest Agent Suite with permission
name: Pentest Agent Suite Hooks, MCP Servers or Stealth Browser Started
query: (process.command_line:(*\/tools\/scope_hook.py* OR *\/tools\/chain_pressure_hook.py* OR *\/tools\/validity_guard.py* OR *\/tools\/cvss_version_guard.py* OR *\/tools\/file_path_guard.py* OR *\/tools\/pentest\-statusline.sh* OR *\/tools\/autopilot_gate.py* OR *\/tools\/coverage_record.py*)) OR (process.command_line:(*mcp\-bounty\-server\/server.py* OR *mcp\-writeup\-server\/server.py*)) OR process.command_line:*tools\/camofox_ctl.sh* OR (process.command_line:(*tools\/scaffold.py\ hackerone* OR *tools\/scaffold.py\ bugcrowd* OR *tools\/scaffold.py\ intigriti* OR *tools\/scaffold.py\ yeswehack* OR *\-m\ tools.installer\ install* OR *pentest\-agents\ install*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests whose user agent names the ARTEX agentic penetration testing framework or its
renamed builds (ScopeWeaver, AntiFox). Operators often keep the defaults. Matching is case-sensitive
in some backends, so the list carries the observed spellings.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Agentic Attack Framework User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the local_shell connector of hackingBuddyGPT driving a shell inside tmux. Each model command is framed by
tmux send-keys calls that type echo 'CMDSTART<8 hex>' and echo 'CMDEND<8 hex>' into the session, or, in its
fallback, echo "__CLEAR_<8 hex>__" and echo "__END_<8 hex>__". The commands then run on the machine that hosts the
tmux session.
false_positives: Researchers running hackingBuddyGPT in local shell mode on purpose
Other tmux automation that frames commands with the same marker words
name: hackingBuddyGPT Local Shell Command Markers Sent Through tmux
query: (process.executable:*\/tmux AND process.command_line:*send\-keys*) AND (process.command_line:(*echo\ 'CMDSTART* OR *echo\ 'CMDEND* OR *echo\ \"__CLEAR_* OR *echo\ \"__END_*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files 0security writes: its state folder ~/.0 (the database 0.db, the server-mode access-token file,
the analytics install id and the log of analytics it sent, saved engine and web connections, per-run state
under runs/, the installer's bin/0security), and the folder /tmp/zero-engine it creates on a remote computer
when it deploys an engine there over SSH.
false_positives: Developers and security teams who use 0security
Another program that keeps its state in a folder named .0
name: 0security State, Access Token or Remote Engine Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.0\/0.db OR *\/.0\/access\-token OR *\/.0\/analytics\-id OR *\/.0\/analytics\-sent.log OR *\/.0\/engines.json OR *\/.0\/web\-connections.json OR *\/.0\/bin\/0security OR *\\.0\\0.db OR *\\.0\\access\-token OR *\\.0\\analytics\-id OR *\\.0\\analytics\-sent.log)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.0\/runs\/* OR *\\.0\\runs\\*)) OR TargetFilename:\/tmp\/zero\-engine\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects nmap, nuclei, httpx, katana and ffuf started with the exact argument lists that the Cybermes Go MCP server
(cybermes-mcp, Zyrexnn/Cybermes at 149b9a66) builds for its cybermes_nmap_scan, cybermes_nuclei_scan,
cybermes_http_probe, cybermes_recon_crawl and cybermes_fuzz_endpoints tools. The parent is cybermes-mcp. An operator
typing the same tools by hand rarely uses the same flags in the same order.
false_positives: Authorized security testers who run Cybermes
Scripts that happen to call these scanners with the same flags in the same order
name: Scanners Started With Cybermes MCP Argument Order
query: ((process.parent.executable:(*\/cybermes\-mcp OR *\\cybermes\-mcp.exe)) OR process.parent.executable:*cybermes\-mcp\-v*) OR (process.command_line:*\-sT\ \-\-open\ \-T3\ \-\-max\-rate\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-oN\ \-\ *) OR process.command_line:*\ \-silent\ \-jsonl\ \-timeout\ 10\ \-duc* OR process.command_line:*\ \-silent\ \-status\-code\ \-title\ \-tech\-detect\ \-json\ \-timeout\ * OR process.command_line:*\ \-jc\ \-silent\ \-ct\ * OR (process.command_line:*\/FUZZ\ \-w\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-timeout\ 5\ \-s\ \-json*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files the DarkMoon stack writes: the GPU state file and MCP boot log in its containers, the toolbox
workflow output folder, the campaign store under darkmoon-settings, and the Markdown report
pentest_report_<host>_<date>-<time>.md.
false_positives: Security teams running DarkMoon
Other tools that name reports pentest_report_<something>.md (the report selection alone is weaker)
name: DarkMoon Configuration, Campaign or Report Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(\/run\/darkmoon\-gpu.env OR \/tmp\/darkmoon\-mcp\-boot.log)) OR TargetFilename:\/opt\/darkmoon\/out\/* OR TargetFilename:*\/darkmoon\-settings\/campaigns\/camp_* OR (TargetFilename:*\/reports\/pentest_report_* AND TargetFilename:*.md)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Xalgorix writes on the host that runs it: its environment files, its systemd unit, and the scan
data folder with scan.json and events.jsonl for every target.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters and security teams running Xalgorix
name: Xalgorix Configuration, Service or Scan Data Written
query: (TargetFilename:(\/etc\/xalgorix.env OR \/etc\/systemd\/system\/xalgorix.service OR \/tmp\/xalgorix.log OR \/tmp\/xalgorix\-crash.log)) OR TargetFilename:*\/.xalgorix\/data\/* OR TargetFilename:*\/.xalgorix.env

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host resolving a name built by Agentic Bug Hunter's OOB helper (awarexone/Agentic-Bug-Hunter at 82f4512e,
bughunter/tools/oob_listener.py): a first label of ssrf-, xxe-, sqli-, rce- or log4j- followed by 12 hex characters,
in front of the operator's interactsh host. A server that resolves one ran an injected SSRF, XXE, SQL, command or
Log4Shell payload.
false_positives: Hosts with names that start with one of the class words and 12 hex characters
name: Agentic Bug Hunter Out-of-Band Payload Marker Resolved
query: dns.question.name:/(ssrf|xxe|sqli|rce|log4j)-[0-9a-f]{12}\..*/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the wrapper CTF Agent puts around every command it runs through the Docker API in a solver sandbox:
bash -c "timeout --signal=KILL --kill-after=5 <seconds> bash -c '<command>'" (backend/sandbox.py:165-171). Each new
sandbox first runs uname -m this way with a 10 second limit, so the exact start command is
timeout --signal=KILL --kill-after=5 10 bash -c 'uname -m' (backend/agents/claude_solver.py:93,
backend/agents/codex_solver.py:177). The processes are inside the ctf-sandbox container; the sensor has to see
container processes.
false_positives: Scripts that use the same timeout options around bash -c; check for many of them from one container
name: CTF Agent Sandbox Command Wrapper in a Container
query: process.command_line:*timeout\ \-\-signal\=KILL\ \-\-kill\-after\=5\ * AND process.command_line:*\ bash\ \-c\ *

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files RedAI (kpolley/redai) writes under its home folder ~/.redai/: scan runs in runs/<runId>/ (run.json,
events.ndjson, state.json, report.md, report.json, report.html, agent transcripts and validation evidence under
artifacts/), the copied browser profile, and validator environments in validator-environments/<id>/environment.json.
REDAI_HOME moves the folder.
false_positives: Authorized application security tests with RedAI
Another program that keeps a folder named .redai in the home directory
name: RedAI Run, Report or Validator Environment Files Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/.redai\/runs\/* OR *\/.redai\/validator\-environments\/* OR *\/.redai\/artifacts\/* OR *\\.redai\\runs\\* OR *\\.redai\\validator\-environments\\* OR *\\.redai\\artifacts\\*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Pensar Apex command line tool (npm package @pensar/apex, binary pensar) starting a headless pentest, a
targeted pentest, a threat model or a detached local run worker, its installation, and the kali-apex container from
the repository's compose file. Command names come from src/cli.ts:266-290, src/cli/agent-runs.ts:27-38,
README.md and container/docker-compose.yml:2-5. A bare "pensar" (the TUI) is too short to match on its own.
false_positives: Developers and security teams that use Pensar Apex
name: Pensar Apex CLI or Kali Container Started
query: (process.command_line:(*pensar\ pentest\ * OR *pensar\ targeted\-pentest\ * OR *pensar\ threat\-model* OR *pensar\ agent\-runs\ worker* OR *pensar.js\ pentest\ * OR *pensar.js\ targeted\-pentest\ *)) OR (process.command_line:(*@pensar\/apex* OR *pensarai.com\/install.sh* OR *pensarai.com\/apex.ps1* OR *brew\ install\ apex*)) OR (process.command_line:(*exec\ kali\-apex* OR *kali\-apex\:latest*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests a Nebula (BerylliumSec/nebula) core receives: device pairing redemption at
/api/v1/auth/pairings/redeem, background tool results posted to /api/v1/automation-processes/<id>/results, and
its terminal client's user agent nebula-chat. In the logs of a web server or reverse proxy you run, these mean a
Nebula core is served from it.
false_positives: A Nebula core you run on purpose behind your own reverse proxy
name: Nebula Core Pairing, Tool Results or Terminal Client in Web Logs
query: url.path:\/api\/v1\/auth\/pairings\/redeem OR (url.path:\/api\/v1\/automation\-processes\/* AND url.path:*\/results) OR user_agent.original:nebula\-chat

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files the research PentestAgent (nbshenxm/pentest-agent, arXiv 2411.05185) writes: the execution agent's
misspelled log exeuction_agent.log, the planning agent's CVE and exploit scoring files, and the recon agent's chat
memory. The scoring file names are built in code; the folders come from config.yaml.
false_positives: Researchers reproducing the PentestAgent paper
name: PentestAgent (Paper Code) Logs, Recon Memory or Exploit Planning Files Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/exeuction_agent.log OR (TargetFilename:(*\/CVEMAP\/cvemap.json* OR *\/conf_score_from_code_* OR *\/otpt_from_code_* OR *\/vul_impact_features_from_code_* OR *\/isRemote_features_from_code_* OR *\/exp_maturity_features_*)) OR TargetFilename:*\/Trend_Score.json OR (TargetFilename:*\/recon_memory\/* AND TargetFilename:*.json)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Shannon (KeygraphHQ/shannon, npm @keygraph/shannon) on the host that runs it: the CLI starting a scan, the
docker run that starts its worker container (image keygraph/shannon, container shannon-worker-<hex>, labels
shannon.workspace and shannon.workflow-id), the worker process inside it, the per-agent browser sessions
(playwright-cli -s=agent1 to agent5) and the Typst command that renders its PDF report.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Shannon
Developers evaluating Shannon
name: Shannon AI Pentest Agent CLI, Worker Container or Report Renderer
query: process.command_line:*@keygraph\/shannon* OR process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ ]))?shannon["']?[ ]+start[ ](.*[ ])?(-u|--url)[ =].*/ OR (process.command_line:(*keygraph\/shannon\:* OR *\-\-name\ shannon\-worker\-* OR *shannon.workspace\=* OR *shannon.workflow\-id\=* OR *TEMPORAL_ADDRESS\=shannon\-temporal\:7233*)) OR (process.command_line:*temporal\/worker.js* AND process.command_line:*\-\-task\-queue* AND process.command_line:*\-\-workflow\-id*) OR process.command_line:/.*playwright-cli[ ]+(.*[ ])?-s=agent[1-6](([ ]).*)?/ OR process.command_line:*brand\=Shannon\ \|\ AI\ Pentester\ by\ Keygraph*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Agentic Bug Hunter (awarexone/Agentic-Bug-Hunter at 82f4512e) writes on the host that runs it: its
home folder ~/.bughunter/ (config.json, google_oauth.json, workspace/), the scope cache ~/.cache/bbhunt/scope/, the
hunt memory logs, the per-target spray audit log recon/<target>/spray/attempts-<time>.jsonl, the autonomous agent
session file, and the skills and agents its installer copies into a coding assistant's folder.
false_positives: Security staff who use Agentic Bug Hunter
name: Agentic Bug Hunter Configuration, Memory or Spray Log Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.bughunter\/* OR *\/.cache\/bbhunt\/scope\/* OR *\/hunt\-memory\/audit.jsonl* OR *\/hunt\-memory\/journal.jsonl* OR *\/skills\/johnwick\/SKILL.md* OR *\/skills\/omni\-killchain\/SKILL.md* OR *\/agents\/credential\-hunter.md*)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/spray\/attempts\-* AND TargetFilename:*.jsonl) OR TargetFilename:*\/autonomous_session.json

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects outbound requests from a host running 0security, by the user agents it sets itself: 0security/<version>
on usage analytics to PostHog, @0/cli/update-check on its daily release check against the GitHub API,
@0/cli/<version> on uploads to its cloud worker, 0security-audit-sink on audit log forwarding, 0security on Kimi
device sign-in, and 0/1.0 on its DuckDuckGo fallback web search; and any request to its cloud host
cloud.0.security. These are HTTPS, so the user agents are visible only to a proxy that decrypts.
false_positives: Developers and security teams who use 0security
name: 0security Client Traffic in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(0security\/* OR @0\/cli\/*)) OR (user_agent.original:(0security OR 0security\-audit\-sink OR 0\/1.0)) OR url.domain:/[cC][lL][oO][uU][dD]\.0\.[sS][eE][cC][uU][rR][iI][tT][yY]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects commands that Pentest Copilot (BugBase) runs on its work host or Kali box: the login-shell wrapper it puts
around every agent command ("${SHELL:-$(command -v bash || command -v sh)}" -l -c), the heredoc it runs Python
scripts through (PYTHON_SCRIPT_EOF), the codex or claude CLI it calls with the system prompt "You are an inference
transport inside Pentest Copilot", its Kali container reading /run/pentest-copilot.env, its work folder check and
the Burp CA it adds to the browser's certificate store. All of these strings are in the code.
false_positives: Authorized tests, bug bounty work or CTF play with Pentest Copilot
name: Pentest Copilot Agent Command Wrapper or Subscription Transport
query: process.command_line:(*\"$\{SHELL\:\-$\(command\ \-v\ bash\ \|\|\ command\ \-v\ sh\)\}\"\ \-l\ \-c* OR *\<\<\ 'PYTHON_SCRIPT_EOF'* OR *You\ are\ an\ inference\ transport\ inside\ Pentest\ Copilot* OR *\/run\/pentest\-copilot.env* OR *.pentest\-copilot\-write\-test* OR *Pentest\ Copilot\ Burp\ CA*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the placeholder paths ARTEX agents request to learn how a site answers a missing resource,
right before a burst of guesses. These names have no legitimate caller.
false_positives: Unknown
name: ARTEX Placeholder Probe Paths
query: url.path:(*\/zzz\-nonexistent\-xyz123* OR *zzz_nonexistent_abc.txt* OR *Notexist\-xyz*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files PentestCode writes on the host that runs it: the engagement folder ~/.pentestcode/engagements/<name>/
(state.json, findings.md, changelog.json, decisions.json, agent-contexts.json, wordlists.json, reflection.json), its
knowledge base, the skills it seeds from the binary, and the OpenCode-style data folder ~/.local/share/pentestcode/.
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentestCode
name: PentestCode Engagement State or Data Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.pentestcode\/engagements\/* OR *\/.pentestcode\/knowledge\/* OR *\/.pentestcode\/skills\/bundled\/*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.local\/share\/pentestcode\/* OR *\/.config\/pentestcode\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Nebula (BerylliumSec/nebula) writes: its core data folder ~/.local/share/nebula/v3/ (database,
runtime/operator-token, runtime/connection.json, logs), the desktop app's data folder io.nebula.security/core/, the
process group files /tmp/nebula-process-<id>.pid and /run/nebula/public-ip in its Kali containers, the files it
bakes into its Kali image, the build folder /tmp/nebula-kali-*, and its protected memory runner's state.
false_positives: Penetration testers and security teams running Nebula
Other software named Nebula that uses the same folder names
name: Nebula Data Folder, Runtime or Container Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.local\/share\/nebula\/v3\/* OR *\/io.nebula.security\/core\/*)) OR (TargetFilename:\/tmp\/nebula\-process\-* AND TargetFilename:*.pid) OR (TargetFilename:(\/run\/nebula\/public\-ip OR \/etc\/cron.d\/nebula\-public\-ip OR \/usr\/local\/share\/nebula\/security\-tools.json OR \/usr\/local\/bin\/nebula\-terminal\-entrypoint OR \/usr\/local\/lib\/nebula\-public\-ip\-update)) OR (TargetFilename:\/tmp\/nebula\-kali\-* AND TargetFilename:*\/Dockerfile) OR (TargetFilename:(\/run\/nebula\-memory\-runner\/* OR \/var\/lib\/nebula\-memory\-runner\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects traffic to a cyber-harness Web Hub, the console that cyber-scan and cyber-audit agent nodes connect to: the
node WebSocket /api/aop/node/ws, the browser WebSocket /api/aop/application/ws and its ConnectRPC services
/cyber.rpc.<pkg>.<Service>/. Also detects a download of a cyber-harness or AIScan release from GitHub, directly or
through the ghfast.top mirror that the Hub's Quick Connect offers, which is how a new node is installed.
false_positives: Security teams running or installing cyber-harness for authorized tests
name: cyber-harness Web Hub Traffic or Release Download Through a Proxy
query: (url.original:(*\/api\/aop\/node\/ws* OR *\/api\/aop\/application\/ws* OR *\/cyber.rpc.aop.AOPService\/* OR *\/cyber.rpc.chat.SessionService\/* OR *\/cyber.rpc.scan.ScanService\/* OR *\/cyber.rpc.config.ConfigService\/* OR *\/cyber.rpc.agent.AgentService\/* OR *\/cyber.rpc.system.SystemService\/* OR *\/cyber.rpc.artifact.ArtifactService\/*)) OR (url.original:(*github.com\/chainreactors\/cyber\-harness\/releases\/download\/* OR *github.com\/chainreactors\/cyber\-harness\/releases\/latest\/download\/* OR *github.com\/chainreactors\/aiscan\/releases\/download\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Windows persistence commands in the CyberStrikeAI implant: a Run value named SystemUpdate added with
reg.exe, or a SystemUpdate scheduled task created with schtasks. Kaspersky saw the SystemUpdate task, running as
SYSTEM and also created on remote hosts, in attacks on education organizations.
false_positives: Software that really names its updater task or Run value SystemUpdate (check the binary it starts)
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Windows Persistence Named SystemUpdate
query: (process.command_line:*reg* AND process.command_line:*\ add\ * AND process.command_line:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run* AND process.command_line:*SystemUpdate*) OR (process.command_line:*schtasks* AND process.command_line:*\/create* AND process.command_line:*SystemUpdate*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects command lines that carry the names ARTEX agents give their own test artifacts: artex-probe
files with a counting number, ArtexProbe accounts, the VAPOR PANDA working folder artx5v, art18-
comments and probe marker strings.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Artifact Names in Command Lines
query: process.command_line:(*artex\-probe\-* OR *ArtexProbe* OR *\\ProgramData\\artx5v* OR *art18\-* OR *ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE* OR *ARTX_PERSIST_OK* OR *artex_control_marker_zz9q*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Cochise launchers: uv run cochise, the cochise console script in a virtual environment, python
src/cochise.py from clones older than February 2026, and the cochise-replay and cochise-analyze-* scripts that read
its run logs (pyproject.toml:21-25, README.md:103,116). Cochise drives a Kali VM over SSH with a model choosing the
commands, against Active Directory networks.
false_positives: Authorized research runs of Cochise and replays of its logs
name: Cochise AI Pentest Agent Launcher
query: (process.command_line:(*\/bin\/cochise OR *\\Scripts\\cochise.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*uv\ run\ cochise* OR *src\/cochise.py* OR *cochise.cli.cochise* OR *\/bin\/cochise\-replay\ * OR *\/bin\/cochise\-analyze\-* OR *uv\ run\ cochise\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests to the operator and strategy API of an Incalmo C2 server: the LLM agent action queue, the environment state
report, manual command tasking and the initial environment call, and POST /agent/download.
false_positives: Research use of Incalmo in a lab
name: Incalmo C2 Operator API Requested Through a Proxy
query: (url.original:(*\/get_llm_agent_action* OR *\/start_llm_agent_action* OR *\/stream_llm_agent_logs* OR *\/update_environment_state* OR *\/send_manual_command* OR *\/get_initial_environment*)) OR (cs-method:POST AND url.original:*\/agent\/download*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects CTF Agent playing against a CTFd platform you run: its CTFd client sends exactly
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64) AppleWebKit/537.36 on every request (backend/ctfd.py:14,40-46), polls
/api/v1/challenges?per_page=500 and the solves endpoint every 5 seconds (backend/poller.py:24,122-125,
backend/ctfd.py:127,173-189) and submits flags to /api/v1/challenges/attempt (backend/ctfd.py:142-149). With no
token configured it logs in as admin with the password admin (backend/config.py:10-12, backend/ctfd.py:49-76).
false_positives: Authorized CTF play with CTF Agent; whether automated solvers are allowed is the event's rule
name: CTF Agent CTFd Client User Agent in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:"Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 6.1; WOW64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36"

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects KaliGPT, a CLI AI pentest agent, requesting a page on your web server through its own HTTP tools.
"HackerX WebRequestFramework/1.0" comes from web_request_analysis and get_raw_response: one request per call, any
method and body the model chooses, redirects followed. "LocalScraper/1.0" comes from get_local_server_content, a
GET that extracts the page text. Scans run through the shell tool (nmap, curl, gau) carry those tools' own user
agents.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with KaliGPT
Another scraper that uses the user agent LocalScraper/1.0
name: KaliGPT Tool User Agent in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:("HackerX WebRequestFramework\/1.0" OR LocalScraper\/1.0)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the cracker role of Ares (dreadnode/ares). Every hashcat job runs as nice -n <adj> hashcat ... --session
ares-hc-<pid>-<seq> --restore-disable --potfile-disable, and every John job with --session=ares-jtr-<pid>-<seq>
(ares-tools/src/cracker.rs:18-30,100-108,854,1073).
false_positives: Authorized Ares operations
name: Ares Hashcat or John Session Name
query: process.command_line:(*\-\-session\ ares\-hc\-* OR *\-\-session\=ares\-hc\-* OR *\-\-session\=ares\-jtr\-* OR *\-\-session\ ares\-jtr\-*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the NPS client (npc) hand-off that BreachWeave's shipped skills (redis-webroot-rce, intranet-pentest,
known-product-exploit, remote-cmd-execution) tell the solver to run on a compromised host: certutil or curl/wget
fetching npc from the operator's bridge under /files/nps/npc_ (port 44944 in the skills), and npc started with
-server=<bridge>:<port> -vkey=auto through wmic process call create, setsid, nohup or a scheduled task named
"Windows Update". The vkey value "auto" and the /files/nps/ path are the skills' literals.
false_positives: Administrators who run the NPS client with the literal vkey "auto" (NPS clients normally pass a per-client key)
name: BreachWeave Playbook NPS Client Staged on a Host
query: process.command_line:*\/files\/nps\/npc_* OR (process.command_line:*\-server\=* AND process.command_line:*\-vkey\=auto*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects MCP Kali Server's Metasploit route: the API server writes the module and its options to the fixed file
/tmp/mks_msf_resource.rc and runs msfconsole -q -r /tmp/mks_msf_resource.rc. Under the Kali package's service the
file sits in the service's private /tmp, but the command line keeps the /tmp path.
false_positives: Authorized tests driven through MCP Kali Server
name: MCP Kali Server Metasploit Resource File Run
query: process.command_line:*mks_msf_resource.rc*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects numasec's built-in probes against a web server: the AppSec probe user agent numasec-appsec-probe/ (with
' OR 1=1--, <script>numasec-xss</script>, a login as numasec-probe@example.invalid and Origin https://evil.example),
the page fetch fallback user agent numasec, the directory fuzzer's /numasec_404_check_<epoch ms> baseline, and the
service prober's request with the host header target.
false_positives: Authorized tests with numasec
A host or virtual host literally named target (selection_service_probe)
name: numasec Probe Markers in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:numasec OR user_agent.original:numasec\-appsec\-probe\/* OR url.path:\/numasec_404_check_* OR url.query:*numasec\-xss* OR (url.domain:/[tT][aA][rR][gG][eE][tT]/ AND url.path:\/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests Nebula (BerylliumSec/nebula) makes with its own user agents: nebula-chat (its terminal client
talking to a remote core), Nebula-Terminal/1 (its Kali containers checking their public address at api.ipify.org
every five minutes) and Nebula/3 knowledge-source-fetcher or -renderer (pages an operator adds as knowledge);
and requests to a core's device pairing and tool result endpoints.
false_positives: Penetration testers and security teams running Nebula
name: Nebula User Agents or Core API in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(nebula\-chat OR Nebula\-Terminal\/1)) OR user_agent.original:Nebula\/3\ knowledge\-source\-* OR url.original:*\/api\/v1\/auth\/pairings\/redeem* OR (url.original:*\/api\/v1\/automation\-processes\/* AND url.original:*\/results*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the far-host hive dump of Ares (dreadnode/ares) on a SQL Server it reached over a linked server. Ares runs
a fixed PowerShell script through xp_cmdshell as powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand
JABFAHIAcgBv... (always the same base64, since the script has no variables), and the script runs reg save HKLM\SAM,
HKLM\SYSTEM and HKLM\SECURITY to %TEMP%\a.hive, b.hive and c.hive (lateral/mssql.rs:345-385,480-497).
false_positives: Authorized Ares operations
An administrator who saves registry hives to files named a.hive, b.hive or c.hive
name: Ares SQL Server Hive Dump Through xp_cmdshell
query: process.command_line:*JABFAHIAcgBvAHIAQQBjAHQAaQBvAG4AUAByAGUAZgBlAHIAZQBuAGMAZQA9ACcAUwB0AG8AcAAnAAoAJAB0AD0AJABlAG4AdgA6AFQARQBNAFAACgAkAGEAPQAiACQAdABcAGEALgBoAGkAdgBlACIA* OR (process.command_line:*save* AND process.command_line:*HKLM\\SAM* AND process.command_line:*\\a.hive*) OR (process.command_line:*save* AND process.command_line:*HKLM\\SYSTEM* AND process.command_line:*\\b.hive*) OR (process.command_line:*save* AND process.command_line:*HKLM\\SECURITY* AND process.command_line:*\\c.hive*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a lookup of cloud.0.security, the default host of 0security's cloud service (cloud credentials and the
Windows evidence worker). It is used only when an operator has configured a cloud token.
false_positives: Developers and security teams who use the 0security cloud service
name: 0security Cloud Host Lookup
query: dns.question.name:/[cC][lL][oO][uU][dD]\.0\.[sS][eE][cC][uU][rR][iI][tT][yY]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects /tmp/.dm_proof, the file DarkMoon's database and cache agents write on a target to prove command
execution or file write: PostgreSQL COPY ... TO PROGRAM 'id > /tmp/.dm_proof', MySQL INTO OUTFILE, sys_exec,
and a Redis cron line. A database or cache server process writing it means an attack worked.
false_positives: Authorized tests with DarkMoon
name: DarkMoon Proof File /tmp/.dm_proof Written on a Server
query: TargetFilename:\/tmp\/.dm_proof

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Decepticon installer (curl https://decepticon.red/install | bash, irm https://decepticon.red/install.ps1),
the Decepticon launcher commands, and its containers being pulled or run from ghcr.io/bittersecurity/decepticon-*
(litellm, sandbox, langgraph, cli, skillogy, rea, c2-sliver, c2-havoc).
false_positives: Authorized tests and research with Decepticon
name: Decepticon AI Red Team Agent Installed or Started
query: (process.command_line:(*decepticon.red\/install* OR *raw.githubusercontent.com\/BitterSecurity\/Decepticon\/*)) OR process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ ]))?decepticon(\.exe)?["']?[ ]+(onboard|start|stop|status|doctor|update|attach|resume|mcp[ ]+serve)(([ ]).*)?/ OR process.command_line:*ghcr.io\/bittersecurity\/decepticon\-* OR ((process.command_line:(*decepticon\-sandbox* OR *decepticon\-langgraph* OR *decepticon\-c2\-sliver* OR *decepticon\-c2\-havoc*)) AND process.command_line:*docker*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a shell command run by Mitsu's built-in bash tool, which the model calls for anything the Armory tools do
not cover. Mitsu runs every such command as /bin/bash -o pipefail -c <command> from its own Python process
(installed as the mitsu console script, or python -m mitsu). When the command contains sudo, Mitsu asks the
operator for the password in its UI and runs sudo -S -p "" -- /bin/bash -o pipefail -c <command> instead, with
the password on standard input. Armory installers also run as /bin/bash -o pipefail -c <script>.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with Mitsu
Another program installed as a script named mitsu that runs bash with -o pipefail
name: Mitsu Shell Tool Command
query: process.command_line:*\/bin\/bash\ \-o\ pipefail\ \-c\ * AND ((process.parent.command_line:(*\/bin\/mitsu OR *\ \-m\ mitsu)) OR process.parent.command_line:*\/uv\/tools\/mitsu\/*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: A request, sign-in or cloud API call carried a user agent that names the ARTEX framework or a renamed build.
name: ARTEX Agentic Attack Framework User Agent

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects commands that Pensar Apex (pensarai/apex) builds for its agent tools. Apex adds -H "User-Agent: pensar-apex"
(its default session header) to every curl, wget, nuclei, ffuf, gobuster, httpx, feroxbuster, dirb, wfuzz, wpscan,
sqlmap or nikto command the model writes against an in-scope host, and its get_page tool uses PensarBot/1.0. Its
callback listener starts as node -e "eval(Buffer.from('<base64>' ..." where the base64 always begins with the
encoded first line "use strict"; // Apex callback listener, and its readiness probe evaluates the APEX_CB_PROBE
variable. Its file, grep, glob and list helpers and its prompt injection payload writer pass APEX_* variables and
heredoc markers. All of these strings are in the code (src/core/http/targetHeaders.ts:242-316,
src/core/agents/offSecAgent/tools/callbackListener.ts:32-42, executeCommand.ts:244-257, grepImpl.ts:468,
globImpl.ts:97, listFilesImpl.ts:195, fileWorkspaceRemote.ts:221). The User-Agent value can be changed with
pensar config headers; the helper strings cannot without editing Apex.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests run with Pensar Apex or Pensar Console
name: Pensar Apex Agent Command Markers
query: process.command_line:(*User\-Agent\:\ pensar\-apex* OR *PensarBot\/1.0* OR *InVzZSBzdHJpY3QiOwovLyBBcGV4IGNhbGxiYWNrIGxpc3RlbmVy* OR *process.env.APEX_CB_PROBE* OR *APEX_HIDDEN_PAYLOAD_COUNT* OR *APEX_FILE_PAYLOAD_COUNT* OR *__APEX_GREP_EXIT_* OR *\<\<'APEX_GLOB_PY'* OR *\<\<'APEX_LIST_PY'*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects two example payloads from the ARTEMIS specialist prompts that a model may send as written: the PHP object
O:8:"stdClass":1:{s:4:"test";s:11:"injection";} (codex-rs/core/web.md:75; the length 11 is wrong for "injection",
which makes the string distinctive) and the open redirect target https://attacker.site from
/nav?to=/logout&next=https://attacker.site (codex-rs/core/client_side_web.md:48). They are prompt examples, so the
model may change them; a match means the request was written from this prompt or copied from it.
false_positives: Copies of the same PHP example in other tools or training material
Other tests that use attacker.site as a redirect target
name: ARTEMIS Prompt Example Payloads in Web Logs
query: (url.query:(*s\:11\:%22injection%22* OR *s%3A11%3A%22injection%22* OR *s\:11\:\"injection\"*)) OR (url.query:(*\/\/attacker.site* OR *%2F%2Fattacker.site*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests from CyberStrikeAI's webshell manager to a planted webshell: its hard-coded user agent, or the
"echo :OSPROBE_%OS%:END" command it sends in the cmd parameter (visible in GET mode).
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI
name: CyberStrikeAI Webshell Manager User Agent or OS Probe in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:*CyberStrikeAI\-WebShell\/* OR (url.query:(*OSPROBE_* OR *OSPROBE%5F*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files of MCP Kali Server: the Metasploit resource file /tmp/mks_msf_resource.rc its API server writes before
every Metasploit run (inside a systemd private /tmp under the Kali package's service), and the files the Kali package
mcp-kali-server installs (/usr/share/mcp-kali-server/, the wrapper scripts, their /etc/default files and the
kali-server-mcp and mcp-server systemd units).
false_positives: Kali users who installed mcp-kali-server for authorized testing or CTF work
name: MCP Kali Server Files Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/mks_msf_resource.rc OR TargetFilename:\/usr\/share\/mcp\-kali\-server\/* OR (TargetFilename:(*\/usr\/bin\/kali\-server\-mcp OR *\/etc\/default\/kali\-server\-mcp OR *\/systemd\/system\/kali\-server\-mcp.service))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the two user agents hard-coded in cyber-harness (chainreactors/cyber-harness, formerly AIScan), an LLM agent
harness that drives the chainreactors scanners: the exact user agent cyber (aiscan in builds before September 2026)
of the scan pipeline's basic-auth check, sent to a URL that answered 401 just before the zombie stage guesses
passwords against it, and the user agent of its fetch tool, Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; cyber/1.0;
+https://github.com/chainreactors/cyber-harness). Both are code defaults.
false_positives: Authorized tests with cyber-harness or AIScan
A script or client that sets its user agent to the bare word cyber or aiscan
name: cyber-harness User Agent in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(cyber OR aiscan)) OR (user_agent.original:(*github.com\/chainreactors\/cyber\-harness\)* OR *github.com\/chainreactors\/aiscan\)*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests Pentest Swarm AI sends when it maps an API or verifies a finding: the negative-control path
/nx-<16 hex> (also under /api/), the open redirect host evil.pentestswarm.invalid, the template check 191*193, and
its own user agents. All are defaults of the published code.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Pentest Swarm AI
An application with real paths named nx- and 16 hex characters
name: Pentest Swarm AI Probe Marker in Web Logs
query: (cs-method:GET AND url.path:/\/(api\/)?nx-[0-9a-f]{16}/) OR (url.query:(*evil.pentestswarm.invalid* OR *191\*193* OR *191%2A193*)) OR user_agent.original:pentestswarm\-*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the two-stage Shadow Credentials chain of Ares (dreadnode/ares), an LLM-driven Active Directory attack
agent. Its pywhisker wrapper always writes the exported PFX to <temp>/ares_shadowcred_<millis>-<pid>-<seq>_<account>
and sets the PFX passphrase to the fixed string ares-shadow-cred; the follow-up certipy auth call opens that file
with -password ares-shadow-cred (ares-tools/src/acl.rs:262,270,409-418,456-480, privesc/adcs.rs:285-297).
The rule fires on the attacking host, where the tools run.
false_positives: Authorized Ares operations
name: Ares Shadow Credentials Passphrase or PFX Name
query: process.command_line:(*ares\-shadow\-cred* OR *\/ares_shadowcred_*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agent of CAI's fetch_url tool, Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like
Gecko) Chrome/124.0 Safari/537.36. The Chrome version has two parts where real Chrome sends four (124.0.0.0). The
operator can change it with CAI_FETCH_USER_AGENT; other scrapers may copy the same short form.
false_positives: Scrapers that send the same shortened Chrome version
Authorized tests with CAI
name: CAI fetch_url User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:("Mozilla\/5.0 \(X11; Linux x86_64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36 \(KHTML, like Gecko\) Chrome\/124.0 Safari\/537.36" OR Mozilla\/5.0\+\(X11;\+Linux\+x86_64\)\+AppleWebKit\/537.36\+\(KHTML,\+like\+Gecko\)\+Chrome\/124.0\+Safari\/537.36)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the RedAmon Docker stack being run (its container names, control script and sandbox servers) and the
tunnels it opens for reverse shells: ngrok or chisel forwarding port 4444 to the Metasploit handler in its Kali
sandbox. RedAmon is a penetration testing platform; on a host that is not a tester's, find out who installed it.
false_positives: Penetration testers and students running RedAmon
Another tool that forwards port 4444 through ngrok or chisel, which is also worth a look
name: RedAmon Stack or Reverse Shell Tunnel on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*redamon\-kali* OR *redamon\-agent* OR *redamon\-webapp* OR *redamon\-recon\-* OR *redamon\-docker\-broker* OR *\/opt\/mcp_servers\/run_servers.py* OR *\/opt\/mcp_servers\/tunnel_manager.py* OR *redamon.sh\ *)) OR process.command_line:*ngrok\ tcp\ 4444* OR (process.command_line:*chisel\ client* AND process.command_line:*R\:4444\:localhost\:4444*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the pivot recipe PentestCode's tunnel_manage tool hands its agents, run on a compromised Linux host: a
base64 copy of chisel or ligolo-ng assembled in /tmp from 2 KB chunks, decoded, made executable and started from
/tmp, then connected back to the attacker as a reverse SOCKS (chisel, port 8000) or a ligolo-ng agent (port 11601).
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentestCode or an operator who follows the same chisel or ligolo-ng recipe
name: PentestCode Pivot Binary Staging or Tunnel Agent on a Foothold
query: (process.command_line:*base64\ \-d\ \/tmp\/* AND process.command_line:*.b64\ \>\ \/tmp\/* AND process.command_line:*chmod\ \+x\ \/tmp\/*) OR (process.command_line:*\/tmp\/* AND process.command_line:*\ client\ * AND process.command_line:*\:8000\ R\:* AND process.command_line:*\:socks*) OR (process.command_line:*\/tmp\/* AND process.command_line:*\ \-connect\ * AND process.command_line:*\:11601* AND process.command_line:*\-ignore\-cert*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups for payload hosts that ThreatDefence saw active in ARTEX operator toolkits on November 20, 2026.
Fortinet separately reports the vietnam852.com hosts serving Gh0st RAT and an XMRig miner to brute-forced SQL Servers.
false_positives: Unknown
name: DNS Query for Payload Hosts Active in ARTEX Operator Toolkits
query: (dns.question.name:/[vV][iI][eE][tT][nN][aA][mM]852\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[zZ][hH][zZ][yY]999\.[nN][eE][tT]/ OR dns.question.name:/[jJ][iI][aA][nN][cC][aA][iI]008\.[cC][oO][mM]/) OR (dns.question.name:/.*\.[vV][iI][eE][tT][nN][aA][mM]852\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[zZ][hH][zZ][yY]999\.[nN][eE][tT]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[jJ][iI][aA][nN][cC][aA][iI]008\.[cC][oO][mM]/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the provider CLI processes OpenHack v2 (openhackai/OpenHack) starts when it reuses a Claude Code or Codex
subscription login: claude with --safe-mode and the settings {"disableAllHooks":true,"apiKeyHelper":"",
"forceLoginMethod":"claudeai"} and a system prompt that says "You are a source-review worker inside OpenHack",
or codex exec whose output schema and instructions file sit in a temporary folder named openhack-subscription-.
One process starts per model turn, so a scan produces many.
false_positives: Developers scanning their own code with OpenHack v2 in subscription mode
Another wrapper that starts Claude Code with the same settings
name: Claude Code or Codex CLI Started by OpenHack
query: (process.command_line:*\-\-safe\-mode* AND process.command_line:*disableAllHooks* AND process.command_line:*forceLoginMethod*) OR process.command_line:*openhack\-subscription\-* OR process.command_line:*source\-review\ worker\ inside\ OpenHack*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests to oob.openhack.com, the out-of-band collector of the OpenHack v0.x pentest agent (PyPI openhack
0.2.4). A server calling https://oob.openhack.com/<label>-<12 hex>/... ran a blind SSRF, command injection or XXE
payload the agent sent; the agent's own host calls /_hits?token=...&q=<marker> with the user agent openhack to read
the callbacks.
false_positives: The workstation or server that runs the OpenHack v0.x agent, when it polls the collector
name: Request to the OpenHack Out-of-Band Collector
query: url.domain:/[oO][oO][bB]\.[oO][pP][eE][nN][hH][aA][cC][kK]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[oO][oO][bB]\.[oO][pP][eE][nN][hH][aA][cC][kK]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Virga's operator CLI building a beacon: it runs go build on ./internal/implant/main.go with linker flags
that set github.com/r74tech/virga/internal/implant/config.BuildC2Host, BuildC2Port, BuildC2Path and
BuildUserAgent, and with the build tag llama_selfextract when the beacon carries a local model. The Go linker
child process receives the same -X values. The command line names the C2 host and port of the new beacon.
false_positives: Red teams and researchers building Virga beacons
name: Virga Beacon Built with go build
query: (process.command_line:(*internal\/implant\/config.BuildC2Host\=* OR *internal\/implant\/config.BuildLlamaEnabled\=*)) OR (process.command_line:*llama_selfextract,prebuilt* AND process.command_line:*internal\/implant\/main.go*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Pentest Agent Suite (H-mmer/pentest-agents at 41d49b64) writes: the per-workspace brain under
.claude/agent-memory-local/brain/ and its chain-pending.md, the cross-engagement brain ~/.claude/agent-memory/pentest-global/,
the installer manifest (.pentest-agents/manifest.json or ~/.config/pentest-agents/manifest.json) and its .pa-backup
copies, the writeup index folder ~/.local/share/pentest-writeups/, the statusline caches /tmp/.pa-statusline-* and
/tmp/.pa-session-*, the camofox_ctl.sh pid and log files /tmp/camofox.pid and /tmp/camofox.log, and the /autopilot
surface evidence under ~/bounties/<platform>-<program>/evidence/<host>/surface/.
false_positives: Bug bounty researchers using Pentest Agent Suite with permission
Another tool that uses a ~/bounties/ folder with evidence/<host>/surface/ output
name: Pentest Agent Suite Workspace, Memory or Stealth Browser Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.claude\/agent\-memory\-local\/brain\/* OR *\/.claude\/agent\-memory\/pentest\-global\/* OR *\/.local\/share\/pentest\-writeups\/* OR *\/tmp\/.pa\-statusline\-* OR *\/tmp\/.pa\-session\-*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.claude\/agent\-memory\-local\/chain\-pending.md OR *\/.pentest\-agents\/manifest.json OR *\/.config\/pentest\-agents\/manifest.json OR *.pa\-backup OR *\/tmp\/camofox.pid OR *\/tmp\/camofox.log)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/bounties\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/evidence\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/surface\/*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Pensar Apex writes: a session folder under ~/.pensar/sessions/<id>/ (session.json, README.md,
findings/, scratchpad/, logs/, pocs/), the run store ~/.pensar/runtime/runs.sqlite, the staged callback listener
callback-listeners/listener-<32 hex>.cjs, and a prompt injection payload /tmp/apex_payload_<uuid>.txt
(src/core/session/index.ts:393-437, src/core/runtime/runStorePath.ts:4-12, callbackListener.ts:693-697,
executeCommand.ts:251-257). PENSAR_DATA_DIR moves the data folder.
false_positives: Developers and security teams that use Pensar Apex
name: Pensar Apex Session, Run Store or Callback Listener Files
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.pensar\/sessions\/* OR *\\.pensar\\sessions\\* OR *\/.pensar\/runtime\/runs.sqlite* OR *\\.pensar\\runtime\\runs.sqlite*)) OR (TargetFilename:*callback\-listeners* AND TargetFilename:*.cjs) OR TargetFilename:*\/tmp\/apex_payload_*

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects an MCP client driving a remote HexStrike server: requests to /api/tools/<tool> or /api/command on port 8888.
false_positives: Authorized tests with HexStrike
name: HexStrike Tool API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:(*\:8888\/api\/tools\/* OR *\:8888\/api\/command*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: tasklist run against many remote machines from one host in ten minutes, how ARTEX agents look for hosts with no endpoint sensor.
false_positives: Automation and infrastructure-as-code pipelines. Baseline before alerting
name: Remote tasklist Fan-Out From One Host
query:
from logs-*, filebeat-*, winlogbeat-*, packetbeat-* metadata _id, _index, _version | where (ends_with(process.executable.caseless, "\\tasklist.exe") or process.pe.original_file_name=="tasklist.exe") and (process.command_line like "* -s *" or process.command_line like "* /s *" or process.command_line like "* –s *" or process.command_line like "* —s *" or process.command_line like "* ―s *")
| eval timebucket=date_trunc(10minutes, @timestamp) | stats event_count=count() by timebucket, host.name
| where event_count >= 10

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects files created with the names and folders ARTEX agents use for their own test artifacts.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Probe Artifact Created
query: TargetFilename:(*artex\-probe\-* OR *\\ProgramData\\artx5v\\* OR *zzartx0000.php*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files numasec writes: the operation folder <workspace>/.numasec/operation/<slug>/ with its ledger, facts,
evidence and deliverables, its database numasec.db in the numasec data folder, and its out-of-band session store
interact-sessions.json.
false_positives: Security teams and testers who use numasec
name: numasec Operation, Database or Out-of-Band Session Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.numasec\/operation\/* OR *\\.numasec\\operation\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/numasec\/numasec.db OR *\\numasec\\numasec.db OR *\/numasec\/interact\-sessions.json OR *\\numasec\\interact\-sessions.json))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects pentest-ai traffic leaving through a proxy: the user agents its own HTTP code sends to targets and to
crt.sh and the Wayback Machine (pentest-ai/<version>, ptai-api-discovery/<version>, pentest-ai/authscan), its
opt-in telemetry (pentest-ai-telemetry/1.0 to telemetry.pentestai.xyz) and its cloud sync to app.pentestai.xyz.
false_positives: Security teams and bug bounty researchers running pentest-ai
name: pentest-ai User Agents or Services in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(pentest\-ai\/* OR ptai\-api\-discovery\/* OR pentest\-ai\-telemetry\/*)) OR (url.domain:/[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][eE][sS][tT][aA][iI]\.[xX][yY][zZ]/ OR url.domain:/[aA][pP][pP]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][eE][sS][tT][aA][iI]\.[xX][yY][zZ]/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Custom AI Agent Burp extension on a host: its release JARs (Custom-AI-Agent-full-<version>.jar,
Custom-AI-Agent-bapp-<version>.jar, custom-ai-agent-bapp.jar) and the files it writes under ~/.burp-ai-agent/
(audit.jsonl, logs/ai-request-log.jsonl, cache/, AGENTS/, certs/mcp-keystore.p12, backends/).
false_positives: Penetration testers and security teams who use the extension
name: Custom AI Agent (burp-ai-agent) Extension Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.burp\-ai\-agent\/* OR *\\.burp\-ai\-agent\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*Custom\-AI\-Agent\-full\-* OR *Custom\-AI\-Agent\-bapp\-* OR *custom\-ai\-agent\-bapp.jar*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects Entra ID sign-ins whose user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in Entra ID Sign-In Logs
query: user_agent.original:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files sapper-v2 writes: its engagement graph store (.sapper/ with project.json, facts/, intents/,
hints/, arena.json and ai-channel.txt), the sapper-graph.html board snapshot, and in its contest image the run folder
under /work/runs (commander-state.md, pane-env/*.env, rotated.env) and the commander scripts under /opt/sapper/.
false_positives: Contest teams and testers running sapper-v2 or a fork of it
The Svelte Sapper framework uses __sapper__ and @sapper, not .sapper/, and should not match
name: sapper-v2 Engagement Graph or Run Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.sapper\/facts\/* OR *\/.sapper\/intents\/* OR *\/.sapper\/hints\/* OR *\/opt\/sapper\/docker\/commander\/* OR *\/work\/runs\/pane\-env\/*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.sapper\/project.json OR *\/.sapper\/arena.json OR *\/.sapper\/ai\-channel.txt OR *\/.sapper\/ai\-peers.json OR *\/sapper\-graph.html OR *\/work\/runs\/commander\-state.md OR *\/work\/runs\/rotated.env OR *\/.claude\/skills\/sapper\-setup))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Pentest Copilot (BugBase) writes: its work folder check .pentest-copilot-write-test, the Kali-mode
workspaces and VPN profiles under /kali-data, the temporary folders in which it calls the codex or claude CLI
(pentest-codex-*, pentest-claude-*), its model registry in /srv/data and the Burp CA it exports to burp-ca/burp-ca.der.
false_positives: Authorized tests, bug bounty work or CTF play with Pentest Copilot
name: Pentest Copilot Work Folders, Model Transport or Burp CA Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/.pentest\-copilot\-write\-test OR (TargetFilename:(*\/kali\-data\/workspaces\/* OR *\/kali\-data\/vpn\-profiles\/*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/pentest\-codex\-* OR *\/pentest\-claude\-*)) OR (TargetFilename:(\/srv\/data\/model\-registry.json OR \/srv\/data\/burp\-ca\/burp\-ca.der))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents hard-coded in NeuroSploit: NeuroSploit/<version> on the harness's own requests (also sent to
crt.sh for subdomain lists), NeuroSploit-WebShell/1.0 from its web shell manager, the bare NeuroSploit from its
GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Slack and Graph integrations, and neurosploit-logship/<version> from its log shipping.
false_positives: Authorized tests with NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit User Agents in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(NeuroSploit\/* OR neurosploit\-logship\/*)) OR user_agent.original:*NeuroSploit\-WebShell\/* OR user_agent.original:NeuroSploit

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects CTF Agent (verialabs/ctf-agent) starting on a host: its console script ctf-solve with one of its own options
(backend/cli.py:31-43), the codex app-server process it starts for each Codex solver and the Codex coordinator, with
ctf-solve in the parent command line (backend/agents/codex_solver.py:186-191), and the Claude Code CLI started by the
Claude Agent SDK with the agent's system prompt (backend/agents/claude_solver.py:97-104,
backend/agents/claude_coordinator.py:34-35). The prompt selection assumes the SDK passes the system prompt on the
command line of the claude process, which depends on the claude-agent-sdk version.
false_positives: Authorized CTF play or research runs of CTF Agent
name: CTF Agent Launcher or Its Model CLIs
query: (process.command_line:*ctf\-solve* AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-ctfd\-url* OR *\-\-ctfd\-token* OR *\-\-challenges\-dir* OR *\-\-coordinator* OR *\-\-max\-challenges* OR *\-\-msg\-port* OR *\-\-no\-submit*))) OR (process.command_line:*codex\ app\-server* AND process.parent.command_line:*ctf\-solve*) OR (process.command_line:(*IMPORTANT\:\ You\ are\ running\ inside\ a\ Docker\ sandbox.\ All\ files\ are\ under\ \/challenge\/* OR *You\ are\ a\ CTF\ competition\ coordinator\ running\ for\ the\ ENTIRE\ duration\ of\ a\ live\ competition*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the command Hexstrike-redteam's server runs when an AI assistant asks it for an evasive payload:
python3 <dir>/BOAZ_beta/Boaz.py -f <dir>/BOAZ_beta/<input> -o <dir>/BOAZ_beta/<output>, started by hexstrike_server.py
with BOAZ_beta as the working folder. Through the MCP client the command also carries -l <loader> -c <compiler>
-t <shellcode type> (defaults -l 16 -c mingw -t donut). A Boaz.py run outside HexStrike matches too, which is
still a Windows payload being wrapped for evasion on a Linux host.
false_positives: Red teams building payloads with BOAZ for an agreed engagement
name: Hexstrike-redteam BOAZ Evasive Payload Build
query: process.command_line:*\/BOAZ_beta\/Boaz.py* OR (process.parent.command_line:*hexstrike_server.py* AND (process.command_line:*Boaz.py* AND process.command_line:*\ \-f\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-o\ *))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects pentest-ai-agents (0xSteph/pentest-ai-agents at e5d7aa02, 3.4.0) being installed: 52 Claude Code subagent
definitions copied to ~/.claude/agents/ (or .claude/agents/ in a project), slash commands in ~/.claude/commands/, and
a findings database helper set in ~/.pentest-ai/bin/ with the SQLite file ~/.pentest-ai/findings.db. Most agent file
names are generic (recon-advisor.md, vuln-scanner.md), so only the distinctive ones are listed. Not the same tool as
0xSteph/pentest-ai (folder frameworks/pentest-ai), which also uses ~/.pentest-ai/ but for other files.
false_positives: Security staff who use pentest-ai-agents
Another subagent collection that uses one of the same file names
name: pentest-ai-agents Subagents or Findings Database Installed
